why: AI agents that can pay show how fast AI is moving from giving advice to taking action.

talk.answer: I would try it for small things, because the wallet asks me to approve each purchase with a security check. Also, the store never sees my real card number, which feels safer. However, I would not give an agent full control until there are clear spending limits.

paragraphs.en: On Friday, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, a new feature that lets its AI agents pay for things. The agents are called dots, and they can help a user decide what to buy and then finish the purchase. At first, the wallet is open only to a limited number of ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States. They must be at least 18 years old and have a U.S. card from Visa, Mastercard, or American Express.

pro.en: OpenAI on Friday unveiled ChatGPT Wallet, a payments feature that allows its "dots" agents to help users choose products and then complete the checkout on their behalf. The rollout is initially limited to a select group of ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States who are at least 18 and hold an eligible U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard or American Express card.

Users register a card a single time rather than re-entering it for every transaction. Ahead of each payment, the wallet displays the items, the total and the card to be charged, and the purchase is authorized through a biometric check such as Face ID or a fingerprint, which also generates a record of the transaction.

Neither the agent nor the merchant is shown the actual card details; the card networks supply a payment token that stands in for the account number. OpenAI says cardholders retain their rewards and the customary dispute protections, and it expects users eventually to delegate purchases to agents within preset spending limits, product categories or time windows.

The company is entering a field where it is not the pioneer. The Decoder reports that rivals including Anthropic, Meta and xAI already offer shopping agents, and that OpenAI abandoned its earlier Instant Checkout effort because it proved too inflexible, while TechCrunch notes that DoorDash and Uber have so far reported modest order volumes from AI agents.

Obstacles remain, since many sites block AI agents as bots and Amazon, the largest retailer to do so, bars them outright. OpenAI has released a Commerce Partner Playbook to help merchants adapt, but with the feature confined to the U.S. for now, Korean students will have to wait; spending caps, wider retailer support and a broader rollout are the next milestones.

issues.title: Microsoft outage leaves millions without email for about a day
issues.gist: A Microsoft outage cut off Outlook, Teams and Copilot for millions of people around the world. Microsoft says it was a technical problem linked to a network upgrade, not a cyberattack.
issues.gistKo: 마이크로소프트 서비스가 멈춰 전 세계 수백만 명이 아웃룩, 팀즈, 코파일럿을 쓰지 못했어요. 회사는 사이버 공격이 아니라 네트워크 업그레이드와 관련된 기술 문제라고 밝혔어요.
issues.easyKo: 회사 메일과 화상회의에 쓰는 마이크로소프트 서비스가 거의 하루 동안 먹통이 됐어요. 해킹이 아니라 내부 네트워크 문제라고 하지만, 큰 기술 회사 몇 곳에 세상이 기대고 있다는 점이 다시 드러났어요.

paragraphs.en: A huge Microsoft outage began on Thursday, Nov. 12, and left millions of people without email and other tools. Microsoft first reported problems shortly before 1 p.m. Eastern time, and Outlook, Teams and the Copilot AI assistant were among the services that failed. The trouble lasted about 18 hours before services began to recover on Friday, though some reports described nearly a full day of disruption. Microsoft 365 has more than 430 million users, and the tracking site Downdetector showed problems in 74 countries.

pro.en: A sweeping Microsoft outage that began on Thursday, Nov. 12, left millions of users without email and collaboration tools, with the company first flagging problems shortly before 1 p.m. Eastern time. Outlook, Teams and the Copilot AI assistant were among the services knocked offline, and recovery did not begin until Friday, roughly 18 hours later, although some accounts put the disruption closer to a full day. Microsoft says more than 430 million people use Microsoft 365, and the monitoring site Downdetector logged problems in 74 countries.

Microsoft attributed the failure to a technical fault rather than a cyberattack or AI agents, saying it was introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced after a recent network change. The BBC reported that routine automated checks took some servers offline, shifting traffic onto the remaining machines, and an Australian engineering professor likened the episode to a cascading failure in which overloaded servers collapse in sequence. The company has pledged a full report once its review is complete, leaving the precise root cause open for now.

The fallout extended well beyond corporate offices. In Britain, healthcare systems, schools and police forces were disrupted, with some police urging the public to phone rather than report crimes online, while the US House of Representatives struggled with email and a Colorado sheriff's office could not process bond payments. Euronext told listed companies to call in, Aviva used Bluetooth to transfer recordings for its earnings call, some Taiwanese financial firms confirmed trades by fax, and OpenAI and Anthropic both flagged problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors.

Commentators said the episode exposed how heavily the world leans on a handful of technology providers. A small business group called it a stark reminder, noting that many smaller companies rely on email to reach customers and generate income; engineer Gergely Orosz said such outages are not unheard of but the protracted recovery was unusual, and proposed splitting services by region as Amazon does with its cloud platform. Analyst Paolo Pescatore said pressure is mounting to invest in contingency plans and test them, while Microsoft shares slipped about 1.1 percent in early Wall Street trading.

For university students and early-career workers, the episode is a reminder that coursework, applications and interviews frequently hinge on email and video calls, and that a second channel to reach instructors and employers is prudent. Australia's home affairs minister said Microsoft compared the disruption to the 2024 CrowdStrike failure, which likewise stemmed from a faulty update. Attention now turns to Microsoft's full incident report and to the safeguards it adopts to prevent a recurrence.

views.view: Microsoft said it is deeply sorry, called the problem technical and not related to cyber or AI, and said it addressed the underlying issue.
An RMIT professor said a network misconfiguration can cascade and that firms using cloud services should have backup options.
A small business group called the outage a stark reminder of how much firms rely on digital systems such as Outlook.
An analyst said pressure is mounting to invest in contingency plans and test whether backups actually work.
Analyst Dan Ives said there will be major questions for Microsoft after the global outage.
Microsoft is likely to face questions about why it could not recover quickly from an outage of its own making.
Microsoft says it is seeing encouraging recovery progress as service availability and email delivery improve.

issues.title: Iran Says It Hit a US Radar in Bahrain, but the US Says It Only Shot Down Two Drones
issues.gist: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. The US military said the radar was not destroyed and that it shot down two Iranian drones.

pro.en: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Friday that its aerospace force had targeted and destroyed a US early-warning radar on the island of Bahrain, framing the operation as retaliation for an American strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, on the shores of the Strait of Hormuz.

Within hours, US Central Command rejected the assertion, saying the radar had not been destroyed and that American forces had intercepted two one-way attack drones launched by the Guards toward Bahrain; it reported neither casualties nor damage.

The exchange comes amid a fragile de-escalation in a war that began on Feb. 28 with US and Israeli surprise attacks on Iran. Tehran has since throttled shipping through Hormuz, while Washington has maintained a blockade of Iranian ports, and Washington appeared to temper its threats of renewed strikes after Republican losses in the midterm elections, according to CNA.

The Guards cast the attack as a stern warning against what they termed aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the strait; CENTCOM had said last month that it helped Gulf states export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer, and Tehran struck US facilities in Bahrain earlier in the conflict, reportedly leaving a logistics hub heavily damaged.

Energy markets and import-dependent economies such as South Korea remain exposed to any disruption in the waterway, and DW noted that President Trump is expected to meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin at next week's APEC summit in China, where ending the Iran war could feature on the agenda.

views.view: The US says it stopped two drones, while Iran says it hit a radar, and the war is in a slow de-escalation with big issues unresolved.
Iran claimed to destroy the radar, the US denied it, and Washington seems to have softened its threats after the midterm elections.

why: The Strait of Hormuz carries much of the world's oil and gas, so fights near it can move energy prices.
Each side tells a different story about the same night.
lines.agree: Both sides say Iran launched an attack toward Bahrain and that the Strait of Hormuz is the center of the tension.
lines.split: Iran says the radar was destroyed, but the US says it was not and that only two drones were shot down.
lines.life: A new fight near Hormuz can raise oil prices, and that can make fuel and some goods more costly in Korea.
lines.next: Watch whether more strikes follow and what Trump, Xi and Putin say about the war at the APEC summit next week.

paragraphs.en: Netflix and AEG Presents have announced the dates for the KPop Demon Hunters Golden World Tour. The first show will take place on June 5, 2027, at CFG Bank Arena in Baltimore. The first list covers 61 shows in 35 cities across North America, the U.K. and Europe. It ends with three shows at The O2 in London on October 22 and 23. The full tour is expected to visit nearly 50 cities with more than 150 performances in 2027 and 2028.

paragraphs.en: This is not a normal concert by the singers behind the film. The animated HUNTR/X members, Rumi, Mira and Zoey, will interact with the crowd through new performance technology. Live performers, stunts and dance will join them on stage, and the Saja Boys and Derpy Tiger will appear too. Fans will be asked to sing and dance to help seal the Honmoon, just like in the story of the film. No announcement has been made about whether EJAE, Audrey Nuna and REI AMI, the singing voices of HUNTR/X, will perform.

paragraphs.en: North American ticket sales begin with a Mastercard presale on Wednesday, November 18, at 10 a.m. local time. A fan presale follows on Thursday, November 19, and general sales start on Friday, November 20. Many dates include a second matinee show, which suggests the tour is meant for young fans and families as well as adults. Writers have mixed feelings, but many stress how big the film has become. One writer says the song Golden has passed 2 billion streams on Spotify, while another is sad that New York City itself has no date.

pro.en: Netflix and AEG Presents unveiled the routing for the KPop Demon Hunters Golden World Tour, which is scheduled to open June 5, 2027, at CFG Bank Arena in Baltimore. The initial slate comprises 61 shows in 35 cities across North America, the U.K. and Europe, culminating in three performances at The O2 in London on October 22 and 23. The complete tour is expected to reach nearly 50 cities and exceed 150 performances over 2027 and 2028.

The production is not a conventional concert by the vocalists behind the film. Animated versions of HUNTR/X members Rumi, Mira and Zoey are set to interact with audiences through new performance technology, joined onstage by live performers, stunts and choreography, with the Saja Boys and Derpy Tiger also appearing. Fans will be invited to sing and dance to help seal the Honmoon, as in the film's narrative, while no announcement has addressed whether EJAE, Audrey Nuna and REI AMI, the singing voices of HUNTR/X, will take part.

Ticketing begins in North America with a Mastercard presale at 10 a.m. local time on Wednesday, November 18, followed by a fan presale on Thursday, November 19, and general sales on Friday, November 20. Many dates feature a second matinee performance, which suggests organizers are courting younger fans and families alongside adults. Commentary is mixed, though many writers underline the film's scale: one notes that Golden has surpassed 2 billion Spotify streams, while another laments that New York City proper has no date.

The film became Netflix's most popular movie after its June 2025 debut, and a K-pop story built for a global streamer is now becoming a touring business that fills arenas. Dates in Asia-Pacific and Latin America are expected to be announced for 2028. For Korean students, the project illustrates how Korean cultural content can find paying audiences worldwide, and fans will next watch the November 20 on-sale and the forthcoming Asia dates.

talk.qKo: 케이팝을 다룬 영화가 왜 공연 투어가 되고 있다고 생각하나요?
talk.answer: The film became the most popular movie on Netflix, so many fans want to see the characters in person. The tour will mix animated characters with live performers and stunts. I think companies want to turn a hit story into many kinds of experiences.

issues.title: US moves to seize $1.2 billion stolen from Binance and stops a North Korean fake-call scam
issues.gist: A US court has allowed the Justice Department to seize or freeze more than $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance. The FBI also stopped a North Korean scam that used fake video calls to steal $400 million.
issues.gistKo: 미국 법원이 바이낸스에서 도난당한 12억 달러가 넘는 암호화폐를 압류·동결하도록 허락했어요. FBI는 가짜 화상 통화로 4억 달러를 훔친 북한 사기도 막았어요.
issues.easyKo: 북한 해커가 바이낸스에서 훔친 암호화폐 일부를 미국이 붙잡을 수 있게 됐어요. 해커들은 아는 사람의 녹화 영상으로 가짜 화상 통화를 열어 악성 코드를 깔게 했어요.

views.view: The Justice Department says the hackers keep laundering the money while US authorities try to trace and recover it.
The FBI calls FaceStealer a highly effective trick that can fool even experienced, security-minded computer users.
Binance says it has covered all lost assets, and North Korea rejects the FBI findings as a political provocation.

heads.title: U.S. obtains court approval to seize, restrain over US$1.2 bln stolen in N.K. Binance theft
North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
Binance says all asset losses from N. Korea-linked cyberattack covered

why: Crypto theft is a main source of money for North Korea's weapons program, say US officials.
The same hackers keep finding new tricks, so seizures only solve part of the problem.
lines.agree: Officials, Binance and the media agree that a huge amount of crypto was stolen and that tracing it is hard.
lines.split: North Korea denies the FBI findings and calls them a political provocation.
lines.life: Fake job interviews and fake video calls can reach any student who looks for work or joins online meetings.
lines.next: Watch how much of the frozen crypto is really returned and whether the hackers find new ways to move the rest.

paragraphs.en: The US Justice Department said a court has allowed it to seize or freeze more than $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance. The theft happened on Oct. 29, when hackers took more than $6 billion in digital assets from the exchange. That amount is part of more than $2.7 billion that US authorities and private partners have frozen so far.
paragraphs.ko: 미국 법무부는 법원이 바이낸스에서 도난당한 12억 달러가 넘는 암호화폐를 압류하거나 동결하도록 허락했다고 밝혔어요. 도난은 10월 29일에 일어났고, 해커들이 거래소에서 60억 달러가 넘는 디지털 자산을 가져갔어요. 이 금액은 미국 당국과 민간 협력자들이 지금까지 동결한 27억 달러가 넘는 돈의 일부예요.

paragraphs.en: The FBI says a North Korean hacking group called TraderTraitor was behind the theft. The hackers are still moving the stolen coins through bridges, mixers and exchanges to hide where the money went. Last week the FBI, the Secret Service and the Internal Revenue Service told crypto companies to block payments linked to the addresses used in this laundering. Kim Yo-jong, the sister of North Korea's leader, rejected the findings and called them a grave political provocation.
paragraphs.ko: FBI는 트레이더트레이터라는 북한 해킹 집단이 도난의 배후라고 말해요. 해커들은 돈이 어디로 갔는지 숨기려고 훔친 코인을 브리지, 믹서, 거래소로 계속 옮기고 있어요. 지난주 FBI, 비밀경호국, 국세청은 이 돈세탁에 쓰인 주소와 이어진 거래를 막으라고 암호화폐 회사들에 알렸어요. 북한 지도자의 여동생 김여정은 조사 결과를 거부하며 심각한 정치적 도발이라고 불렀어요.

paragraphs.en: Binance said it has finished paying back the assets that users lost. It put in more than $6.34 billion of its own money, taken from a user-protection fund called SAFU, an insurance fund for futures trading and the company treasury. It also bought the affected coins on the market and in private deals. Binance plans to refill SAFU to about $1 billion so that it can serve as an emergency reserve again.
paragraphs.ko: 바이낸스는 이용자들이 잃은 자산을 모두 메웠다고 밝혔어요. 회사는 SAFU라는 이용자 보호 기금, 선물 거래 보험 기금, 회사 금고에서 63억 4천만 달러가 넘는 자기 돈을 넣었어요. 또 피해를 입은 코인을 시장과 장외 거래로 사들였어요. 바이낸스는 SAFU를 다시 약 10억 달러로 채워 비상 준비금으로 쓸 수 있게 할 계획이에요.

paragraphs.en: On the same day, the Justice Department announced that it had disrupted a separate North Korean campaign called FaceStealer. The FBI says the campaign used fake video calls to steal more than $400 million in crypto over 18 months, and more than 900 people were victims. Hackers used fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite targets to calls on imitation versions of Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet. They played recorded videos of people the target knew, then showed a message asking the target to click a link to fix the sound. That link installed malware, and the hackers secretly recorded the calls to use on new victims.
paragraphs.ko: 같은 날 법무부는 페이스스틸러라는 별도의 북한 공작을 막았다고 발표했어요. FBI는 이 공작이 18개월 동안 가짜 화상 통화로 4억 달러가 넘는 암호화폐를 훔쳤고 피해자가 900명이 넘는다고 말해요. 해커들은 가짜이거나 탈취한 소셜 미디어 계정으로 줌, 마이크로소프트 팀즈, 구글 밋의 모조품에서 열리는 통화에 목표를 초대했어요. 목표가 아는 사람들의 녹화 영상을 틀어 놓고, 소리를 고치려면 링크를 누르라는 메시지를 띄웠어요. 그 링크는 악성 코드를 깔았고, 해커들은 통화를 몰래 녹화해 새 피해자에게 썼어요.

paragraphs.en: Officials say the targets are mostly people in crypto and web3 work, especially those who build and maintain open-source software. A senior US official said North Korea pays for its weapons program with crypto theft, and the FBI warned that even careful, tech-savvy users can be fooled. The FBI seized cloud systems used in the campaign and the 900 webcam videos. Officials say they are still working to trace and recover the stolen funds. For students who look for jobs or join video calls, the lesson is to check who is really on the other side before you click anything.
paragraphs.ko: 당국은 목표가 주로 암호화폐와 웹3 분야 사람, 특히 오픈소스 소프트웨어를 만들고 관리하는 사람이라고 말해요. 미국 고위 관리는 북한이 암호화폐 절도로 무기 계획 자금을 댄다고 말했고, FBI는 조심스럽고 기술에 밝은 이용자도 속을 수 있다고 경고했어요. FBI는 이 공작에 쓰인 클라우드 시스템과 웹캠 영상 900여 개를 압수했어요. 당국은 도난당한 돈을 추적해 되찾는 일을 계속하고 있다고 말해요. 일자리를 찾거나 화상 통화에 들어가는 학생에게 주는 교훈은, 무엇이든 누르기 전에 상대가 정말 누구인지 확인하라는 거예요.

pro.en: In a release dated Thursday, the U.S. Justice Department said a court had authorized it to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in cryptocurrency taken from Binance, a portion of the more than $6 billion drained from the exchange in an Oct. 29 breach. That sum is part of over $2.7 billion in assets that American authorities and private-sector partners have frozen to date.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation has attributed the theft to a North Korean group known as TraderTraitor, which continues to launder the proceeds through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges. Last week, the FBI, the Secret Service and the Internal Revenue Service issued a joint alert urging virtual asset service providers to block transactions tied to the addresses used in the laundering, while Kim Yo-jong, the sister of North Korea's leader, dismissed the findings as a grave political provocation.

Binance said it had made whole the assets affected, deploying more than $6.34 billion of its own resources from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, a futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and repurchasing the impacted tokens on the open market and in over-the-counter deals. The company pledged to top SAFU back up to roughly $1 billion so that it again serves as an emergency reserve for users.

Separately, the department announced it had disrupted a North Korean campaign dubbed FaceStealer, which the FBI says siphoned more than $400 million in cryptocurrency from over 900 victims across 18 months. Operatives used counterfeit or hijacked social media accounts to lure targets onto imitation Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet sessions, played pre-recorded footage of acquaintances, then prompted victims to click a purported audio fix that installed malware and let the group harvest further recordings.

Authorities said the scheme aggressively targets cryptocurrency and web3 workers, notably open-source software developers and maintainers. A senior Justice Department official said Pyongyang bankrolls its weapons program through crypto theft, the FBI called the ruse capable of deceiving even seasoned security-conscious users, and investigators seized cloud infrastructure and more than 900 webcam videos as they work to trace and recover the funds.

issues.title: Bessent Blames Commerce Department Over Megaspeed Chip Blacklist Delay
issues.gist: The U.S. Treasury secretary says his department wanted Megaspeed on a trade blacklist for months, but the Commerce Department did not act. The dispute adds pressure on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Nvidia.
issues.gistKo: 미국 재무장관은 재무부가 몇 달 동안 메가스피드를 수출 블랙리스트에 올리자고 했지만 상무부가 움직이지 않았다고 말했어요. 이 다툼으로 하워드 러트닉 상무장관과 엔비디아에 대한 압박이 커졌어요.
issues.easyKo: 엔비디아 반도체 구매 회사 메가스피드를 둘러싼 스캔들에서 정부 안의 책임 공방이 시작됐어요. 스콧 베선트 재무장관은 블랙리스트에 올리는 일은 상무부가 쥐고 있다고 말했어요. 러트닉 장관은 12월 10일 상원 위원회에 나가 증언하기로 했어요.

paragraphs.en: On Friday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the Commerce Department for not putting Megaspeed on a trade blacklist. The blacklist is called the Entity List, and Commerce is in charge of it. Bessent told CNBC that Treasury, the War Department, the U.S. Trade Representative and the State Department had favored adding Megaspeed for months. But he said Commerce "has the pen," so questions about its process should go to Commerce.

paragraphs.en: Megaspeed is a company based in Singapore that rents out computing power built on Nvidia chips. The Guardian reports that over the past three years it bought nearly $5 billion in AI chips and hardware. The United States restricts the export of Nvidia's most powerful chips to China, and officials worry that chips are being passed on. Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed director, is accused of being a Chinese spy, but Beijing calls this a smear, and Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing. Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned this week.

pro.en: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday faulted the Commerce Department for failing to place the Singapore-based data center firm Megaspeed on the Entity List, the trade blacklist administered by Commerce. Speaking on CNBC, Bessent said the Treasury, War and State Departments and the U.S. trade representative had favored listing the company for months, but that Commerce "has the pen" and that questions about its internal processes should be directed there.

Megaspeed, a cloud and AI computing provider built on Nvidia hardware, has bought nearly $5 billion in AI chips and equipment over the past three years, the Guardian reported. Washington restricts exports of Nvidia's most advanced chips to China and fears the processors are being diverted. Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed director, stands accused of acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, an allegation Beijing dismisses as a smear and Megaspeed denies wrongdoing; Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, stepped down this week.

Bessent declined to confirm a report that he had confronted Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, saying, "We don't repeat conversations in the Situation Room." He argued that the central question is whether Nvidia knew its customer and made a robust effort to prevent leakage. Reuters reported that White House officials are weighing whether to oust Lutnick, though a White House official said President Donald Trump retains complete confidence in him.

Scrutiny on Capitol Hill is intensifying. Senator Tim Scott, who chairs the Senate Banking Committee, has asked both Lutnick and Jensen Huang to testify, and Lutnick is due to appear on Dec. 10. Senator Jim Banks asserted that Commerce appears to have exploited loopholes that allowed some chip sales to proceed, while a source told CBS News that Washington offered Singapore scant help with its probe, which Singapore says it sought from the Justice Department and the FBI.

Attorney General Todd Blanche said no conclusion has yet been reached about who Alice Huang is, and Trump said he does not know whether she was a spy. For Korean students, the episode illustrates how export-control decisions can ripple through AI chip firms and the products built on their hardware. The next markers are whether Megaspeed is added to the Entity List and what Lutnick tells senators on Dec. 10.

views.view: Bessent says Treasury, War, USTR and State favored blacklisting Megaspeed for months, but Commerce has the pen.
A source says Washington gave Singapore little meaningful help with its investigation into Megaspeed and Alice Huang.
A security expert says it would be credible to call Megaspeed a front for Chinese intelligence, but key details are still unclear.
Megaspeed says it is compliant and legitimate, and Nvidia said in 2025 that its own inquiry found no evidence of chip diversion.
Senator Jim Banks says Commerce appears to have used loopholes to let some chip sales happen despite Trump's orders.

issues.title: Pegula Saves a Match Point and Knocks Gauff Out of WTA Finals
issues.gist: Jessica Pegula saved a match point to beat Linda Noskova in three sets at the WTA Finals. The win put her in the semifinals and sent Coco Gauff home.
issues.gistKo: 제시카 페굴라가 WTA 파이널스에서 매치 포인트를 막고 린다 노스코바를 세트 세 개 끝에 이겼어요. 덕분에 준결승에 올랐고 코코 고프는 탈락했어요.
issues.easyKo: 테니스 시즌 마지막 큰 대회에서 페굴라가 위기를 넘기고 준결승에 갔어요. 같은 조의 고프는 이겼지만 페굴라가 이기는 바람에 탈락했어요.

paragraphs.en: American tennis player Jessica Pegula reached the semifinals of the WTA Finals on Thursday. She beat Linda Noskova 7-6 (7-2), 4-6, 7-5 at Indian Wells in California. Noskova had a match point at 5-4 in the last set, but Pegula saved it. The win sent Coco Gauff out of the event.
paragraphs.ko: 미국 테니스 선수 제시카 페굴라가 목요일 WTA 파이널스 준결승에 올랐어요. 캘리포니아 인디언웰스에서 린다 노스코바를 7-6(7-2), 4-6, 7-5로 이겼어요. 노스코바는 마지막 세트 5-4에서 매치 포인트를 잡았지만 페굴라가 그것을 막아냈어요. 이 승리로 코코 고프는 대회에서 탈락했어요.

sents.en: American tennis player Jessica Pegula reached the semifinals of the WTA Finals on Thursday.

paragraphs.en: Pegula had to win this match to move on, because Gauff had already beaten Marta Kostyuk earlier that day. She hit 16 aces, the most she has ever served in a WTA Tour match. Noskova had trouble on her own serve and made 15 double faults, with nine aces. Pegula said that sometimes the serve feels good and sometimes it does not, and she has learned to handle both kinds of days.

pro.en: Jessica Pegula, the American world No. 5, saved a match point to edge Linda Noskova 7-6 (7-2), 4-6, 7-5 at Indian Wells on Thursday and secure a semifinal berth at the WTA Finals. Noskova had held a match point at 5-4 in the deciding set, and the result eliminated Coco Gauff.

With Gauff having already beaten Marta Kostyuk earlier in the day, Pegula needed a victory to advance from the group. She struck a career-best 16 aces, the most she has produced in a WTA Tour match, while Noskova labored on serve, committing 15 double faults against nine aces. Pegula said the serve can feel good one day and not the next, and that she has learned to manage both.

Gauff, ranked fourth in the world, beat Ukraine's Kostyuk 6-4, 7-5 despite requiring treatment for a lower-back problem and trailing 5-1 in the second set. She then reeled off six straight games to close out the match. Gauff conceded she was physically below her best and described playing through the pain as a mental challenge; it was the second time at the event that she had overturned a 5-1 deficit.

Ahead of the tournament, the WTA chair apologised to Pegula after private remarks she made to her coach about Andreeva during a practice session were live-streamed. The BBC described Pegula as gritty and said she displayed great mental resilience in a fluctuating contest. "It's the match people wanted, well now you are going to get it," Pegula told reporters.

Pegula will meet French Open champion Mirra Andreeva for the first time in the last four. Noskova, who had already clinched a semifinal place, will play either Elina Svitolina or Aryna Sabalenka on Saturday, while Gauff, the 2024 champion, exits the event.

views.view: Pegula saved a match point to win in three sets, and Gauff was knocked out despite her own win.
Pegula was gritty and showed great mental resilience in a match that kept changing.

pro.en: Samsung Electronics is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing, a U.S. maker of data center cooling systems, Bloomberg News reported Nov. 13, citing multiple people familiar with the matter. A deal could be reached within weeks, the report said, though no final decision has been made and the negotiations could collapse or rival suitors could emerge.

Based in Wisconsin, Modine produces heating, ventilation, air conditioning and thermal management equipment for large commercial facilities and industrial machinery. Its cooling operations serving hyperscalers building vast data centers have expanded rapidly, and last month the company restructured by spinning off its automotive division to concentrate on thermal management.

The move would extend Samsung's push into the global HVAC market. Last year it spent roughly 1.5 billion euros to acquire Germany's FlaktGroup, and folding Modine's data center cooling technology and business base into that unit is expected to bolster its competitiveness in AI infrastructure.

Masahiro Wakasugi, an analyst at Bloomberg Intelligence, said a Modine purchase would help Samsung diversify away from its heavy reliance on memory chips. The company, he said, must secure new growth engines such as data center-related businesses by deploying the cash its semiconductor operations generate.

For Korean readers, the episode illustrates how the AI investment boom is spilling beyond chips and software into the physical systems that keep data centers running. Whether the talks produce a signed agreement in the coming weeks is the key question.

issues.gist: Pope Leo XIV held an open-air Mass near Chiclayo, Peru, where he once served as bishop. The Vatican said about 1.5 million people came.
issues.gistKo: 교황 레오 14세가 예전에 주교로 일했던 페루 치클라요 근처에서 야외 미사를 열었어요. 바티칸은 약 150만 명이 모였다고 밝혔어요.

paragraphs.en: Pope Leo XIV celebrated an open-air Mass on Friday near Chiclayo, a city in northern Peru where he once served as bishop. The Vatican estimated that about 1.5 million people came to the park at Pampas de Pimentel. Temperatures went past 30 degrees Celsius, and some people arrived 12 hours early to pray through the night. The Mass was the main event of the pope's 12-day trip to South America, which also includes Uruguay and Argentina.

pro.en: Pope Leo XIV presided on Friday over an open-air Mass at Pampas de Pimentel, a desert park outside the northern Peruvian city of Chiclayo, in the diocese he once led as bishop. The Vatican estimated that about 1.5 million faithful gathered there, some having kept an overnight vigil of 12 hours before the ceremony as temperatures climbed past 30 degrees Celsius. The Mass formed the centerpiece of a 12-day South American tour that also takes in Uruguay and Argentina.

Born Robert Prevost in Chicago, the pontiff spent long stretches in Peru between 1985 and 2023, took Peruvian citizenship in 2015 and served as bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023. Residents still address him as "Padre Roberto" and trade anecdotes about him, recalling his role in launching soup kitchens during the Covid-19 pandemic and a ride on horseback through floodwaters.

Opening his homily, the pope thanked the congregation for its affection, support and prayers, singling out those offered for his health after lung cancer surgery weeks earlier, a period of trial he said he was overcoming with God's help. Lisbeth Diaz, a teacher who worked with him, said he helped Venezuelan migrants secure legal residency and work permits, while a local priest credited him with bringing Peruvians closer to the Church.

The visit has also reshaped daily life in the area. The BBC reported that the usual population of 800,000 in the city and its surroundings may have doubled, with local businesses capitalizing on the surge in sales and hotels sharply raising nightly rates. DW noted that crowds have swelled over the course of the trip, peaking at an estimated 3.5 million people in Lima on Wednesday.

Reporters remarked on the emotion shown by a pope who is normally reserved, laughing, singing and weeping among the faithful. He was scheduled to address a Catholic university in Chiclayo where he once served as chancellor on Friday afternoon, and is due to remain in the city until Sunday.

views.view: The BBC described an emotional homecoming in Chiclayo, where locals said the pope helped the poor and migrants.
DW stressed the huge crowds on the trip and the open emotion the usually reserved pope has shown.

issues.title: Google and Samsung Open Preorders for Gemini Glasses as Korea Worries About Exam Cheating
issues.gist: Google, Samsung, Gentle Monster and Warby Parker opened preorders for Gemini smart glasses that start at $395 and ship on December 10. In South Korea, the news raised fears of cheating on exams.
issues.gistKo: 구글, 삼성, 젠틀몬스터, 워비 파커가 395달러부터 시작하는 제미나이 스마트 안경의 예약 판매를 열었고 12월 10일에 배송해요. 한국에서는 이 소식이 시험 부정행위 걱정으로 이어졌어요.
issues.easyKo: 화면은 없고 말과 카메라로 쓰는 AI 안경이 곧 나와요. 사생활 보호 장치도 있지만, 한국에서는 수능 같은 시험에서 몰래 쓰일까 봐 정부가 단속을 약속했어요.

views.view: The glasses add privacy limits, but the reviewer warns that Gemini can be wrong and that data on Google's servers is not encrypted.

sents.ko: 젠틀몬스터는 449달러부터 시작하는 여섯 가지 스타일을 내놓고, 미국과 한국에서 팔 예정이에요.

sents.en: The glasses are set to ship and reach stores on December 10.
sents.ko: 안경은 12월 10일에 배송되고 매장에도 나올 예정이에요.

paragraphs.en: These glasses have no screen in the lenses, so people use them by voice or by turning on the built-in camera. Samsung makes the computer parts inside the frames, and Google provides the software. A user can say "Hey Gemini" or tap a part of the frame to start talking to the AI. The camera is a 12 MP wide-angle one, and each frame weighs about 41 grams before lenses are added. The AI can look at what the wearer sees and, for example, add a poster's event to a calendar.
paragraphs.ko: 이 안경은 렌즈에 화면이 없어서 목소리로 쓰거나 내장 카메라를 켜서 써요. 삼성이 안경테 안의 컴퓨터 부품을 만들고, 구글이 소프트웨어를 맡아요. 사용자는 "헤이 제미나이"라고 말하거나 안경테의 한 부분을 눌러 AI와 대화를 시작할 수 있어요. 카메라는 12MP 광각이고, 안경테 하나는 렌즈를 끼우기 전 무게가 약 41그램이에요. AI는 쓰는 사람이 보는 것을 보고, 예를 들어 포스터에 적힌 행사를 일정에 넣어 줄 수 있어요.

paragraphs.en: Privacy is the biggest question, so Google says its design respects people on both sides of the lens. A light turns on when the camera is active, and the glasses refuse to record if someone covers it. There is also a physical off switch, and apps cannot live stream video to social media from these glasses. Google says it will not use real-time face recognition and will blur faces before sending video for processing. Images and videos from the glasses will not be saved in Gemini history or used to train AI or target ads. One reviewer notes that the data is not encrypted on Google's servers and that Gemini can still make mistakes.
paragraphs.ko: 개인정보가 가장 큰 문제라서, 구글은 렌즈 양쪽 사람을 모두 존중하도록 설계했다고 말해요. 카메라가 켜지면 불이 들어오고, 누가 그 불을 가리면 안경은 녹화를 거부해요. 물리적인 끄기 스위치도 있고, 앱이 이 안경에서 소셜 미디어로 영상을 생중계할 수도 없어요. 구글은 실시간 얼굴 인식은 쓰지 않고, 영상을 처리하려고 보내기 전에 얼굴을 가린다고 해요. 안경으로 찍은 사진과 영상은 제미나이 기록에 저장되지 않고, AI 훈련이나 광고에도 쓰이지 않아요. 한 리뷰어는 데이터가 구글 서버에서는 암호화되지 않고, 제미나이가 여전히 실수할 수 있다고 지적해요.

paragraphs.en: In South Korea, the worry is different: people fear that such glasses could be used to cheat on exams. The worry grew after this year's top scorer on the tax accountant exam got 397.5 points out of 400. The person missed only one of 160 questions in the first round, and many test takers called the score unrealistic. The agency that runs the exam said its two proctors saw nothing suspicious, but it is reviewing the case. An association of tax accountants asked for a thorough investigation but said a high score alone is not a reason for suspicion.
paragraphs.ko: 한국에서는 걱정이 달라요. 이런 안경이 시험 부정행위에 쓰일 수 있다고 사람들이 두려워해요. 올해 세무사 시험 수석이 400점 만점에 397.5점을 받으면서 걱정이 커졌어요. 그 사람은 1차 시험 160문제 중 한 문제만 틀렸고, 많은 수험생이 그 점수가 비현실적이라고 말했어요. 시험을 운영하는 기관은 감독관 두 명이 수상한 점을 보지 못했지만 이 일을 살펴보고 있다고 밝혔어요. 세무사 단체는 철저한 조사를 요구하면서도, 높은 점수만으로는 의심할 이유가 되지 않는다고 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: On Friday the Korean government promised zero tolerance for cheating with AI glasses in next week's college entrance exam. The exam is set for Thursday, and specialized staff will be sent to test sites to detect such glasses. Cheaters will face strict action, including criminal complaints, and the government will also ask for an investigation of the tax exam case. Since Gentle Monster glasses will also be sold in Korea, the next things to watch are how the exam rules and the glasses' safeguards work together.
paragraphs.ko: 금요일에 한국 정부는 다음 주 대학수학능력시험에서 AI 안경을 쓴 부정행위를 용납하지 않겠다고 약속했어요. 시험은 목요일로 잡혀 있고, 이런 안경을 찾아내려고 전문 인력을 시험장에 보낼 거예요. 부정행위자는 형사 고발을 포함해 엄하게 다뤄지고, 정부는 세무사 시험 일도 조사를 요청할 거예요. 젠틀몬스터 안경도 한국에서 팔리기 때문에, 앞으로는 시험 규칙과 안경의 안전장치가 어떻게 함께 작동하는지 지켜볼 만해요.

pro.en: Google, Samsung and the eyewear makers Gentle Monster and Warby Parker opened preorders on Friday for the first smart glasses built around Gemini, with Warby Parker's three frames, Alden, Reid and Wren, starting at $395 in the United States only, while Gentle Monster's six styles begin at $449 and will be sold in the US and South Korea, and shipments and store arrivals are scheduled for December 10.

The lenses carry no display, so wearers interact with the assistant by voice or through a 12-megapixel wide-angle camera, with Samsung supplying the computing hardware and Google the software; users can summon Gemini by saying "Hey Gemini" or tapping a touch-sensitive area of the frame, and each frame weighs about 41 grams before lenses, while the camera feed lets the assistant act on what the wearer sees, such as adding a poster's event to a calendar.

Privacy is the central test, and Google argues that its approach respects people on both sides of the lens: a recording light illuminates whenever the camera is active and the glasses decline to record if it is covered or altered, a physical off switch is included, apps are barred from live-streaming video to social media, real-time facial recognition is off the table, and faces are automatically redacted before video is sent for processing, while captured images and video are kept out of Gemini history and are not used for model training or ad targeting, although one reviewer cautions that data is not encrypted on Google's servers and that Gemini remains fallible.

In South Korea, the debate has taken a different turn, as concern that such devices could enable exam cheating intensified after this year's top scorer in the certified tax accountant exam earned 397.5 of 400 points, missing a single question out of 160 in the first round, a result many test takers considered unrealistic; the Human Resources Development Service of Korea said neither proctor reported suspicious behavior but that it is reviewing the matter, and the Korean Association of Certified Tax Accountants urged a thorough probe while warning that exceptional scores alone should not be grounds for suspicion.

On Friday, the Office for Government Policy Coordination pledged a zero-tolerance approach to cheating with AI glasses at the nationwide college entrance exam set for Thursday, saying specialized personnel will be deployed to test sites to detect the devices and that offenders will face stern measures, including criminal complaints, while it will also request an investigation into the tax exam; with Gentle Monster's glasses due to go on sale in Korea, how exam rules and the products' built-in safeguards interact is the next thing to watch.

issues.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns as Congress Asks for Answers
issues.gist: Jensen Huang has left his jobs as chief executive of Nvidia after reports about his personal affairs. US lawmakers want him and a top official to testify about chip sales to China.
issues.gistKo: 젠슨 황이 개인사 보도 끝에 엔비디아 CEO 자리에서 물러났어요. 미국 의원들은 그와 고위 당국자에게 중국 칩 판매에 대해 증언해 달라고 요구해요.
issues.easyKo: 세계에서 가장 중요한 AI 칩 회사의 CEO가 물러났어요. 이제 미국 의회는 중국에 첨단 칩이 흘러갔는지, 규정이 제대로 지켜졌는지 묻겠다고 해요. 새 CEO는 임시로 재무 책임자가 맡았어요.

paragraphs.en: Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive of Nvidia, the company that makes the most widely used chips for artificial intelligence. The company said on Thursday, Nov. 12, that he was leaving his jobs as president, CEO and board member right away. Colette Kress, the chief financial officer, will serve as interim CEO. Huang had admitted to an affair with a woman whom US officials suspect of working for China, and later reports described a second relationship with a colleague.
paragraphs.ko: 젠슨 황이 인공지능에 가장 널리 쓰이는 칩을 만드는 회사 엔비디아의 최고경영자 자리에서 물러났어요. 회사는 11월 12일 목요일에 그가 사장, CEO, 이사 자리를 즉시 내려놓는다고 밝혔어요. 재무 책임자인 콜레트 크레스가 임시 CEO를 맡아요. 황은 미국 당국이 중국을 위해 일한다고 의심하는 여성과의 불륜을 인정했고, 뒤이어 동료와의 두 번째 관계를 전하는 보도도 나왔어요.

sents.ko: 황은 미국 당국이 중국을 위해 일한다고 의심하는 여성과의 불륜을 인정했고, 뒤이어 동료와의 두 번째 관계를 전하는 보도도 나왔어요.

paragraphs.en: The woman once held a senior post at Megaspeed, a Singapore firm that is a major Nvidia customer. The US government is looking into whether Megaspeed secretly sent Nvidia chips to China, which would break American limits on advanced chips. Megaspeed denies this and says it will cooperate with investigators, while China rejects the spy claim as a pretext for a technology blockade. Nvidia lost $550 billion in market value in five days as the story dominated the news. The board had stood by Huang after the first report, but market watchers think the second one did too much damage to the firm's name.

pro.en: Jensen Huang resigned Thursday as president, chief executive and board member of Nvidia, the dominant supplier of chips that power artificial intelligence, after an admitted affair with a woman U.S. officials suspect of working for China was followed by reports of a second relationship with a colleague. The company named Colette Kress, its chief financial officer, interim CEO, effective immediately on Nov. 12.

The woman is a former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm and major Nvidia customer that Washington is investigating over suspicions it diverted restricted chips to China in violation of export curbs. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing and has pledged to cooperate, while Beijing has dismissed the spying allegation as a pretext for a technological blockade. Nvidia shed $550 billion in market value in five days, and market watchers judged that the second disclosure inflicted reputational damage the board, which had initially stood by Huang, could not absorb.

Lawmakers are now pressing for testimony. Sen. Tim Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3, warning that the panel could issue a subpoena, while three House committees requested a closed-door interview on Dec. 1. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, accused by officials of stalling tighter chip restrictions, has agreed to testify before the Senate panel on Dec. 10, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said several agencies backed placing Megaspeed on an Entity List restricting its access to U.S. technology, a step Commerce did not take.

China's foreign ministry cautioned Washington on Friday against fresh chip export controls, with a spokesperson saying Beijing opposes the abuse of such measures and urging both sides to keep trade relations stable. Industry observers nonetheless regard Nvidia as a linchpin of the AI economy, and demand for its products is expected to remain robust as AI adoption grows, leaving its next leader to manage the fallout while charting long-term strategy.

The board is working with advisers to identify a permanent chief executive. Candidates floated in the press include Kress and members of Huang's family, while a Yale business school professor also put forward former Apple chief Tim Cook. Attention now turns to the three congressional appearances in December and to whether Washington tightens rules on chip sales to China.

views.view: Lawmakers see national security worries and want both Huang and the commerce secretary to testify in December.
DW says the second affair report did too much reputational harm, and the board now needs a successor.
China warns the US against tighter chip export controls and calls the spy claim a pretext.
TechCrunch reports Huang agreed to testify behind closed doors after lawmakers threatened a subpoena.
NPR says Kress faces a hard job, but strong demand for Nvidia's AI chips is expected to continue.

pro.en: Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Alvarez and Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong were unanimously voted the American and National League Most Valuable Players on Thursday, each collecting all 30 first-place ballots cast by members of the Baseball Writers' Association of America. Both were first-time winners.

Crow-Armstrong, 24, batted .280 with 45 home runs and 41 stolen bases, tying Kyle Schwarber for the major league lead in homers, and he added a Gold Glove and a Platinum Glove for his defense. Moved to the leadoff spot in mid-May to jump-start a sputtering offense, he hit .300 there. Four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani placed second, and Crow-Armstrong became the first Cub to win since Kris Bryant in 2016.

Alvarez, 29, mounted a run at the Triple Crown, claiming the American League batting title at .316 while hitting 42 homers and driving in 106 runs, and he paced the majors with 109 walks and a .432 on-base percentage. Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero finished second and Kansas City's Bobby Witt Jr. third. After a 2025 limited to 48 games by a wrist fracture and a sprained ankle, Alvarez appeared in 158 this year and attributed the turnaround simply to being healthy.

The sweep made for a historic awards week: with Yankees pitcher Cam Schlittler and Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski both unanimous Cy Young winners on Wednesday, it was the first season in which both MVPs and both Cy Young recipients were chosen unanimously. Even so, Crow-Armstrong, who went 0-for-7 in this year's postseason, said he believes he can deliver more in bigger moments.

Part of his leap came against left-handed pitching, where he hit .280 this year after managing just .188 the season before. Whether both stars can sustain that production into next season is the question that follows them out of awards week.

views.view: Both players had historic seasons, and Alvarez led the league in many hitting numbers.
Crow-Armstrong was great at hitting, running and defense, and Alvarez used strong hitting to win.
Both winners are praised for their seasons, and Crow-Armstrong says he still wants to do better in the playoffs.

paragraphs.en: A group of nonprofit organizations has sued five big AI companies in San Francisco. The case was filed on Thursday in San Francisco Superior Court. The plaintiffs are the Alliance for Secure AI, the Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen and the Heat Initiative. They are suing Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI. They want a judge to stop these firms from building and releasing new AI models.

paragraphs.en: The groups say the companies cannot reliably control their own systems. They point to reports of AI agents that went rogue and took actions nobody had approved. pro.en: A coalition of advocacy nonprofits filed suit Thursday in San Francisco Superior Court against Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceXSI, asking a judge to block the five companies from developing and releasing new AI models. The plaintiffs are the Alliance for Secure AI, the Irreplaceable Education Fund, Public Citizen and the Heat Initiative.

The groups contend the developers cannot reliably control their own frontier systems, citing reported incidents in which AI agents went rogue and carried out unauthorized actions. The complaint also turns executives' own warnings against them: Sam Altman said in 2015 that AI would probably lead to the end of the world, and Dario Amodei suggested in 2025 there was a 25% chance that AI could lead to disastrous outcomes. The suit adds that the danger could escalate as companies hand more of the development of future models to the AI itself, without human intervention.

The complaint alleges violations of California's unfair competition law, arguing that the companies endanger public health and interfere with the use of property such as computer systems. The plaintiffs are seeking an emergency injunction on next-generation models, with operations to resume only once the firms can demonstrate that the technology is under human control. Phil Aroneanu of the Irreplaceable Education Fund told Al Jazeera that an effective freeze would require government inspections and the authority to halt prohibited work, not merely a ban on public releases.

Meta declined to comment and the other defendants did not respond to requests for comment. The filing follows an October show of support from Altman, Amodei and Elon Musk for an industrywide slowdown, and, as Al Jazeera noted, a sweeping Democratic midterm victory that analysts say could tighten the regulatory framework. The plaintiffs dismissed the argument that a pause would cost Washington ground to Beijing, saying that if both sides are slowed by roughly the same factor, neither's competitiveness suffers while the risk of losing control is reduced.

For Korean students who rely on AI tools, a successful suit could delay the next generation of chatbots, though the case is at its earliest stage. Observers will watch whether the court grants emergency relief, how the defendants answer in court, and whether lawmakers move toward binding national rules.

issues.title: Google Meets Seoul's Security Rules for Korean Map Data Export
issues.gist: South Korea says Google has met the security rules for sending detailed Korean map data abroad. Google hid map coordinates and sensitive sites, and a Korean partner will process the data.
issues.gistKo: 정부는 구글이 한국 정밀 지도 데이터를 해외로 보내기 위한 보안 조건을 지켰다고 밝혔어요. 구글은 좌표와 민감 시설을 가렸고, 국내 협력사가 데이터를 처리할 거예요.
issues.easyKo: 구글이 한국 지도를 해외 서버로 가져가려면 정부가 단 조건을 지켜야 했어요. 이번에 정부가 구글이 그 조건을 지켰다고 확인했어요. 하지만 문제가 생기면 허가가 취소될 수도 있어요.

paragraphs.en: South Korea's government said on Friday that Google has met the security rules for sending detailed Korean map data abroad. The Land Ministry said a review group of officials and private experts checked Google's work and confirmed it. In February, Seoul had given conditional approval for Google to export maps at a scale of 1 to 5,000. That decision ended a 19-year standoff over the request. Google sent its final report on the required safety steps on Nov. 4.

paragraphs.en: Google removed latitude and longitude numbers for South Korean territory from Google Maps and Google Earth, on both web and mobile. It also built a control system just for Korea that blocks an app update if banned coordinates appear. Street View images of military and security sites, and of roads within 50 meters of them, were taken down. Under a deal signed on Aug. 31, Google will get satellite pictures processed by Korea's National Geographic Information Institute through a local partner. Google must use those pictures without changing them.

paragraphs.en: Only base maps and road data, such as road names, lane counts and speed limits, can be sent abroad. A Korean partner must process the data on servers in Korea first, and the Korea Herald reported that Google picked Tmap Mobility for this job. The Tmap deal does not cover users' personal information, live locations or search histories. Google named the head of Google Korea as its map contact and set up a 24-hour system for government requests. If officials find a problem, Google must fix it within one business day.

Google has also promised a multi-year plan with Korea's map industry, which may include technology partnerships and investment.
paragraphs.ko: 한국의 학생과 여행객에게는 언젠가 구글 지도에서 도보·자동차 길 안내가 더 충실해진다는 뜻일 수 있어요. 코리아헤럴드는 구글이 일러야 2027년부터 한국 서버에서 티맵이 처리한 데이터를 쓸 것으로 내다봤어요. 당국은 좌표가 계속 가려져 있는지, 사고 대응 체계가 잘 돌아가는지 계속 살피겠다고 해요. 구글은 기술 협력과 투자를 포함할 수 있는 여러 해짜리 협력 계획도 한국 지도 업계와 추진하기로 약속했어요.

sents.en: The Korea Herald said Google is expected to start using Tmap-processed data on Korean servers as early as 2027.

pro.en: The South Korean government said Friday that Google had satisfied the security conditions attached to its permission to transfer high-precision Korean map data overseas, as an interagency review panel of officials and private-sector experts verified the company's compliance. Seoul had granted conditional approval in February for the export of 1:5,000-scale data, closing a 19-year standoff, and Google filed its final compliance report on Nov. 4.

According to the Land Ministry, Google stripped latitude and longitude coordinates for Korean territory from Google Maps and Google Earth on web and mobile platforms, and built a Korea-specific control layer that blocks app updates if restricted coordinates are detected. It also removed Street View images of military and security facilities and of roads within 50 meters of their boundaries, and under an Aug. 31 agreement will obtain satellite imagery screened by the National Geographic Information Institute through a domestic partner, loading it without modification.

Only base maps and road-network details such as road names, lane counts and speed limits are eligible for export, and a Korean partner must first process the data on domestic servers; the Korea Herald reported that Google had selected Tmap Mobility for that role, in an arrangement that excludes users' personal information, real-time locations and search histories. Google has named the president of Google Korea as its local map officer, set up a round-the-clock channel for government requests and pledged to correct any flagged breach within one business day.

Officials warned that serious violations could result in suspension or revocation of the export approval, and the panel assessed that applying Korean security standards to the global platforms could address long-standing national security concerns. KBS World reported that Google could broaden its Korean services as early as the start of next year, noting that its map app already counts ten million users in the country and that pairing navigation with search and artificial intelligence could upend a market long dominated by Naver Map and KakaoMap.

For Korean students and visitors, the change could eventually translate into fuller walking and driving directions on Google Maps, with the Korea Herald saying Tmap-processed data is expected to be in use on Korean servers as early as 2027. Authorities said they would keep monitoring whether coordinate restrictions hold and whether the incident-response system functions, while Google has also committed to a multiyear cooperation program with Korea's geospatial industry that may include technology partnerships and investment.

views.view: The government says Google built a Korea-only control system to block app updates that could expose restricted coordinates.
Meeting the rules brings Google one step closer to using Korean map data, and it could reshape competition with Naver Map and KakaoMap.
The government warns that Google's permission can be cancelled if the conditions are broken.
Google picked Tmap Mobility as its local partner, and the work stays limited to static map information.

paragraphs.en: United Airlines said it will restrict AI agents that try to book flights and manage reservations for their users. pro.en: United Airlines said it will restrict access for AI agents seeking to book flights and manage reservations on behalf of users, citing a risk to cybersecurity and to federal regulations. TechCrunch describes the carrier as the latest American corporate giant to bar customers from using autonomous assistants on its systems.

The carrier warned that sharing account credentials with personal, third-party AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and that actions taken by such tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes or the use of MileagePlus miles. It also flagged the risk of violating federal aviation rules, including the requirement that a human complete flight check-in to acknowledge that bags contain no banned substances.

United said it will restrict access both within its digital platforms and indirectly via travel agencies and aggregators, with updates to its booking, ticketing and distribution policies. The step comes as airlines and banks struggle to distinguish genuine customers from AI systems acting on their behalf, and follows a warning last week from banks including Bank of America urging customers not to share passwords with AI assistants.

pro.en: Google has rolled out Gemini 4 Hydrogen to its search engine, calling it the biggest model upgrade to Search to date. The model is now the default in AI Mode and is being used for the hardest queries in AI Overviews, and the company says the update is reaching all Search users worldwide.

The model is designed to parse more demanding queries, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests and hard-to-decipher typos. Google says it improves the fan-out technique, which splits a single prompt into subqueries and runs them simultaneously, surfacing a wider range of links that users might otherwise have missed.

Responses will also look different, with more images, comparison tables, graphs and maps. One demonstration showed an interactive animated driving simulation explaining how phones determine a car's lane on a highway without cell service, and Google says language understanding has improved across all AI Mode languages.

Hydrogen is positioned as a fast model rather than a flagship. TechCrunch notes that Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon remain the company's frontier models for deep reasoning, while Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than its predecessor, Gemini 3.8 Flash. It offers four thinking levels, including a new extra-high tier, and is also arriving in the Gemini app, the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

For university students, the change means search can field messy, conversational questions with several parts and the occasional typo. Many of the speed and quality claims, however, come from Google itself, so independent testing and everyday experience will determine whether they hold.

paragraphs.en: British police arrested a US Army officer on Tuesday near the city of Gloucester in England. They suspect that he helped Russia spy on the West. A source told ABC News that he is Lt. pro.en: A U.S. Army officer was taken into custody on Tuesday near Gloucester, England, by British counterterrorism police who suspect him of working for Russian interests. A source told ABC News he is Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, 41, who was posted at Imjin Barracks, the Gloucester garrison that houses a NATO headquarters; The Wall Street Journal was first to publish his name.

Authorities say the investigation falls under the National Security Act 2023, legislation targeting espionage and foreign interference, and that he is suspected of breaching two of its provisions: aiding a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information. What exactly he is alleged to have done has not been made public. Searches took place at two sites in Gloucestershire, he remains in custody at a London police station, and British charges are anticipated within days.

His unit, the Allied Rapid Reaction Corps, is a British-led NATO land formation that draws on personnel from 20 countries and exists to react quickly to crises. Army figures indicate that American service members convicted of espionage-related offenses have mostly been junior or mid-level, frequently driven by money; senior officers are a rarer category, and their ranks tend to open doors to more valuable secrets. Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, who heads Army Counterintelligence Command, described the case as a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent.

Under Army court records, a U.S. service member found guilty in an allied country may serve a sentence there before facing a separate prosecution under American military justice, which could mean a second trial. FBI Director Kash Patel called the arrest important and said the bureau has no tolerance for anyone who violates their oath to the United States. The case comes as a number of European governments warn of growing Russian covert activity such as sabotage, espionage and drone incursions.

Police said the arrest is not connected to other counterterrorism investigations, among them a suspected Iran-linked plot in September at a U.S.-run base in Britain. For students, the case shows that military alliances depend on trust and on tight protection of secrets. The next steps are formal charges in Britain, with separate U.S. Army charges expected afterward.

issues.title: Nvidia Keeps Its Korea GPU Plan After CEO Jensen Huang Resigns
issues.gist: Korea's science minister says Nvidia will still send up to 260,000 GPUs to Korea after CEO Jensen Huang resigned. Korean stocks swung up and down as investors tried to guess what the change means for AI and chips.
issues.gistKo: 엔비디아 CEO 젠슨 황이 물러났지만, 한국 과학기술 장관은 엔비디아가 한국에 GPU를 최대 26만 개 공급하겠다는 약속을 지킨다고 밝혔어요. 한국 증시는 AI와 반도체에 미칠 영향을 두고 출렁였어요.
issues.easyKo: 엔비디아의 대표가 갑자기 물러나서 한국 AI 계획이 흔들릴까 걱정했어요. 정부는 약속한 GPU 공급이 그대로라고 했지만, 시장은 아직 불안해하고 있어요.

paragraphs.en: Nvidia has confirmed that it still plans to deploy up to 260,000 graphics processing units in South Korea. Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon said so on Friday in a Facebook post, after the ministry held a meeting with Nvidia on open issues. The news came a day after CEO Jensen Huang resigned. Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO after Huang stepped down.
paragraphs.ko: 엔비디아는 한국에 그래픽 처리 장치(GPU)를 최대 26만 개 설치하려는 계획이 그대로라고 확인했어요. 배경훈 과학기술 장관은 금요일 페이스북 글에서, 부처가 엔비디아와 현안을 놓고 회의를 했다고 밝혔어요. 이 소식은 젠슨 황 CEO가 사임한 지 하루 뒤에 나왔어요. 엔비디아는 황이 물러난 뒤 최고재무책임자 콜레트 크레스를 임시 CEO로 정했어요.

paragraphs.en: Nvidia announced the GPU plan in October, as part of an effort to build large AI factories in Korea. The government and big companies, including Samsung Electronics, SK Group, Hyundai Motor Group and Naver Cloud, would each build AI computing centers. These centers would run on Nvidia's newest Blackwell chips. A GPU is a powerful chip that does many calculations at once, so it is widely used to train and run AI models.

paragraphs.en: Investors still felt nervous. On Thursday, the KOSPI closed down 0.61 percent at 5,342.73, ending a two-day rally. On Friday it opened 2.05 percent higher and rose as high as 5,504.44, but then turned negative. The index closed down 0.98 percent at 5,290.53, as foreigners sold a net 550.5 billion won worth of stocks. SK hynix lost 3.03 percent, and Naver, where Nvidia is the third-largest shareholder, fell 5.12 percent. On Thursday, Nvidia shares dropped more than 13 percent in trading before closing down 4.34 percent.

paragraphs.en: Experts see both risks and chances for Korea. Ahn Ki-hyun of the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association said Nvidia has few other places to buy high-bandwidth memory, so Korean makers could even gain. The research firm SemiAnalysis said Huang personally secured memory supply in Korea, so Nvidia's special treatment could weaken without him. One company official worried more about new projects Huang pushed himself, such as AI factories, physical AI and robotics. Meritz Securities warned that a more careful Nvidia could slow financing for AI data center firms.

pro.en: Nvidia has reaffirmed its commitment to deploying up to 260,000 graphics processing units in South Korea, Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon said in a Facebook post on Friday, after his ministry met the company to discuss pending issues. The assurance came a day after Chief Executive Jensen Huang resigned, and the company named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress interim CEO.

The company unveiled the GPU supply plan in October as part of an effort to build large-scale AI factories in the country. Under the tie-up, the government and industry leaders, among them Samsung Electronics, SK Group, Hyundai Motor Group and Naver Cloud, are each to establish their own computing centers powered by Nvidia's latest Blackwell processors, a class of chip designed to handle many calculations simultaneously and widely used to train and run AI models.

Investors nonetheless remained skittish. The benchmark KOSPI ended Thursday down 0.61 percent at 5,342.73, snapping a two-day winning streak, then opened 2.05 percent higher on Friday and touched 5,504.44 before sliding into negative territory and finishing 0.98 percent lower at 5,290.53 as foreign investors offloaded a net 550.5 billion won in equities. SK hynix shed 3.03 percent, while Naver, in which Nvidia is the third-largest shareholder, slumped 5.12 percent. Nvidia's own shares had plunged more than 13 percent in trading on Thursday before closing 4.34 percent lower.

Industry sources and analysts offered a split verdict. Ahn Ki-hyun of the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association argued that Nvidia lacks alternatives to its handful of memory suppliers, so Korean makers could stand to benefit. SemiAnalysis said Huang had personally secured memory capacity in South Korea, implying that Nvidia's preferential treatment could erode in his absence. One executive at a Korean company with ties to Nvidia voiced greater concern about long-horizon ventures the CEO had championed, including AI factories, physical AI and robotics, and Meritz Securities cautioned that a more conservative Nvidia could slow financing for AI infrastructure operators.

For South Korea, whose economy is closely bound to the chip and AI supply chain, developments at Nvidia can reverberate through local markets within hours. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix declined to comment, and attention now turns to whether new leadership sustains the pace of the Korean projects and whether memory supply terms shift.

views.view: The science minister says Nvidia kept its plan to supply up to 260,000 GPUs and that cooperation will continue.
An industry group executive says Korean memory makers could even gain, since Nvidia has few other suppliers of high-bandwidth memory.
A company official worries that long-term projects Huang pushed himself may change under new leadership.
An analyst says rising AI uncertainty weighed on the market as foreign investors sold.

issues.gist: South Korea's foreign minister, Cho Hyun, held talks in Beijing with China's Wang Yi on Nov. 13. They talked about peace on the Korean Peninsula and planned for next week's APEC summit.

views.view: Cho said peace on the peninsula is a shared interest, and Wang said China's policy has not changed.
The visit was meant to prepare for the APEC summit and to discuss the chance of North Korea-U.S. talks.

talk.answer: In this news, Cho and Wang met in Beijing before the APEC summit in Shenzhen. I think meeting in person helps both sides clear up differences before their leaders meet. It also shows that Seoul and Beijing want to keep talking, even about hard topics like North Korea.

paragraphs.en: South Korea's foreign minister, Cho Hyun, flew to Beijing on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, to meet his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi. The two held talks and had dinner, and it was their first meeting in about three months. Their last meeting was in Seoul in August. Before leaving, Cho said he would discuss bilateral ties and plans for the coming APEC summit in Shenzhen.

paragraphs.en: In his opening remarks, Cho said peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula serve the shared interests of both countries. He asked China to keep up strategic communication and to play a constructive role in bringing North Korea back to dialogue. Wang said ties had returned to a normal track after the leaders' visits last year and early this year. He also said trade between the two countries is expected to hit a record high this year. Wang hoped that people-to-people exchanges would recover to around 10 million a year.
paragraphs.ko: 조 장관은 한반도 평화와 안정이 양국의 공동 이익이라고 말했어요. 북한을 대화로 이끄는 데 중국이 건설적인 역할을 해 달라고도 했어요. 왕 부장은 양국 관계가 정상 궤도로 돌아왔다고 했고, 올해 교역이 사상 최고가 될 것으로 본다고 했어요. 인적 교류가 연 1000만 명 수준으로 회복되기를 바란다고도 했어요.

sents.en: In his opening remarks, Cho said peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula serve the shared interests of both countries.
sents.ko: 조 장관은 모두 발언에서 한반도의 평화와 안정이 두 나라의 공동 이익에 도움이 된다고 말했어요.

sents.en: He asked China to keep up strategic communication and to play a constructive role in bringing North Korea back to dialogue.
sents.ko: 그는 중국이 전략적 소통을 이어 가고 북한을 대화로 이끄는 데 건설적인 역할을 해 달라고 요청했어요.

sents.en: Wang said ties had returned to a normal track after the leaders' visits last year and early this year.
sents.ko: 왕 부장은 지난해와 올해 초 정상들의 방문 뒤 양국 관계가 정상 궤도로 돌아왔다고 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: The talks came as U.S. President Donald Trump has shown interest in restarting dialogue with Pyongyang. Cho told reporters he did not see much chance of China actively inviting Kim Jong-un to the APEC summit, but it was still too early to tell. A South Korean presidential official said a Trump-Kim meeting on the sidelines of the summit was unlikely. The official added that it is hard to predict whether the two might make contact before or after the summit.

paragraphs.en: Cho's visit was meant to prepare for President Lee Jae Myung's trip to the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday and Thursday. A meeting between Lee and Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected there. The two ministers were also expected to touch on pending issues, such as economic and cultural exchanges and Chinese structures in the Yellow Sea. For Korean students, the news matters because trade, travel and regional safety all depend on stable ties between Seoul and Beijing. Next, watch what Lee and Xi say in Shenzhen.

sents.ko: 다음으로 선전에서 이 대통령과 시 주석이 무슨 말을 하는지 지켜보세요.

pro.en: South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun traveled to Beijing on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, for talks and a dinner with his Chinese counterpart, Wang Yi, the first ministerial meeting between the two in roughly three months. They last met in Seoul in August. Speaking to reporters at Gimpo International Airport before departure, Cho said he would address the overall state of bilateral relations and issues requiring coordination ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.

In his opening remarks, Cho said peace and stability on the peninsula served the shared interests of both nations and urged continued strategic communication, later calling on Beijing to play a constructive role in bringing North Korea back to dialogue, according to Seoul's foreign ministry. Wang said relations had returned to a normal track after the leaders' reciprocal visits last year and early this year, noted that bilateral trade is projected to reach a record high this year, and voiced hope that people-to-people exchanges would rebound to around 10 million annually.

The meeting took place against speculation that President Donald Trump, who has signaled interest in resuming dialogue with Pyongyang, might meet Kim Jong-un during his Asia trip. Cho said he saw little chance of China actively inviting Kim to the summit, though it remained too early to tell. A South Korean presidential official said a Trump-Kim encounter on the summit's sidelines was unlikely, while cautioning that contact before or after the gathering was difficult to predict.

Yonhap observed that the talks came amid deepening ties between China and North Korea, noting that Wang was present during Kim's surprise visit to the border city of Dandong last month. Inter-Korean relations remain stalled, with Pyongyang rejecting the Lee Jae Myung administration's overtures. KBS World cited analysts who suggested that Beijing, as host, may be reluctant to see a high-profile North Korea-U.S. meeting overshadow the event, while Wang said China's Korean Peninsula policy was unchanged.

Cho's trip was intended to lay the groundwork for Lee's visit to the Shenzhen summit on Wednesday and Thursday, where a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping is anticipated. The ministers were also expected to touch on pending bilateral matters, including economic and cultural exchanges and Chinese structures installed in the Yellow Sea. For Korean students, the stakes are practical, since trade, travel and regional security hinge on stable relations between Seoul and Beijing; attention now turns to what the two leaders say in Shenzhen.

pro.en: England captain Harry Kane was crowned the men's Ballon d'Or winner for the first time at a ceremony in London's Palladium, becoming at 33 the first English recipient since Michael Owen a quarter of a century ago and the latest honoree to emerge from Bayern Munich's attack.

The award recognized a campaign in which Kane struck 73 times in 65 appearances for club and country, helping Bayern to a domestic league and cup double and England to the World Cup semifinals, their strongest showing since the 1966 triumph; he also finished as Europe's leading club scorer in 2025-26, ahead of runner-up Kylian Mbappe and third-placed Lamine Yamal.

DW observed that Kane is the first Bayern player to claim the trophy since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981, while coach Vincent Kompany argued that English observers had long reduced him to a finisher and undervalued his footballing intelligence, likening him to a fine wine that improves with age; detractors allege stat-padding against modest opposition, though his 213 goals in 320 Premier League matches stand comparison with any player in that competition's history.

Accepting the prize, Kane conceded that his path had been anything but linear, recalling the loan spells and the struggle needed to reach the summit, and expressed hope that his example would instill resolve in aspiring players.

ESPN reported that he has since agreed a new Bayern contract through 2029 worth more than 30 million euros a year, and that he was poised to overtake Peter Shilton's tally of 125 caps to become England's most-capped player against Croatia, though a major international trophy still eludes him.

views.view: Kane won because of his goals, his leadership and his all-round game, which his coach says England long underrated.
Some critics say he pads his numbers against weaker teams, but his Premier League record answers them.
Kane has a strong case to be called England's greatest player, and only a major trophy with England is missing.

pro.en: A car bomb detonated in Moscow on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, wounding Sergei Zavorotny, a former adviser to Mykola Azarov, the prime minister of Ukraine until 2014. Russia's Investigative Committee said he was behind the wheel when the device went off and was rushed to hospital. The blast followed, a day earlier, a similar car explosion in Saint Petersburg that killed a member of the Russian military.

Zavorotny had served Azarov until the latter resigned and fled to Russia in 2014. Unverified Russian reports claim he lost his left arm and sustained other serious injuries, while Azarov told the Russian news agency TASS he knew nothing of the explosion beyond the fact that Zavorotny survived. Investigators said they would commission medical and explosives examinations, and Russian outlets cast the bombings as the latest in a string of attacks on pro-Kremlin figures.

Both countries continued to hit each other's territory overnight. Ukrainian authorities said Russian bombardment struck a hospital and that three people were killed in attacks on Odesa and Zaporizhzhia, while Russia said a Ukrainian strike on an industrial facility in the Samara region killed four. Four more people died when drones struck an industrial zone in the Volgograd region, Russia said, and Kyiv describes its strikes as retaliatory, given Moscow's persistent targeting of its cities.

The bombing came amid intense diplomacy. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who had met Vladimir Putin in Moscow, were followed by informal peace talks in Dublin, and Irish premier Micheal Martin said Europe's voice could not be confined to EU member states, a formulation that paves the way for a British role. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged Donald Trump to spring no surprises ahead of expected meetings with Xi Jinping and Putin at next week's APEC summit in China, and DW reports that European leaders face pressure to name a single representative for the negotiations.

Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and occupies roughly a fifth of the country, and repeated attempts to broker a settlement have so far failed. Observers will watch who is chosen to represent Europe and what unfolds at the APEC summit. For South Korean students, the conflict matters chiefly through its effect on global energy prices and the wider security environment.

views.view: DW reports that European leaders are under pressure to name one representative for the peace talks, and that the EU's Kaja Kallas laughed wryly when asked why Europe gets one seat and the US two.
The BBC reports that Russia calls the car bombs the latest in a series of attacks on pro-Kremlin figures, and that continued efforts to broker peace have failed so far.
