pro.en: The Korea Baseball Organization published its list of free-agent-eligible players Friday, with two linchpins of the Samsung Lions' Korean Series championship at the top. The league said 28 players qualify this offseason: 15 for the first time, six for a second or third time, and seven who held off last year.

Captain Koo Ja-wook, 33, took Korean Series MVP honors by batting 10-for-20 with one homer and six RBIs as his side beat the KT Wiz in five games, and he claimed his first batting title at .371. He has reportedly retained a U.S.-based agent to pursue a major league opening, although the Lions are expected to try to retain their franchise player.

Starter Won Tae-in, 26, earned the win in the clincher, working five innings of one-run ball, which masked a regular season of 7-9 with a 4.52 ERA over 26 outings, his worst figures in six years. A longtime fan favorite in Daegu, he is expected to command considerable interest in a market short of viable starting pitchers.

The Wiz and the SSG Landers each have six eligible players, while the Doosan Bears have three, among them 39-year-old catcher Yang Eui-ji. Players have until Sunday to exercise their rights, the final list is due Monday, and negotiations with any club open Tuesday, with compensation owed to the previous club rising with the signee's salary class.

pro.en: South Korea's rice output declined for a fifth consecutive year in 2026, the Ministry of Data and Statistics reported on Friday. Production slipped 0.9 percent from a year earlier to 3.5 million tons, the fourth-lowest total since the government began compiling the data in 1965.
Land given over to rice paddies shrank 1.1 percent to 670,000 hectares, the smallest footprint ever recorded, though the harvest from every 1,000 square meters edged up 0.2 percent to 524 kilograms.

Rice is still a pillar of the Korean diet, yet Koreans have been eating steadily less of it for decades as tastes have shifted. The decline in output also coincided with official efforts to manage production and to encourage farmers to switch to other crops.

By region, South Jeolla Province and Gwangju together accounted for 736,000 tons, the largest share, followed by South Chungcheong Province at 681,000 tons and North Jeolla Province at 526,000 tons. For students, the figures illustrate how everyday food choices can reshape an entire farming sector, and observers will next watch whether the paddy area continues to shrink.

views.view: Rice output fell for the fifth year as people's diets changed, and paddy area reached a record low.
The paper carries the same report: output is down, yield per area is up, and the government wants farmers to switch crops.

pro.en: Kia has announced a $2 billion investment in a second Indian manufacturing site, after Kia India signed a memorandum of understanding with the Andhra Pradesh state government in the country's southeast. The plant will rise in Anantapur, where the carmaker has been running a factory since 2019.
Production is slated to begin in early 2030 at an annual capacity of 200,000 vehicles, which would lift Kia's combined capacity in India beyond 600,000 units a year.
Kia's current Indian lineup spans the Seltos, Sonet, Syros, Carens, Carens Clavis and Carnival, in a country that ranks as the world's third-largest car market behind China and the United States.

The project is one strand of Hyundai Motor Group's wider push to strengthen its presence in India, where the conglomerate said in October it would commit $15.5 billion between 2026 and 2032, a pairing of commitments that underscores how much weight Korean carmakers now attach to the market.

views.view: Yonhap says Kia will build a second plant in India as part of Hyundai Motor Group's wider push there.

pro.en: Eurovision, the continent-spanning song contest, stages its inaugural Asia edition in Bangkok on Saturday, Nov. 14, with 11 countries competing in a show to be broadcast on television in participating nations and streamed on YouTube. The flagship contest drew 131 million viewers in 2026, making it the world's biggest televised live music event.

The finalists were selected in national competitions. South Korea sends K-pop star Junhee, Bangladesh fields Beatmosphere, an all-male a cappella beatbox collective, and Nepal is represented by Pratik Himal Rai, while Vietnam's Toc Tien, performing a pop-dance track, is tipped as a favourite to win.

Skeptics abound. India, Japan and China are missing from the lineup, ticket sales have been sluggish, and the production reportedly absorbed a one-million-dollar budget cut, though the executive producer insists that a first year inevitably carries limitations. Eurovision expert Dean Vuletic argues that most entries are love songs lacking a pointed message.

Half of the votes are cast by a jury and half by viewers, and no nation may vote for itself, so ballots often track national relationships. The producer noted that viewers in Cambodia and Thailand, which clashed over their border last year, could vote against one another, and he voiced hope that the event would be the first of many.

views.view: BBC says the Asia contest is not widely known in the region, though many Asian fans love Eurovision.
The report says ticket sales are slow, three big Asian countries are absent, and the budget was cut.

pro.en: CL of 2NE1 has secured a deal with the music agency The Black Label, the company announced on Friday. She will reunite with Teddy, the K-pop producer behind the music of her group as well as acts such as Blackpink.
The arrangement marks the first time in roughly seven years that the performer has been affiliated with another agency, having parted ways with YG Entertainment in 2019.

The agency said CL was embarking on a journey grounded in profound trust in Teddy, with whom she has long collaborated, adding that she was preparing for a leap in her career, beginning with a new single due by the end of this year.

The 2NE1 leader had been forging her own path through a one-person agency, Very Cherry, and released her first solo studio album, Alpha, in 2021. Fans will now wait to hear what the new single sounds like.

views.view: CL has joined The Black Label and will work again with Teddy, with a new single planned by the end of the year.

pro.en: South Korea's yearly count of foreign visitors went past 20 million for the first time, according to the culture ministry on Thursday. Second Vice Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism Kim Dae-hyun went to Incheon International Airport, the country's main gateway, to receive the 20 millionth arrival.

The country needed 14 years to reach the threshold after yearly arrivals first exceeded 10 million in 2012. The government credited the record to a range of factors, among them the worldwide appeal of Korean pop culture and the hospitality extended to foreign tourists.

Minister Chae Hwi-young called the milestone a "starting point" in Seoul's drive to become an "irreplaceable tourism powerhouse," and pledged that the government would build the capacity to draw 30 million foreign visitors a year before ushering in an era of 40 million.

For university students, a surge in visitors could translate into more work in retail, food service, lodging and guiding, along with more occasions to use English. The question ahead is whether the 30 million target will be matched by enough accommodation, staffing and transport.

pro.en: Musinsa, the South Korean fashion and retail platform operator, announced on Friday that it will enter the Thai market through a partnership with Central Marketing Group, or CMG, to open Musinsa Standard stores there. The company offered no timeline for the openings, and the Korea Herald reported that the exclusive distribution agreement was signed on Nov. 4.

CMG is the retail arm of the Thai conglomerate Central Retail and manages more than 30 global brands. Musinsa cited rising demand for Korean fashion as Korean entertainment and culture gain popularity in Thailand, noting that transaction value in Thailand on its global online store climbed 26 percent in the first half of the year from a year earlier, and said it intends to translate that online interest into offline sales.

Thailand becomes Musinsa's fifth Southeast Asian market after the Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam and Malaysia, although Yonhap noted that no outlets have yet opened in those four countries. In China, the company already operates two Musinsa Store outlets and five Musinsa Standard stores, and it plans to open its first Standard store in Japan next year.

At home, Musinsa runs 49 Musinsa Standard stores and eight Musinsa Store outlets, and about 20,000 Korean fashion brands sell on its online platform, roughly 4,000 of which are also available through its English-language Musinsa Global. For students eyeing fashion or retail careers, the move illustrates how Korean brands lean on local partners to scale abroad, and attention now turns to when the first Thai stores will open.

pro.en: The U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday passed the Combating Foreign Threats to Main Street Act of 2026, legislation aimed at shielding American small businesses from economic and cybersecurity threats posed by foreign adversaries, including North Korea.

The measure would direct the Small Business Administration to furnish small firms with information and guidance for identifying and responding to hazards including intellectual property theft, cyberattacks, counterfeit goods and predatory investment practices, and, beginning in October 2027, to review its educational materials annually.

Rep. Roger Williams, a Texas Republican, told the chamber that such threats touch businesses of every size, yet smaller firms are frequently the most vulnerable because they lack the resources and expertise to protect themselves.

The bill now awaits deliberation in the Senate. For Seoul, it illustrates how Washington frames North Korean cyber activity as an economic-security problem, and whether the Senate takes the measure up is the next development to watch.

pro.en: Google has rolled out Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a general-purpose model aimed at everyday workloads and agentic coding, and it supersedes Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company's product line with immediate availability. The elemental naming convention, as Ars Technica observed, is less descriptive than the earlier Pro and Flash tiers.

According to Google, Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8 at the default high setting and cuts fabricated claims more than fivefold in the company's own evaluation. It offers four reasoning tiers, low, medium, high and a new xhigh, along with a one-million-token context window for input.

On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Hydrogen posts 51 at the default tier and 54 at xhigh, edging out the larger Argon's 50, a result The Decoder said could render Argon obsolete less than four weeks after its debut. The independent evaluation nonetheless showed it trailing Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol on agentic terminal tasks.

Developers can access the model through the API at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, unchanged from 3.8 Flash, whereas Carbon and Argon are priced at $2 and $10 for now but are slated to rise to $4 and $20 from next month, Ars Technica reported.

Google is also folding Hydrogen into Search, promising better handling of lengthy, multipart queries and more visual responses; Ars Technica cautioned, however, that AI Plus and free Gemini app users remain on an older, smaller model.

views.view: Hydrogen is much faster, makes fewer false claims and keeps the old price, though Google has made big claims before.
Hydrogen is cheaper and can beat the larger Argon on one index, which may leave Argon obsolete.
An independent test found Hydrogen rarely makes things up but is weaker than rivals at terminal work.

pro.en: NBC has slotted its new single-camera comedy Sunset P.I. for a Monday, Feb. 8 premiere at 8:30 p.m. ET/PT, with episodes arriving on the Peacock streaming service the following day. The network also unveiled a batch of first-look images.

The 10-episode workplace comedy centers on Mickey Wilder, played by Jake Johnson, a sharp, cynical and heartbroken private investigator and former LAPD officer whose life collapsed three years earlier. He works at a Hollywood detective agency run by his boss, Julius Royal, played by Keith David, while Jane Levy plays Faye, an investigative journalist.

Dan Goor and Luke Del Tredici created the series and serve as writers and executive producers, with Akiva Schaffer directing the pilot for Universal Television. The creators have cited the 1980s dramedy Moonlighting and the acclaimed medical drama The Pitt as inspirations.

Sunset P.I. was officially ordered to series in May as one of four new shows NBC commissioned for the 2026-2027 season. It will air after St. Denis Medical at 8 p.m., taking over the slot now held by The Rise and Fall of Reggie Dinkins, which wraps its second season in mid-January.

pro.en: Samba Schutte has been elevated to series regular status on Apple TV's Pluribus for its second season, which is currently in production. He appeared as a guest star in the first season, playing Mr. Diabaté.

The character is a Mauritanian man who sees the bright side of the situation and cultivates a hedonistic lifestyle in a Las Vegas hotel. Like Rhea Seehorn's Carol, he is immune to the outbreak, and Schutte earned a Saturn Award nomination for best guest star.

The series premiered on Apple TV in November 2025 to a favorable reception from critics and viewers. Its first season collected 18 Emmy nominations and six wins, including outstanding lead actress in a drama series for Seehorn and outstanding writing for creator Vince Gilligan.

Schutte is a Dutch-Mauritanian actor raised in Ethiopia, whose credits include the HBO Max pirate comedy Our Flag Means Death and the NBC sitcom Sunnyside. The second-season cast also features Karolina Wydra and Carlos-Manuel Vesga.

views.view: The show was well received by critics and audiences and was one of the most nominated series at the Emmys.
Schutte's guest role earned a Saturn Award nomination, and the show won six Emmys in season one.

issues.title: Seoul Press Club Voices Concern Over Russia Holding a Japanese Journalist
issues.gist: A club of foreign reporters in Seoul says it is deeply worried that Russia is holding a Japanese journalist on spying suspicion. It says legitimate reporting must be respected.
issues.gistKo: 서울의 외신 기자 단체가 러시아가 일본 기자를 간첩 혐의로 붙잡고 있는 것을 깊이 우려한다고 밝혔어요. 정당한 취재는 존중받아야 한다고 했어요.
issues.easyKo: 러시아가 일본 신문 기자를 간첩 혐의로 구금하자, 서울에 있는 외신 기자 모임이 걱정을 밝혔어요. 기자의 안전과 법적 권리를 지키고 구금 이유를 설명하라는 요구예요.

views.view: The Seoul club says legitimate newsgathering must be respected and threats to a journalist's safety cannot be justified.
It says Russia must immediately release the Japanese journalist and warns that journalists must not be used as leverage.
It reports Russia's claim that he gathered information on defense for Japanese intelligence, a charge that can bring up to 20 years in prison.

pro.en: A press group based in Seoul expressed serious alarm on Thursday over Russia's detention of a Japanese journalist on espionage suspicion, insisting that lawful reporting be respected. The Seoul Foreign Correspondents' Club, a foreign press association, published its statement online on Nov. 12.

Last month, Russia's Federal Security Service announced that it had detained a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun in the far eastern Sakhalin region, alleging he was spying. He was subsequently transferred to Moscow, where a court placed him in pretrial detention.

In its statement, the club's board argued that gathering information in the public interest is fundamental to journalism and that endangering a reporter's safety on such grounds cannot be justified. It called on Russian authorities to guarantee the detainee's physical safety and legal rights and to spell out why he is being held.

Other organizations have also responded. The Committee to Protect Journalists demanded his release, and Japan's Foreign Ministry summoned Russia's ambassador to Tokyo and asked that the detained Japanese national be treated in a humane, fair and impartial manner. Reports said the court had remanded him in custody until Dec. 12.

issues.title: Should AI Companies Pay for the Journalism They Use?
issues.gist: More people now get news from AI chatbots, and news groups say AI firms use their reporting without paying. Experts disagree on whether new rules or new payments are the answer.

pro.en: Large numbers of people now rely on AI chatbots for fast answers about current events. A 2026 survey by the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, covering more than 90,000 people worldwide, found that 10 percent use chatbots for news weekly, a figure significantly higher among younger audiences, and the institute's annual report notes that growing numbers are experimenting with chatbots as a new means of access.

For publishers, the shift threatens the economics of reporting. Julia Becker, publisher of Funke Media Group, told a conference in Berlin on Nov. 5 that the old bargain, in which search engines indexed news sites and sent traffic back, had broken down. DW Director General Barbara Massing argued that AI companies draw on quality reporting to generate answers while the journalism itself often remains invisible, adding that such systems should not merely use it but also pay for it.

Legal and political pressure is mounting. In October, German broadcasters ARD and RTL, together with two industry associations, called for stronger copyright protections for media companies, while in the United States The New York Times has sued Brave Software for allegedly using its content without permission and circumventing its paywall. European legal institutions, including the European Court of Justice, are examining whether AI-generated answers can themselves infringe copyright.

Experts put forward competing remedies. Martin Senftleben, a professor at the University of Amsterdam, said compensation for training is legally thornier than the more pressing question of AI systems drawing on journalism to answer queries in real time, and floated a mandatory scheme under which each such answer would trigger a payment gathered by a collecting body and distributed in the manner of music royalties. Google said it is willing to negotiate with German media companies and is piloting an early-stage "AI Contribution" program with selected publishers.

Others urge caution. Joerg Heidrich, a technology lawyer at Heise, warned that additional rules could hamper European firms in the global AI race and overlook startups, independent developers and research institutions that rely on data to build and train models. How the courts, EU regulators and licensing deals settle the question will shape where chatbot answers come from and who is paid for the news readers consume.

views.view: Publishers worry that chatbots use their reporting while sending fewer readers and less money back to news sites.
A law professor says AI answers that use journalism could trigger payments collected like music royalties, while a lawyer warns that more rules could hurt startups and research.

issues.title: Could the AI Boom Make Borrowing More Expensive in Europe?
issues.gist: US tech giants are selling huge amounts of bonds to pay for AI data centers. Some experts worry this could raise borrowing costs for European governments and companies.

pro.en: With more than $1 trillion flowing into the artificial intelligence buildout, US tech giants are now vying with European governments and companies for the same pool of investment capital. Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle have issued roughly $250 billion in dollar bonds since the start of 2025 and a further €37 billion in euros, while Microsoft recently joined the borrowing spree with a $25 billion sale. Goldman Sachs projects $420 billion in new AI hyperscaler bond issuance next year.

That is unwelcome for euro zone sovereigns such as France, whose bond yields have already risen sharply. With public debt at 119% of GDP, France has seen its 10-year yield climb from about 3.7% to nearly 5% in six months, and its annual interest bill is forecast to rise from €79 billion to €91 billion next year. Energy prices and France's political crisis have also driven the increase, not AI alone.

In August, economists at the European Central Bank said the euro bond market was adjusting well to the AI giants but cautioned that their borrowing could make it harder for other firms to obtain financing, with a potential spillover into the sovereign and supranational segment, although none is evident in the euro area so far. Viktor Hjort of BNP Paribas describes the phenomenon as "bond abundance" and says it already creates competition for investors' funds.

That competition could weigh on European corporates. Goldman found that interest costs as a share of sales among Stoxx 600 firms have climbed by nearly half since 2022, trimming earnings by more than 5%, and companies may be forced to curtail spending on plants, research and shareholder payouts.

Cities and regions may be exposed as well. A study prepared for the OECD found that in several European countries where AI diffusion was fastest, municipal borrowing costs tended to rise, in contrast to the United States, according to its co-author. The article stresses that AI bonds are far from the sole cause of Europe's fiscal strains, but further issuance is planned for next year.

views.view: US tech bond sales may push up borrowing costs for European governments and firms.
The euro bond market is adapting well and no spillovers are clear yet, but the issue needs close watching.
Hyperscalers already create competition for investors' money in the euro bond market.

issues.title: NHS England Removes Claim That 137 Trusts Benefit From Palantir's AI Data Tool
issues.gist: NHS England deleted a webpage saying 137 hospital trusts were benefiting from Palantir's AI data platform. The Guardian had found that 29 of them were not using all or most of it.
issues.gistKo: 영국 NHS 잉글랜드가 팔란티어의 AI 데이터 플랫폼으로 병원 137곳이 혜택을 본다는 글을 지웠어요. 가디언이 그중 29곳은 대부분을 쓰지 않는다고 밝힌 뒤예요.

paragraphs.en: NHS England took down a webpage saying that 137 hospital trusts gain from Palantir's AI health data system. The Guardian had reported that 29 of those trusts were not using all or most of the system. The system is called the federated data platform, or FDP. It was set up to improve patient care, make operating theatres more efficient and speed up the time it takes to discharge patients.
paragraphs.ko: NHS 잉글랜드가 팔란티어 AI 데이터 시스템으로 병원 137곳이 혜택을 본다는 주장을 지웠어요. 가디언이 29곳이 대부분 쓰지 않는다고 밝힌 뒤예요.

sents.en: NHS England took down a webpage saying that 137 hospital trusts gain from Palantir's AI health data system.
sents.ko: NHS 잉글랜드는 병원 조합(트러스트) 137곳이 팔란티어의 AI 보건 데이터 시스템으로 혜택을 본다는 웹사이트의 주장을 지웠어요.

sents.en: The Guardian had reported that 29 of those trusts were not using all or most of the system.
sents.ko: 가디언은 그중 29곳이 시스템의 전부 또는 대부분을 쓰지 않는다고 보도했어요.

sents.en: The system is called the federated data platform, or FDP.
sents.ko: 이 시스템은 연합 데이터 플랫폼(FDP)이라고 불러요.

sents.en: It was set up to improve patient care, make operating theatres more efficient and speed up the time it takes to discharge patients.
sents.ko: 환자 치료를 개선하고 수술실을 더 효율적으로 쓰며 퇴원 속도를 높이려고 만들었어요.

paragraphs.en: Health leaders had published a list of every trust that was "live" with the platform and "realising benefits". Then 29 trusts said it was not live or that they were not using any of its applications. The original list appears to have been taken down. A shorter page now says early users are seeing results such as less admin work and faster patient pathways. The campaign group Medact had sent freedom of information requests to every hospital and integrated care board in England.
paragraphs.ko: 웹사이트는 모든 기관이 「가동 중」이고 「혜택을 얻고 있다」고 올렸지만, 29곳이 그렇지 않다고 했어요. 목록은 내려갔고 더 짧은 글이 남았어요.

paragraphs.en: Ministers are deciding whether to extend Palantir's £330m contract to 2029. The Office for Statistics Regulation says it is examining the NHS claims about how widely the system is used. It had already warned NHS England that there was no evidence for a claim that the technology helped deliver more than 100,000 extra operations. In July, the Health Foundation shared an analysis of one FDP tool used for patient discharge planning. It found no noticeable improvement in discharge performance among trusts using that tool.

pro.en: NHS England has removed a statement from its website asserting that 137 hospital trusts are gaining from Palantir's AI-driven federated data platform (FDP), a retreat that followed a Guardian investigation finding that 29 of those trusts were using little or none of the controversial technology. The platform was intended to lift patient outcomes, make operating theatres run more efficiently and accelerate bed discharges.

Officials had posted a roster of every NHS organisation described as "live" on the FDP and "realising benefits", but once 29 trusts said the system was not yet running or that none of its applications were in use, the roster appears to have been withdrawn. A thinner page now says early adopters are already seeing results, among them reduced admin and faster patient pathways. The campaign group Medact had probed uptake by sending freedom of information requests to every hospital and integrated care board in England.

The development comes while ministers weigh whether to extend Palantir's £330m contract to 2029 and while the Office for Statistics Regulation scrutinises the NHS's claims about how widely the system is used. The watchdog had earlier cautioned NHS England that nothing supported its assertion that the technology helped deliver more than 100,000 extra operations. In July, the Health Foundation shared analysis of one FDP tool used in discharge planning, finding no noticeable improvement in discharge performance among the trusts using it.

Labour MP Ben Coleman called it troubling that NHS England had listed the 137 trusts but apparently pulled the list, and he wants the NHS to drop Palantir in favor of an open platform. The union Unison and several health groups also want the contract ended, while Palantir has said terminating it would be "putting politics above patients". Campaigners argue the deal could be safely ended in 2027 through a termination assistance period written into the contract.
NHS England did not respond to requests for comment. The question now is what ministers decide on the contract, and whether public trust in the platform can be restored.

views.view: The paper reports that NHS England removed a claim after trusts said they were not using the system, and critics call it misleading.

pro.en: A team at MIT has created an AI copilot for structural engineers that makes topology optimization, an algorithmic technique that progressively populates a design space so as to satisfy declared goals such as strength, a more collaborative process by inviting human input while a design is still evolving.

The leading algorithmic design tools remain costly in computing time and show their output only once finished, so users who want alterations typically have to begin afresh; the results can also be hard to fabricate, for example when eight or more beams meet at a single node, and engineers therefore tend to distrust strange-looking designs.

The new system draws on machine learning to forecast which regions of a design a person would most probably wish to modify, having been trained on a synthetic dataset of likely human critiques of thousands of designs concerning aesthetics, performance and manufacturability; Dat Ha, who recently earned his doctorate at MIT, is the lead author and associate professor Josephine Carstensen the senior author.

In demonstrations, the human-in-the-loop approach improved manufacturability or raised the linear buckling load by 39 percent while adding only 15 seconds to total design time, and the team argues that it complements rather than replaces AI-only methods, with Carstensen noting that human involvement also strengthens confidence in the final design.

At present users can only thicken or thin the flagged regions, though the researchers plan to add other modification options and hope the tool will reach academics and students as well as industry, bringing broader adoption of the technique.

issues.gist: A US lawmaker says Nvidia told him in private that it could track its advanced AI chips to fight smuggling. An industry group had said in public that such rules might not be possible.
issues.gistKo: 미국 의원이 엔비디아가 첨단 AI 반도체를 추적해 밀수를 막을 수 있다고 비공개로 말했다고 밝혔어요. 반면 업계 단체는 공개적으로 그런 규칙이 불가능할 수 있다고 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Nvidia told a US lawmaker in private that it could track its advanced AI chips to fight smuggling, the lawmaker said. Representative Bill Foster, an Illinois Democrat, told MIT Technology Review on Thursday that Nvidia's team said it was technically possible. He said they never put anything in writing, and Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment.

pro.en: Nvidia has told a US lawmaker in private that it could put in place ways to track its advanced AI chips and hold back smuggling, Rep. Bill Foster, an Illinois Democrat, said in an interview with MIT Technology Review on Thursday. Foster said the company's representatives put nothing in writing, and Nvidia did not answer requests for comment.

Foster co-sponsors the Chip Security Act, which would oblige the industry to confirm where advanced AI chips are located so they cannot be diverted to China. Its text allows for site inspections, corporate attestations or ping-based mechanisms in which a chip sends out its position once it is connected, and it is among three chip-security proposals being weighed for the Senate's defense authorization bill.

In public, the picture has been murkier: in March 2026 the Semiconductor Industry Association, which counts Nvidia as a member, came out against the bill and called its tracking mandates new, untested and potentially infeasible. Yet in December 2025 Nvidia introduced Fleet Intelligence, which lets customers keep tabs on chip performance across data center sites, and it confirmed to Reuters that the tool could show which country chips were in, while declining to say whether it could help against smuggling.

A September report by the Center for Security and Emerging Technology concluded that centralized ping-based verification, supplemented by physical inspections, would be the most robust and cost-effective approach, while also flagging significant shortcomings, such as an inability to detect a transfer to an unauthorized user when a chip stays put. The article adds that tracking would merely tell investigators where chips are, not allow them to be disabled.

He intends to introduce stricter legislation in the new year requiring a valid license to be verified before a GPU can connect, and he said the fallout at Nvidia following Jensen Huang's resignation has bolstered colleagues' support for the existing rules. Lawmakers will now watch the Senate defense bill and whether Nvidia repeats its private assurances in public.

pro.en: Two Korean series are generating buzz this week: the sequel "Crash 2," premiering Nov. 16, and MBC's psychological thriller "The Perfect Lie," which is already on air.

"Crash 2" continues the hit 2024 drama that was the first Korean series centered on traffic crime investigations. In the new season, the Traffic Crime Investigation unit from Namgang Police Station is elevated to a regional investigative team under the National Office of Investigation, taking on cases nationwide. Lee Min Ki returns as the analytical Cha Yeon Ho alongside Kwak Sun Young, Heo Sung Tae, Lee Ho Chul and Moon Hee, while NCT's Jisung joins as an eager rookie officer.

The cast has promised more elaborate crimes and a larger scale, with Lee Min Ki citing a new member of the team and the payoff of cases that run on from the first season. Despite reuniting after two years, the actors said it felt as though no time had passed. A preview clip shows Jisung's character bursting with enthusiasm over a case, to the astonishment of his sterner colleagues.

"The Perfect Lie" follows a man and a woman who give completely contradictory accounts of the same memory and clash over the truth. The series reunites Yoo Yeon Seok and Seo Hyun Jin, co-stars of "Dr. Romantic" a decade ago, as Min Joon Ho and Kang Ji Sun; branded a "gold digger" and stripped of her job, Kang remains determined to expose his true face.

From episode 5, airing Nov. 13 at 9:50 p.m. KST, Kang Ji Sun starts digging into Min Joon Ho's secrets in earnest, a shift the production team describes as a decision to pick herself back up. The "Crash 2" premiere and the new turn in "The Perfect Lie" are the next things for viewers to watch.

issues.title: North Korea Rejects G7 Call to Give Up Nuclear Weapons
issues.gist: North Korea said it will never give up its nuclear weapons after the G7 called for denuclearization. It also warned of action against a U.S.-led naval buildup.
issues.gistKo: 북한이 G7의 비핵화 요구에 핵무기를 포기하지 않겠다고 답했어요. 미국이 이끄는 해군력 증강에는 행동으로 맞서겠다고도 경고했어요.

paragraphs.en: North Korea answered the Group of Seven (G7) countries this week by saying it will never give up its nuclear weapons. G7 foreign ministers met in Paris and said they strongly condemn the North's nuclear and missile programs. They also repeated their goal of complete denuclearization of North Korea under United Nations Security Council resolutions.

pro.en: North Korea this week rebuffed the Group of Seven, insisting that its pursuit of nuclear weapons remains unshakable. G7 foreign ministers, meeting in Paris, had strongly condemned the North's illicit nuclear and ballistic missile programs and reaffirmed their commitment to its complete denuclearization in line with U.N. Security Council resolutions.

In a commentary carried by state media on Thursday, Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui rejected the appeal, declaring Pyongyang's resolve to retain nuclear arms steadfast and describing them as the most powerful guarantee of its sovereign rights. She argued that the G7 had no standing to comment on others' nuclear programs, noting that members such as the United States and Britain are themselves nuclear-armed.

Separately that day, Kim Jong-sik, a senior official of the ruling Workers' Party, denounced what he called a U.S.-led naval buildup. Citing nuclear submarine programs in South Korea, Japan and Australia, he said they risked fueling a new arms race, and he warned that the North's response would go beyond condemnation, vowing to deter threats through action.

Yonhap's weekly roundup of key developments carried further items: a test of a new torpedo that Pyongyang aims to deploy in early 2027, an expert's assessment that the odds of a Trump-Kim summit rise after the U.S. midterms, and an official's view in Seoul that the North is unlikely to attend APEC or open talks with Washington.

For South Korean readers the stakes are direct, since security on the peninsula hinges on how such exchanges evolve. Further statements from Pyongyang and any hint of dialogue with Washington will be the signals to watch.

issues.title: Germany's Conservatives Pick Ilse Aigner as Candidate for President
issues.gist: Chancellor Friedrich Merz's party named Ilse Aigner as its candidate for Germany's next president. She could become the country's first female president when a special committee votes on January 30.
issues.gistKo: 메르츠 총리의 정당이 일제 아이그너를 독일의 다음 대통령 후보로 정했어요. 1월 30일 특별위원회 투표에서 이기면 독일 최초의 여성 대통령이 될 수 있어요.
issues.easyKo: 독일 대통령은 의례적인 역할이지만 나라의 도덕적 권위로 여겨져요. 집권 정당들이 모두 지지해서 아이그너가 첫 여성 대통령이 될 가능성이 높아요.

views.view: Aigner's election looks highly likely because the governing parties hold a majority in the Federal Convention.
Aigner is respected, handled her years as agriculture minister without major crises, and enjoys excellent popularity ratings.
Her rise could end Söder's chancellor hopes, and the CDU would be unlikely to accept two CSU figures leading the country.

heads.title: Germany: CDU names Ilse Aigner as candidate for president

why: Germany has never had a female head of state, so this choice would be a historic first.
lines.agree: The main governing parties all say Aigner is a good choice for a unifying, mostly symbolic role.
lines.split: Some commentators see party games behind the choice, especially for Bavaria's leader Markus Söder.
lines.life: For Korean students, it shows how a parliamentary system picks a ceremonial leader very differently from a direct vote.
lines.next: Watch the Federal Convention vote on January 30, 2027, and the new president taking office in mid-March.

pro.en: Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats confirmed on Monday that they will put forward Ilse Aigner as a candidate for Germany's next head of state, with Merz announcing the decision alongside her at a Berlin press conference; her Bavarian sister party, the CSU, already supports her, and the Social Democrats, the coalition partner, have signaled they would endorse the nomination.

Aigner, 61, has presided over the Bavarian state parliament since 2018. The daughter of an electrician, she trained as a telecommunications technician and holds no university degree. She entered the Bavarian legislature in 1994, moved to the Bundestag in 1998, and later served as agriculture minister under then-Chancellor Angela Merkel.

The presidency is a largely ceremonial office, with most real political power resting with the chancellor, but a win would make Aigner the first woman and the first CSU politician to hold it. A special committee, the Federal Convention, with 1,260 members, will vote on January 30, 2027, and the CDU/CSU and SPD together command a majority of roughly 50 seats.

Merz praised Aigner as a president with dignity and with heart who could bring people together, while Aigner said she was humbled by the broad support and wanted to be the candidate of the strong center. DW noted that her election would also likely shut out the chancellor ambitions of Bavaria's state premier, Markus Söder.
Steinmeier's second five-year term ends next March, and the convention's vote on January 30 will choose his successor, with Aigner's prospects considered strong barring unexpected developments.

issues.title: US Experts: Trump May See OPCON Transfer as a Way to Cut Troops in Korea
issues.gist: US experts said President Trump may see the transfer of wartime command to South Korea as a way to pull American troops out. They spoke at a think tank event in Washington on Friday.
issues.gistKo: 미국 전문가들은 트럼프 대통령이 전시작전통제권 전환을 주한미군을 줄이는 길로 볼 수 있다고 말했어요. 금요일 워싱턴의 한 연구소 행사에서 나온 말이에요.
issues.easyKo: 전시에 군대를 누가 지휘하느냐를 한국으로 넘기는 일을 두고 전문가들이 말했어요. 미국 대통령이 이를 주한미군을 줄이는 방법으로 생각할 수 있다는 이야기예요.

paragraphs.en: On Friday, US experts said President Donald Trump seems to see a planned transfer of wartime operational control, or OPCON, to South Korea as a way to withdraw American troops. The remarks came from Victor Cha, the Korea chair at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, during an online talk on the state of the South Korea-US alliance. The think tank is based in Washington. Cha told the audience that, by many credible accounts, Trump sees the handover as a way to pull American forces off the peninsula.
paragraphs.ko: 금요일 미국 전문가들은 트럼프 대통령이 전시작전통제권(전작권)을 한국에 넘기는 계획을 미군 철수의 한 방법으로 보는 듯하다고 말했어요. 전략국제문제연구소(CSIS)의 한국 석좌 빅터 차는 한미 동맹에 관한 온라인 토론에서 이렇게 말했어요. 이 연구소는 워싱턴에 있어요. 차는 트럼프가 전환을 한반도에서 병력을 빼는 방법으로 본다는 말이 아주 믿을 만하게 전해진다고 했어요.

sents.en: On Friday, US experts said President Donald Trump seems to see a planned transfer of wartime operational control, or OPCON, to South Korea as a way to withdraw American troops.
sents.ko: 금요일 미국 전문가들은 트럼프 대통령이 전시작전통제권(전작권)을 한국에 넘기는 계획을 미군 철수의 한 방법으로 보는 듯하다고 말했어요.

sents.en: The remarks came from Victor Cha, the Korea chair at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, during an online talk on the state of the South Korea-US alliance.

sents.en: The think tank is based in Washington.

sents.ko: 차는 트럼프가 전환을 한반도에서 병력을 빼는 방법으로 본다는 말이 아주 믿을 만하게 전해진다고 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Cha noted that the president is the commander in chief. He said that even if Congress used the National Defense Authorization Act to set a floor for American troop levels in South Korea, Trump could still find ways to cut them. Cha said South Korea should have no illusions about how the US president thinks.

paragraphs.en: Randall Schriver, a former assistant secretary of defense, agreed, saying Trump has long wanted a smaller US military footprint in South Korea. He hoped any move toward the transfer would leave enough time for talks among the Pentagon, military leaders and Congress. Vincent Brooks, a former commander of US Forces Korea, said the transfer should happen only after both allies meet agreed conditions, not just through a political decision. He compared it to a college student who says he could graduate today without taking the required courses or passing the final exam.

paragraphs.en: Brooks said he felt let down that South Korea's Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul had endorsed a view that Seoul could defend itself without much trouble. pro.en: U.S. experts assessed Friday that President Donald Trump appears to regard the envisioned handover of wartime operational control (OPCON) to South Korea as a potential avenue for withdrawing American forces from the peninsula. Victor Cha, holder of the Korea chair at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, made the case during an online discussion on the state of the alliance hosted by the Washington-based think tank, saying it has been said very credibly that Trump views the transition as a means of pulling forces off the peninsula.

Cha stressed that the president is commander in chief and has latitude to act; even if Congress were to set a minimum troop level in South Korea through the National Defense Authorization Act, he said, Trump could still find ways to shrink the American presence. Seoul, Cha cautioned, should harbor no illusions about how the U.S. president thinks.

Randall Schriver, a former assistant secretary of defense, echoed that reading, noting Trump has long sought to reduce the U.S. military footprint in South Korea, and hoped any move toward a transfer would allow ample time for deliberation among the Pentagon, military leaders and Congress. Vincent Brooks, a former commander of U.S. Forces Korea, argued the handover should proceed only once both allies satisfy mutually agreed conditions rather than by political fiat, likening it to a college student claiming he could graduate immediately without completing the coursework or passing the final exam.

Brooks voiced disappointment that South Korean Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul had endorsed an assessment that Seoul could defend itself without major difficulty even if wartime OPCON were returned immediately. Kang, then a nominee, wrote as much in September in response to a parliamentary inquiry, concurring with then-Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back, while stressing that mutual trust in the alliance must be guaranteed. How the allies settle on conditions, and how Congress responds, will shape what follows.

It made the comment in the November edition of its monthly economic report, known as the Green Book. pro.en: South Korea's economy continues to "grow at a solid pace," the finance ministry said Friday in the November edition of its monthly Green Book, signaling a more upbeat reading after months of describing conditions as a "recovery." The ministry adopted the latter term in November 2025 and kept it through October, apart from April.

The ministry credited a substantial increase in exports and accelerating investment growth, with consumption improving gradually. Exports surged 93.7 percent on-year in October to a record $115.3 billion, driven largely by semiconductor shipments, while employment rose by 139,000 from a year earlier, with job growth above the 100,000 mark for a fourth consecutive month.

The ministry cautioned that lingering uncertainties from the Middle East war, inflationary pressure from high oil prices and difficult employment conditions for vulnerable groups could weigh on livelihoods. Consumer prices rose 2.8 percent in October, easing from 2.9 percent in September and 3.1 percent in August, but petroleum product prices climbed 14.9 percent and contributed 0.56 percentage point to inflation. It also cited uncertainty over the direction of AI industry policies as a global risk.

Labor-market gains were uneven: the employment rate for those aged 15 to 29 fell 1.7 percentage points on-year to 42.9 percent, a 30th consecutive monthly decline, and the number of employed people in that bracket fell by 196,000, a 48th straight monthly drop. The ministry pledged to accelerate efforts to broaden the foundations for growth while strengthening policies to stabilize livelihoods and reduce disparities.

pro.en: South Korea's largest festival of traditional alcoholic beverages opened Friday in Seoul with a record 142 producers, up from 120 a year earlier, at the aT Center in Yangjae. The three-day event, now in its 16th year, is expected by the Agriculture Ministry to draw about 30,000 visitors, compared with 28,000 last year.

Attendees can brew makgeolli, a milky rice wine, sample cocktails built on traditional spirits, consult an artificial intelligence sommelier that recommends drinks based on personal taste, and join a blind tasting of this year's presidential award winner. The ministry presented prizes to 18 drinks, with Blue Wine Company of Yeongdong taking the top honor for a fruit wine.

The government is seeking to convert growing global appetite for Korean cuisine into export sales of rice wine, fruit wine and distilled liquor. Agriculture Minister Song Mi-ryung pledged help with sourcing quality ingredients and finding overseas distributors, and the ministry singled out Kooksoondang, whose makgeolli exports totaled $46.15 million over the past five years.

Douglas Passos, a 29-year-old visitor from Mexico, took part in a makgeolli workshop and learned how rice ferments with nuruk, a traditional starter, and said he wanted to introduce the drink to friends when he returned home.

views.view: The festival shows how the government wants Korean food's popularity to lift overseas sales of traditional drinks.

pro.en: Samsung Medison, the medical device arm of Samsung Electronics, formally opened a new manufacturing building at its Hongcheon complex in Gangwon Province on Friday, the largest expansion of its production base since it joined the Samsung group in 2011. The company is investing 50 billion won, about $37.4 million, in a bid to join the world's top three ultrasound equipment makers.

The two-story, 14,548-square-meter structure consolidates processes once scattered across several buildings, linking circuit board production, assembly, testing, packaging and finished-goods storage in a single flow. The company aims to lift annual ultrasound output from roughly 24,000 units this year to as many as 40,000 by 2030, although its existing equipment can already sustain about 27,000 to 28,000 units.

Automation is central to the overhaul. Surface-mount machines place components as small as 0.1 to 0.2 millimeters on boards, with each scanner containing 15,000 to 20,000 parts; boards undergo 48 hours of testing at 40 degrees Celsius, and assembled units a further 24 hours. Son Hyun-soo, who heads the manufacturing team, said humans err while machines do not, though experienced technicians still assemble each unit by hand in about 30 minutes.

The expansion follows several years of strong growth. Revenue climbed 16.2 percent last year, well ahead of the 3.7 percent growth in the global ultrasound market, and has nearly tripled since the 2011 acquisition, with another double-digit increase expected in 2026. The Hongcheon plant ships premium systems to more than 110 territories, with higher-end models accounting for 30 to 40 percent of output.

Chief executive Yoo Kyu-tae described the project as a strategic investment to meet rising global demand, saying the company was within reach of breaking into the top three. Additional equipment, robots and uncrewed transport systems are to be installed in stages as volumes rise, while the company also broadens its AI-powered diagnostic software.

talk.answer: Samsung Medison uses machines to test every board for long hours, because mistakes can be costly. Skilled workers still build each scanner by hand. I think automation works best for repeated checks, while people are better for careful assembly.

issues.title: Go champion Shin Jin-seo beats AI engine KataGo 2-1 with a handicap
issues.gist: Shin Jin-seo, the world's top Go player, won a three-game series against KataGo 2-1. It was the first official series win for a human under this handicap format.
issues.gistKo: 세계 1위 바둑 기사 신진서가 카타고와의 3국 대결에서 2대 1로 이겼어요. 이 접바둑 방식에서 사람이 공식 시리즈를 이긴 첫 사례예요.

talk.answer: I think yes. Commentator Park Jung-sang said humans have kept learning by training with AI for ten years. Shin also won a series with a handicap, so AI is strong but people can still improve.

paragraphs.en: Shin Jin-seo, the world's top-ranked Go player, beat the AI engine KataGo in a three-game series in July. He won the series 2-1 in Seoul. It was the first time a human won an official match against the AI under the tournament's handicap format. Shin lost the first game, then won the second and the deciding third game.

sents.en: Shin Jin-seo, the world's top-ranked Go player, beat the AI engine KataGo in a three-game series in July.

sents.en: It was the first time a human won an official match against the AI under the tournament's handicap format.
sents.ko: 이 대회의 접바둑 방식으로 사람이 공식 대국에서 AI를 이긴 것은 처음이었어요.

sents.en: Shin lost the first game, then won the second and the deciding third game.
sents.ko: 신진서는 1국을 지고, 2국과 결정적인 3국을 이겼어요.

paragraphs.en: Shin played with a two-stone handicap, which means two stones were already on the board. The handicap gave him an estimated 99 percent chance of winning at the start. Even so, KataGo had dominated practice games against professionals who received two stones. In Game 1, KataGo fought back in the middle of the game, and Shin resigned after 245 moves.
paragraphs.ko: 신진서는 두 점 접바둑으로 뒀어요. 바둑판에 돌 두 개가 미리 놓인다는 뜻이에요. 이 접바둑으로 시작할 때 이길 확률이 약 99퍼센트로 계산됐어요. 그래도 카타고는 두 점을 받은 프로 기사들과의 연습 대국을 휩쓸어 왔어요. 1국에서 카타고가 중반 싸움에서 반격했고 신진서는 245수 만에 돌을 던졌어요.

sents.en: In Game 1, KataGo fought back in the middle of the game, and Shin resigned after 245 moves.

paragraphs.en: Game 2 was a long fight of 299 moves. Shin's winning chance briefly fell to 89 percent, but he found a narrow path and won by four and a half points. In Game 3, he won by 11.5 points after 221 moves. AI analysis said his chances never dropped below 95 percent in the last game.

sents.en: Game 2 was a long fight of 299 moves.
sents.ko: 2국은 299수까지 이어진 긴 싸움이었어요.

sents.en: Shin's winning chance briefly fell to 89 percent, but he found a narrow path and won by four and a half points.
sents.ko: 신진서의 승률이 잠시 89퍼센트까지 떨어졌지만 좁은 길을 찾아 4집 반으로 이겼어요.

Shin was modest and said his win does not compare with Lee's one victory. He also said he still cannot say he can beat KataGo with a two-stone handicap every time.
paragraphs.ko: 이 대국은 이세돌과 구글 딥마인드 알파고 대국 10주년을 기념한 것이었어요. 이세돌은 2016년 맞바둑으로 알파고와 두어 4대 1로 졌어요. 신진서는 자신의 승리가 이세돌의 한 판 승리와 비교되지 않는다고 겸손하게 말했어요. 또 두 점 접바둑으로 카타고를 늘 이길 수 있다고는 아직 말할 수 없다고 했어요.

sents.en: The match marked the 10th anniversary of Lee Se-dol's games against Google DeepMind's AlphaGo.
sents.ko: 이 대국은 이세돌과 구글 딥마인드 알파고 대국 10주년을 기념한 것이었어요.

sents.en: Lee faced AlphaGo on even terms in 2016 and lost the series 4-1.
sents.ko: 이세돌은 2016년 맞바둑으로 알파고와 두어 4대 1로 졌어요.

sents.en: Shin was modest and said his win does not compare with Lee's one victory.
sents.ko: 신진서는 자신의 승리가 이세돌의 한 판 승리와 비교되지 않는다고 겸손하게 말했어요.

sents.en: He also said he still cannot say he can beat KataGo with a two-stone handicap every time.
sents.ko: 또 두 점 접바둑으로 카타고를 늘 이길 수 있다고는 아직 말할 수 없다고 했어요.

paragraphs.en: Shin said that AI seems too perfect, because even when it is behind, it does not take desperate risks. He said the beauty of human Go is that players can make bold or unexpected moves. Commentator Park Jung-sang said humans have kept learning by training with AI for ten years. For students, it is a reminder that AI can be a training partner as well as a rival. Whether the handicap changes in a future rematch is still unclear.
paragraphs.ko: 신진서는 AI가 너무 완벽해 보인다고 했어요. 뒤져 있어도 필사적인 모험을 하지 않기 때문이에요. 사람 바둑의 아름다움은 대담하거나 뜻밖의 수를 둘 수 있는 데 있다고 했어요. 해설자 박정상 9단은 사람들이 10년 동안 AI와 연습하며 계속 배워 왔다고 말했어요. 학생에게는 AI가 경쟁자이자 연습 상대도 될 수 있다는 점을 떠올리게 해요. 다음 재대결에서 접바둑이 바뀔지는 아직 알 수 없어요.

sents.ko: 신진서는 AI가 너무 완벽해 보인다고 했어요. 뒤져 있어도 필사적인 모험을 하지 않기 때문이에요.

sents.en: He said the beauty of human Go is that players can make bold or unexpected moves.
sents.ko: 사람 바둑의 아름다움은 대담하거나 뜻밖의 수를 둘 수 있는 데 있다고 했어요.

sents.en: Commentator Park Jung-sang said humans have kept learning by training with AI for ten years.

sents.en: For students, it is a reminder that AI can be a training partner as well as a rival.
sents.ko: 학생에게는 AI가 경쟁자이자 연습 상대도 될 수 있다는 점을 떠올리게 해요.

sents.en: Whether the handicap changes in a future rematch is still unclear.
sents.ko: 다음 재대결에서 접바둑이 바뀔지는 아직 알 수 없어요.

pro.en: Shin Jin-seo, the world's top-ranked Go player, defeated the AI engine KataGo 2-1 in a three-game series in Seoul in July, becoming the first human to win an official match against the program under the tournament's handicap format. He lost the opener before taking the second game and the decisive third.

Shin played with a two-stone handicap, which gave him an estimated 99 percent chance of winning at the outset, yet KataGo had dominated practice games against professionals receiving two stones. In Game 1, the engine seized the initiative in a midgame fight and Shin resigned after 245 moves.

Game 2 stretched to 299 moves, with Shin's winning probability dipping briefly to 89 percent before he found a narrow route through the complications and prevailed by four and a half points. In the decider he won by 11.5 points after 221 moves, and AI analysis put his chances above 95 percent throughout.

The event marked the 10th anniversary of Lee Se-dol's series against Google DeepMind's AlphaGo, which he lost 4-1 on even terms in 2016. Shin was measured, saying his result does not compare with Lee's lone victory and that he still cannot say he could beat KataGo consistently with a two-stone handicap.

Shin said AI seems too perfect, since it takes no desperate risks even when behind, whereas human Go allows bold or unexpected moves. Commentator Park Jung-sang said humans have continued to evolve by training with AI over the past decade. Whether the handicap will be adjusted in any rematch remains an open question.

issues.title: Could AI Help Decide Medals at the 2028 Olympics?
issues.gist: Gymnastics used an AI judging tool at the recent World Championships, and its bosses expect it at the 2028 Olympics. Some gymnasts say it made unfair cuts to their scores.
issues.gistKo: 체조는 최근 세계선수권에서 AI 심판 보조 시스템을 썼고, 협회 관계자들은 2028 올림픽에서도 쓸 것으로 봐요. 일부 선수들은 점수가 부당하게 깎였다고 말해요.
issues.easyKo: 체조 경기에서 AI가 선수 몸의 각도를 재서 심판을 도와요. 협회는 공정하다고 하지만, 선수들은 사람이 아니라 로봇처럼 평가받는 것 같다고 말해요.

paragraphs.en: Gymnastics is leading the way in using artificial intelligence to help judge elite sport. Its leaders told the BBC they would be highly surprised if AI-assisted judging were not used at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. The tool was used at the recent World Championships in Rotterdam.
paragraphs.ko: 체조는 최상위 스포츠 심판에 인공지능을 쓰는 일에서 앞서가고 있어요. 체조 지도부는 BBC에 2028년 로스앤젤레스 올림픽에서 AI 보조 심판이 쓰이지 않는다면 매우 놀랄 것이라고 말했어요. 이 도구는 최근 로테르담 세계선수권에서 쓰였어요.

sents.en: Gymnastics is leading the way in using artificial intelligence to help judge elite sport.
sents.ko: 체조는 최상위 스포츠 심판에 인공지능을 쓰는 일에서 앞서가고 있어요.

sents.en: Its leaders told the BBC they would be highly surprised if AI-assisted judging were not used at the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.
sents.ko: 체조 지도부는 BBC에 2028년 로스앤젤레스 올림픽에서 AI 보조 심판이 쓰이지 않는다면 매우 놀랄 것이라고 말했어요.

sents.en: The tool was used at the recent World Championships in Rotterdam.
sents.ko: 이 도구는 최근 로테르담 세계선수권에서 쓰였어요.

paragraphs.en: The system is called the Judging Support System, and the company Fujitsu has been developing it since 2017. It uses motion analysis to recognise gymnastic elements, and more than 800 elements have been programmed into it. Judges can also watch multi-angle video and see numbers about body angles.
paragraphs.ko: 이 시스템은 심판 지원 시스템(JSS)이라고 하며, 후지쓰가 2017년부터 개발해 왔어요. 동작 분석으로 체조 기술을 알아보며, 800개가 넘는 기술이 입력돼 있어요. 심판은 여러 각도의 영상과 몸 각도에 대한 수치도 볼 수 있어요.

sents.en: The system is called the Judging Support System, and the company Fujitsu has been developing it since 2017.
sents.ko: 이 시스템은 심판 지원 시스템(JSS)이라고 하며, 후지쓰가 2017년부터 개발해 왔어요.

sents.en: It uses motion analysis to recognise gymnastic elements, and more than 800 elements have been programmed into it.
sents.ko: 동작 분석으로 체조 기술을 알아보며, 800개가 넘는 기술이 입력돼 있어요.

sents.en: Judges can also watch multi-angle video and see numbers about body angles.
sents.ko: 심판은 여러 각도의 영상과 몸 각도에 대한 수치도 볼 수 있어요.

paragraphs.en: But some athletes were unhappy. Olympic champion Carlos Yulo and British gymnast Harry Hepworth both did a piked vault, and the difficulty score of each was cut from 5.6 to 5.2. Hepworth said the system saw a tuck position when he bent his legs to prepare for landing, and he said it cost him places in the final. Yulo said, "I'm not a robot," and Hepworth called the tool potentially dangerous because athletes might try straighter legs.
paragraphs.ko: 하지만 일부 선수들은 불만이었어요. 올림픽 챔피언 카를로스 율로와 영국의 해리 헵워스는 둘 다 몸을 굽힌 도마를 했는데, 난도 점수가 각각 5.6에서 5.2로 깎였어요. 헵워스는 착지를 준비하려고 다리를 굽혔더니 시스템이 이를 웅크린 자세로 봤다며, 결선 순위에서 손해를 봤다고 말했어요. 율로는 “나는 로봇이 아니다”라고 했고, 헵워스는 선수들이 다리를 더 곧게 펴려다 위험해질 수 있다고 했어요.

sents.en: Olympic champion Carlos Yulo and British gymnast Harry Hepworth both did a piked vault, and the difficulty score of each was cut from 5.6 to 5.2.

sents.en: Yulo said, "I'm not a robot," and Hepworth called the tool potentially dangerous because athletes might try straighter legs.

paragraphs.en: Andrew Tombs, a gymnastics technical committee president, said the AI guarantees fairness and the decisions were correct based on the system. pro.en: Gymnastics is at the vanguard of applying artificial intelligence to the judging of elite sport, and its officials said they would be "highly surprised" if AI-assisted scoring were not adopted at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, having deployed it at the recent World Championships in Rotterdam.

The Judging Support System, which Fujitsu has been developing since 2017, draws on motion analysis to identify gymnastic elements, with more than 800 elements programmed into it, and gives judges replays from several camera angles together with measured figures on how gymnasts position their bodies.

The rollout drew criticism from competitors. Olympic champion Carlos Yulo and Britain's Harry Hepworth each had the difficulty rating of a piked vault reduced from 5.6 to 5.2 in qualifying. Hepworth said the system read the bending of his legs in preparation for landing as a tuck and that the downgrade cost him places in the final, while Yulo protested that he was not a robot, and Hepworth warned that straightening the legs could prove dangerous.

Andrew Tombs, president of the men's artistic technical committee, maintained that the technology guarantees fairness and that the rulings were correct given the parameters in the system, adding that judges would have downgraded the vaults regardless. He acknowledged, though, that discussions with coaches were under way on the precise moment at which the leg measurement should be taken, and Hepworth conceded that a refined version could be a brilliant tool.

Other judged disciplines are also exploring the technology: aerials skiing will test algorithms alongside human judges this season, and equestrian authorities will trial AI in dressage World Cups, although they insist humans will retain a role because the technology cannot assess the harmony between horse and rider.

views.view: Gymnastics bosses back AI judging for fairness, while some gymnasts say it is wrong and even dangerous.
Hepworth says the tool misread his vault and cost him places, though it could be brilliant if refined.

pro.en: An investigation by Times Higher Education, relayed by Inside Higher Ed on Nov. 13, found that obscure journals had published AI-generated papers under the names of academics who never wrote them. Alan Said, a computer science professor at the University of Gothenburg, received a Google Scholar alert about a paper bearing his name; he had not written it and judged it hollow and machine-made.

Said reported the article to the journal's domain registrar, which said it had been removed, yet the paper remained online under a different author's name and, two days later, under yet another, leaving three versions in circulation. He then identified two affiliated journals with similar graphics, the same editor in chief and overlapping editorial boards.

All three outlets bill themselves as peer-reviewed, open-access and multidisciplinary, though their domains were registered in 2026 even as their sites display archives purportedly years old. One reportedly carried dozens of papers attributed to prominent figures including Stanford's Fei-Fei Li and Christopher Manning and Berkeley's Michael I. Jordan and Stuart Russell. The same editor in chief, Denish Brown, is listed across the journals, whose reported fees range from $10 to $200.

Jure Leskovec of Stanford confirmed that he neither wrote the paper nor authorized the use of his name, learning of it only through THE's email, while Kanakaraju Manupati, a postdoctoral researcher at Virginia Commonwealth University, said he never agreed to sit on a board. THE's inquiries to the journals went unanswered before publication, and Said voiced concern that a new doctoral student seeing his name there might consider submitting work.

The episode underscores how researchers' identities can be misappropriated and how predatory outlets may mislead early-career scholars. Readers and citers would do well to scrutinize a journal's editorial roster and domain history, and attention now turns to whether the journals respond and how the named academics react.

pro.en: Physicists at Brookhaven National Laboratory, working with colleagues at Columbia University and the University of Colorado Boulder, have developed an AI model capable of disentangling particle jets from the background clutter in simulated heavy-ion collisions, according to a study published in Scientific Reports.

Such collisions produce quark-gluon plasma, a superheated medium whose fluctuating debris can swamp the jets researchers seek to characterize; the new approach is unpaired and unsupervised, dispensing with human-labeled or matched training pairs, and instead trains on simulated pure background drawn from the plasma alongside idealized jet simulations.

Evaluated on simulated sPHENIX calorimeter data, the model reconstructed jet positions, energies and internal structure with greater fidelity than conventional background-subtraction techniques, with the edge most pronounced for larger jets, where background fluctuations are most severe, according to Brookhaven physicist Yeonju Go and computer scientist Dmitrii Torbunov.

The Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider wrapped up operations in early 2026, and sPHENIX amassed nearly 300 petabytes across the machine's final three runs; the team intends to apply the model to that experimental data and anticipates possible uses at the Electron-Ion Collider or the Large Hadron Collider, though validation beyond simulation remains outstanding.

views.view: The new AI method reconstructs jets more accurately than conventional methods, though real-data tests are still pending.

issues.title: Germany and Hockey Nations Push Back After Court Says Russia Can Return
issues.gist: A sports court ruled that Russia must be allowed back into world ice hockey tournaments. Several top hockey nations now say they will refuse to play Russia, and Germany says hosting its May championship could become impossible.
issues.gistKo: 스포츠 재판소가 러시아를 세계 아이스하키 대회에 다시 받아들이라고 판결했어요. 여러 강국이 러시아와 경기하지 않겠다고 하고, 독일은 5월 대회 개최가 어려워질 수 있다고 해요.
issues.easyKo: 스포츠 재판소가 러시아 팀의 복귀를 허용하라고 하자 핀란드, 스웨덴, 체코 같은 나라들이 반발하고 있어요. 5월에 대회를 열기로 한 독일도 개최를 못 할 수 있다고 걱정해요.

paragraphs.en: A big fight is growing in world ice hockey. On October 30, the Court of Arbitration for Sport, known as CAS, ruled that the International Ice Hockey Federation must let Russia return to its tournaments. The ruling covers the 2026-2027 season. Russia last played at the men's world championship in December 2021.
paragraphs.ko: 세계 아이스하키에서 큰 다툼이 커지고 있어요. 10월 30일 스포츠중재재판소(CAS)는 국제아이스하키연맹이 러시아의 대회 복귀를 허용해야 한다고 판결했어요. 이 판결은 2026-2027 시즌에 해당해요. 러시아가 마지막으로 남자 세계선수권에 나온 것은 2021년 12월이에요.

paragraphs.en: Since then, several leading hockey nations have pushed back. Finland, Sweden and Czechia say they will not play against Russia in any tournament where it can take part. Several key sponsors have also threatened to leave if the Russians return. The IIHF Council met for three days but had not reached a shared answer by Friday.
paragraphs.ko: 그 뒤 여러 아이스하키 강국이 반발했어요. 핀란드, 스웨덴, 체코는 러시아가 나올 수 있는 어떤 대회에서도 러시아와 경기하지 않겠다고 해요. 주요 후원사 여러 곳도 러시아가 돌아오면 떠나겠다고 위협했어요. 국제아이스하키연맹 이사회는 사흘 동안 모였지만 금요일까지 같은 답을 내지 못했어요.

paragraphs.en: The first event to be hit is the Men's World Juniors, which opens in Canada on December 26. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said that Russian players will not be there while the war in Ukraine goes on. Russian President Vladimir Putin said that countries opposing Russia's return are violating the rights of its athletes.
paragraphs.ko: 가장 먼저 영향을 받는 대회는 12월 26일 캐나다에서 열리는 남자 세계주니어선수권이에요. 마크 카니 캐나다 총리는 우크라이나 전쟁이 이어지는 동안 러시아 선수들은 오지 못한다고 말했어요. 블라디미르 푸틴 러시아 대통령은 러시아의 복귀에 반대하는 나라들이 자국 선수들의 권리를 침해한다고 말했어요.

paragraphs.en: Germany is also in a hard spot because it plans to host the Men's World Championship in May. The games are planned for Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf. Government spokesman Stefan Kornelius said Russian participation would make hosting practically impossible, both in sport and in money. A Foreign Ministry spokesman said visas for a Russian team would be difficult under current restrictions. The head of the German federation said Germany may have to consider giving up its role as host.

sents.en: But under the CAS decision, Russia must be included in the 2027 tournament in Quebec City.

sents.en: Germany says it still hopes for a diplomatic solution so the May event can go ahead as planned.
sents.ko: 독일은 5월 대회가 계획대로 열릴 수 있도록 여전히 외교적 해법을 바란다고 말해요.

pro.en: A dispute that could reshape international ice hockey deepened after the Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled on Oct. 30 that the International Ice Hockey Federation must readmit Russia to its competitions for the 2026-27 season; Russia last featured at the men's world championship in December 2021.

Finland, Sweden and Czechia have since signaled that they will refrain from playing Russia in any tournament in which it is permitted to compete, several key sponsors have warned they could withdraw, and the IIHF Council, after three days of talks, had evidently failed to forge a consensus by Friday.

The Men's World Juniors, opening in Canada on Dec. 26, would be the first event affected, but Prime Minister Mark Carney categorically ruled out Russian participation for as long as the war in Ukraine continues, while President Vladimir Putin accused the countries opposing Moscow's return of violating the rights of its athletes.

Germany, slated to stage the men's world championship in Gelsenkirchen, Mannheim and Düsseldorf in May, finds itself in a bind: government spokesman Stefan Kornelius called Russian participation a development that would render hosting practically impossible from both a sporting and an economic standpoint, a Foreign Ministry spokesman suggested that issuing visas to a Russian team would be difficult under existing restrictions, and the head of the German federation conceded that withdrawal as host might have to be weighed.

The Women's World Championship, under way in Denmark from Nov. 6 to 16, lies outside the ruling, though the CAS decision would oblige the IIHF to include Russia at the 2027 event in Quebec City, and Berlin says it continues to seek a diplomatic solution that would allow the May tournament to proceed as scheduled.

views.view: German officials say that if Russia returns, boycotts would make the May championship practically impossible to host.
The CAS ruling does not touch the women's tournament in Denmark, but it would require Russia at the 2027 event in Quebec City.

pro.en: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's principal stadium on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, ending roughly two years of gang occupation of the Sylvio Cator Stadium in Port-au-Prince. The Haitian National Police said it had seized full control of the venue together with the Task Force, a private security group working for the government, before Salvadoran soldiers assumed responsibility for security there.

The operation forms part of a deployment of some 2,000 soldiers ordered by Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele, who dispatched them to rescue four Salvadoran troops reported missing after an ambush on Oct. 18. Bukele said last Tuesday that his forces had destroyed the headquarters of 400 Mawozo, one of Haiti's main gangs, while the four missing soldiers belong to the Gang Suppression Force, a UN-backed multinational group that has distanced itself from the rescue mission.

Bukele said the forces would establish an operational base in the stadium from which to push into gang-held areas, and he urged gang members to leave before the offensive begins. The Haitian Times said it could not independently verify the extent of the territory secured, and Bukele, who has drawn attention for bringing Salvadoran gangs to heel, has also faced accusations of human rights abuses.

The 10,000-capacity venue matters for sport: its seizure by gangs in 2024 forced Haiti's national football team to play its World Cup qualifiers in Curacao rather than at home. Haiti, the poorest country in Latin America and the Caribbean, remains largely under the sway of armed groups, and observers will watch whether the stadium becomes a secure base and whether the offensive into gang territory begins.

pro.en: A 17-year-old boy with autism was found alive Thursday after spending six days lost in woodland in eastern Australia, police said, identifying him only as William. He vanished last Friday near Walhalla, a former gold-mining town roughly 185 kilometers east of Melbourne, after setting out on a camping trip with a teenage friend.

William had walked a short distance from the campsite to fetch more equipment but never returned to his friend, according to police. He trekked for days across very steep terrain and spent his final two days stranded beside a creek about 2 kilometers from the camp, hemmed in by the topography.

More than 100 emergency services personnel and volunteers took part in the search. A police helicopter crew spotted William asleep on a flat rock beside the creek; officials said he awoke to the sound of the aircraft, gave a thumbs-up and was winched to safety. The weather in the region had been mild, with little rain.

Police said William was in good spirits and, for the most part, in good health, and he was taken to a hospital for monitoring. His mother, Elizabeth, said she was over the moon and joked that he is grounded for life.

issues.title: Billy Evans Speaks Out on Elizabeth Holmes Documentary
issues.gist: Billy Evans, the partner of Elizabeth Holmes, gave his first TV interview about the documentary "You Can See Everything." He says he loves the film even though it makes him look "crazy."
issues.gistKo: 엘리자베스 홈스의 동반자 빌리 에번스가 다큐멘터리 「유 캔 시 에브리싱」에 대해 첫 TV 인터뷰를 했어요. 자신이 "제정신이 아닌" 사람처럼 보여도 영화는 좋아한다고 말했어요.
issues.easyKo: 테라노스 사기로 복역 중인 홈스를 다룬 다큐가 큰 인기를 끌고 있어요. 곁에 있던 에번스는 자신의 묘사가 마음에 안 들지만, 홈스의 모습은 정확하다고 말했어요.

views.view: Evans says he loves the film and that it shows Holmes accurately, but he says it makes him look crazy and he could not control the edit.

why: The film became a hit and shows how people judge a story's characters through editing.
It also keeps the Theranos fraud case in the public eye.
lines.agree: Everyone agrees the film is a huge hit and that Holmes is serving a 10-year prison sentence.
lines.life: When you watch a documentary or read a news story, ask who chose and edited what you see.
lines.next: Watch the full interview on CBS Sunday Morning this weekend and the talk about an Oscar nomination.

pro.en: Billy Evans, who has been with Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes for years, has given his first television interview since the release of "You Can See Everything," the runaway documentary in which he features prominently. The film traces the couple through the final weeks before Holmes entered prison, and the complete interview is scheduled for "CBS Sunday Morning" this weekend.

Holmes once asserted that her company's technology could carry out an array of diagnostic tests on a single drop of blood, a claim later judged fraudulent. She is now serving a 10-year term in federal prison for wire fraud and conspiracy, and she continues to profess her innocence.

In a clip released ahead of the broadcast, Evans said he adores the three-hour film even as he acknowledges that it makes him seem "crazy." Audiences have dwelt on scenes in which he appears domineering, and the documentary discloses that he holds power of attorney over Holmes during her sentence; Evans maintained that he had no control over the edit and dismissed the film as entertainment.

Evans objects to how he is depicted but considers the portrait of Holmes faithful. The documentary has taken in more than $80 million worldwide, and talk has begun that it might become the first documentary nominated for best picture at the Academy Awards, a run that illustrates how differently one person can look depending on who shapes the narrative.

issues.title: When should old, bad science be pulled from the record?
issues.gist: Old science papers with fake or wrong results are rarely retracted. AI tools can now bring them back to new readers.
issues.gistKo: 가짜이거나 틀린 옛 논문은 거의 철회되지 않아요. 그런데 이제 AI 도구가 그 논문을 새 독자에게 다시 보여 줄 수 있어요.
issues.easyKo: 오래된 가짜·오류 논문을 언제 철회할지 학계가 고민하고 있어요. AI 요약이 옛 오류를 되살릴 수 있기 때문이에요.

paragraphs.en: Science papers can be wrong, or even fake, and some of them are decades old. A Nature feature asks when such old papers should be retracted, which means officially withdrawn. The number of retractions has grown a lot, with more than 10,000 recorded in 2023 alone. Journals are also looking farther back in time to fix the record.
paragraphs.ko: 과학 논문은 틀리거나 심지어 가짜일 수 있고, 그중 일부는 수십 년 전 것이에요. 네이처의 기획 기사는 이런 오래된 논문을 언제 철회, 즉 공식적으로 거둬들여야 하는지 물어요. 철회 건수는 크게 늘어서 2023년 한 해에만 1만 건이 넘게 기록됐어요. 학술지들은 기록을 바로잡으려고 더 먼 과거까지 거슬러 올라가 살피고 있어요.

pro.en: Science's archives contain decades-old papers that are fraudulent, unethical or simply wrong, and a Nature feature examines when such work should be retracted. Retractions have surged, with more than 10,000 recorded in 2023 alone, and journals are increasingly reaching further back in time to correct the record.

The case of Vishwa Jit Gupta, an Indian palaeontologist accused of fraud in the 1980s, shows the stakes: more than 450 of his publications were riddled with problems, including maps of collection sites that did not exist. He died in 2022 and none of his papers has been retracted, so Google's AI overview can now direct searchers looking up Himalayan landmarks to his discredited work.

Retracting historical papers is fraught because authors may be dead, original records may be unavailable and journals may be out of print, while publishers' resources are finite. Chris Graf of Springer Nature said an expression of concern is often the preferred mechanism when information is limited, and Nature's analysis found just 358 retraction notices and 120 expressions of concern for papers more than 20 years old at the time of action.

Experts are divided on the right course. Nobel laureate Svante Pääbo acknowledges that his 1985 mummy DNA paper reflected contamination but argues it should stand because nobody is currently misled by it, whereas Elsevier scrubbed two 1984 papers on caesium cancer therapy entirely, a step that can be taken when contents pose a serious public health risk.

For students, the episode is a reminder to scrutinize a source's provenance and whether it remains trusted, since AI summaries can recycle old errors without warning. The next thing to watch is how publishers and bodies such as COPE decide which historical papers to flag.

pro.en: Cacti, long assumed to be hardy in arid conditions, could face a sharply elevated threat of extinction once intense drought is layered on top of rising temperatures, a Nature paper reports after assessing 993 species of Cactaceae, a plant family that already ranks among the most imperiled.

Working from 648,316 occurrence records, the team constructed species distribution models to map the climatically suitable range of each species. Whereas most such models draw only on long-term average conditions, the authors added fresh spatial data on severe drought, and in 91% of cases the drought-inclusive versions fitted the evidence better.

Projecting forward across several emissions pathways with dispersal capped at 100 km, the authors found that including severe drought lifted the proportion of species forecast to lose suitable climatic area from 58–61% to 69–72%; the proportion forecast to forfeit more than a quarter of that area climbed from 26–43% to 55–58%, and those forecast to forfeit over four-fifths from 1–15% to 25–35%.

Dispersal proved pivotal: when cacti were assumed unable to migrate at all rather than moving up to 100 km, the proportion losing suitable area under severe drought rose from 69–72% to 84–85%. The projected declines would thin out species counts in some regions, and five bioregions could see more than 25% of their species disappear.

The authors argue that factoring in climatic extremes, rather than averages alone, can shift how vulnerable biodiversity appears, and that building such extremes into ecological forecasts will be essential for gauging losses of wildlife and shaping conservation strategies.

views.view: Severe drought plus warming can raise the chance that many cactus species lose suitable climate area.

issues.title: Americans Welcome AI Help in Healthcare, With a Human Checking

paragraphs.en: A new Pew Research Center survey asked Americans how they feel about artificial intelligence in healthcare. Pew talked to 3,488 U.S. adults from June 22 to 28, 2026. People are open to AI for some tasks, especially office work like translating and scheduling. But they still want a human to check what AI does.
