pro.en: A new Pew Research Center survey of 3,488 U.S. adults, conducted June 22-28, 2026, finds that Americans are receptive to artificial intelligence in healthcare for certain tasks, particularly administrative ones, but still want a human in the loop reviewing what the technology does.

Roughly eight in 10 adults (78%) are open to AI translating for patients, with 52% preferring a final human review and 26% comfortable with AI acting alone. About half or more are open, with human review, to AI analyzing and explaining medical scans and lab results. Openness falls for higher-stakes calls: nearly half (46%) want AI to have no part in insurance claim decisions, and just 5% would let it make them unaided.

A majority (60%) are uncomfortable with AI in their own care for tasks such as diagnoses and treatment, double the 30% who say they are comfortable. Opinion on outcomes is divided, with 37% expecting better health outcomes, 36% worse and 26% little difference. Adults under 30 have grown more pessimistic, with 45% anticipating worse outcomes, up from 29% in 2022.

Privacy and the patient-doctor bond draw the most concern. Some 51% say AI will worsen the security of personal health information, against 8% who say it will improve it, and 47% say it will worsen the patient-doctor relationship, against 10% who say it will improve it. Views on access to care are somewhat brighter, with 31% expecting improvement and 20% expecting a decline.

Confidence in the institutions overseeing the technology is thin. For health insurers, the federal government, AI companies and state governments, half or more of Americans have little or no confidence they will steer AI toward patients' best interests, while 26% have a great deal or quite a bit of confidence in doctors. Pew's Galen Stocking told CBS News that people want to know when and how providers use AI, and 46% do not know whether AI has ever been used in their care. The question now is whether rules and clear disclosure can keep pace.

views.view: Americans are open to AI for office tasks, but most want humans to make or review the big medical decisions.
Patients like AI for scheduling and translating but want humans using the stethoscope.

heads.title: Expert Brief: Public Opinion on AI in Healthcare

why: AI is moving into hospitals and insurance faster than rules are written, so public trust matters.
lines.agree: Most people accept AI for simple office tasks if a human checks the work.
lines.split: People are split on whether AI will make patient health better or worse.
lines.life: You may meet AI tools in clinics and apps, so it helps to know which jobs people trust AI with.
lines.next: Watch whether rules and clear notices about AI use keep up with how fast it spreads.

issues.title: A Common Sugar May Help Ovarian Cancer Cells Spread
issues.gist: Scientists found that cancer cells that survive chemotherapy can release fructose, a common sugar. In lab tests, it helped nearby cancer cells break free and spread.
issues.gistKo: 과학자들이 항암 치료에서 살아남은 암세포가 흔한 당인 과당을 내보낼 수 있다고 밝혔어요. 실험에서 과당은 주변 암세포가 떨어져 나가 퍼지는 것을 도왔어요.
issues.easyKo: 난소암 세포가 항암 치료 뒤에 과당을 내보내 다른 암세포의 전이를 돕는다는 연구 결과가 나왔어요. 아직 사람에게 쓰기 전 단계의 연구라 사람에게서 확인된 것은 아니에요.

paragraphs.en: Scientists at The Wistar Institute found that a common sugar may help aggressive ovarian cancer spread. The sugar is fructose, and it can be released by cancer cells that survived chemotherapy. The study was published in Nature Aging. The team says fructose acts as a signal that tells nearby tumor cells to break free.
paragraphs.ko: 위스타 연구소 과학자들이 흔한 당이 공격적인 난소암의 전이를 도울 수 있다는 것을 발견했어요. 그 당은 과당이고, 항암 치료에서 살아남은 암세포가 내보낼 수 있어요. 이 연구는 Nature Aging에 실렸어요. 연구팀은 과당이 주변 종양 세포에게 떨어져 나가라고 알리는 신호처럼 작용한다고 말해요.

paragraphs.en: Most patients with ovarian cancer get platinum-based chemotherapy. Many respond well at first, but the cancer comes back in most cases. The spread of cancer, called metastasis, causes approximately 90% of ovarian cancer deaths. Some cells that survive chemotherapy stop dividing, but they stay active and send out molecules. In a preclinical model, those molecules alone were enough to increase the spread of cancer.

pro.en: Researchers at The Wistar Institute have found that fructose released by ovarian cancer cells that survive chemotherapy can act as a signal prompting neighboring tumor cells to detach and spread, according to a study published in Nature Aging.

Most ovarian cancer patients receive platinum-based chemotherapy, and although many respond initially, the disease recurs in most cases. Metastasis accounts for approximately 90% of ovarian cancer deaths. Some cells that survive treatment cease dividing yet remain biologically active, releasing molecules that, in a preclinical model, were sufficient on their own to boost the spread of cancer.

Fructose occurs in fruit, honey, table sugar and high fructose corn syrup. The team found that cells surviving chemotherapy produce and secrete it, and that it suppresses cholesterol production in neighboring cancer cells. Because cholesterol helps hold cells together, lower levels loosen those bonds and let cells break away more readily. In preclinical experiments, high fructose intake comparable to that of sugary drinks also raised signals associated with spread, even without chemotherapy.

The cholesterol finding prompted questions about statins, which roughly 39 million people in the United States take. In the experiments, statins alone also weakened the connections between cancer cells. The researchers stress that this has not been demonstrated in patients and is not a reason to discontinue prescribed statins. They suspect that pancreatic, colon and liver cancers could behave similarly, but they cannot yet call the effect universal.

The findings remain preliminary. The study does not establish that eating sugar causes cancer to spread in humans, and no one has tested whether reducing fructose improves outcomes for ovarian cancer patients. The team is now designing experiments in other cancers, and the work could eventually point toward new strategies for preventing metastasis.

paragraphs.en: The International Atomic Energy Agency, or IAEA, has finished a safety review of a nuclear reactor in Busan, South Korea. pro.en: The International Atomic Energy Agency has urged a set of safety upgrades at Shin-Kori No. 2, a reactor in Busan about 330 kilometers southeast of Seoul, after an Operational Safety Review Team mission that lasted from Oct. 26 to Thursday and was carried out at the South Korean government's request.

Inspectors proposed that the plant look at tightening industrial safety rules, at how operational work is carried out and supervised, and at measures to keep radioactive contamination from spreading, and they underlined the need to pass operating information on accurately and use it properly.

Still, the agency credited the staff with professionalism and a firm drive for continual improvement, and it singled out strong practices such as a virtual training setup for field and control-room workers and an integrated disaster monitoring network that issues real-time alerts about outside hazards.

The reactor, a 1,000-megawatt pressurized water unit that entered commercial service in 2012, is run by Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power. The plant may correct factual points in a draft report it has already received, and the IAEA is due to deliver its final report to South Korea within three months.

views.view: The IAEA suggests several safety improvements but also praises the staff and names good practices.
The operator treats regular international reviews as a way to build public trust in nuclear plants.

pro.en: The remains of two Korean independence fighters interred in the United States and Uzbekistan will be repatriated next week, the veterans ministry said Friday, with Ho Si-han and Lee Gwal due to arrive Sunday in what would be the first return of an independence fighter buried in Uzbekistan.

A homecoming ceremony is set for Monday at a memorial park in Seoul, with roughly 300 people expected, after which the remains will be laid to rest at the national cemetery in the central city of Daejeon.

Ho, a Seoul native born in 1885, was seized by Japanese police while collecting military funds in the wake of the March 1 independence movement, and he took part in fundraising for the cause between 1927 and 1945 before dying in Los Angeles in 1956. Lee, born in North Hamgyong Province in 1898, was active in Korean organizations in Russia's Primorsky Krai in 1919 and served as a diplomatic delegate of the Korean Provisional Government, but he was deported to Uzbekistan in 1937 and died there.

The repatriation coincides with the 80th anniversary of an effort led by civilians and the government that began in 1946 with the return of three renowned independence fighters, including Yun Bong-gil.

To date, 158 sets of remains have come home from 14 countries, and the ministry, which has located 240 tombs of independence fighters in 10 countries including China, the United States and Kazakhstan, intends to repatriate more once it has consulted bereaved families.

views.view: The ministry says the return marks 80 years of efforts to bring home independence fighters buried overseas.

pro.en: South Korea and France opened the 27th session of their joint coordinating committee on nuclear energy in Saclay, in France, this week, with the gathering ending Friday local time, Seoul's Ministry of Science and ICT said.

The forum has been organized since 1982, following the 1981 bilateral accord on the peaceful use of nuclear energy, and it comes as the two nations mark the 140th anniversary of diplomatic relations this year.

Delegates reviewed 21 areas of technological cooperation spanning nuclear energy research, safety and industry, and agreed to broaden collaboration on next-generation reactors and the nuclear supply chain, building on memorandums of understanding signed at bilateral summits in April and September.

The ministry said it would use the committee to further reinforce the cooperative framework between the two countries. For engineering students in Korea, the meeting underscores how nuclear technology is advanced through international partnership, and the progress of new reactor projects is the next thing to watch.

views.view: Korea's science ministry said the committee helps strengthen the cooperation framework with France and bring new progress in nuclear work.

pro.en: South Korea will face North Korea, China and the Philippines in the final Asian qualifying tournament for the 2028 Olympic women's football competition next spring, after the Asian Football Confederation drew the groups on Thursday at its headquarters in Kuala Lumpur. The top two finishers in each group will advance directly to the Olympics, while the two runners-up will contest a two-legged playoff in February and March 2028, the winner of which will meet Argentina in an intercontinental playoff. The Los Angeles Games will feature 16 women's football teams, up from 12 at the Paris Olympics.

Women's football debuted at the Olympics in 1996, and South Korea has yet to qualify. The Taegeuk Ladies have long struggled against North Korea, with a record of one win, five draws and 16 losses, and against China, with five wins, 10 draws and 29 losses, although this fall's Asian Games brought a 1-1 draw with the North in the group stage and a 1-0 win over China in the bronze medal match.

issues.title: Samsung Plans $34.5 Billion HBM Hub at Its Onyang Chip Campus
issues.gist: Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong said the Onyang campus will become a hub for advanced chip packaging, including HBM. The company will invest 46 trillion won, or $34.5 billion, there.
issues.gistKo: 삼성전자 이재용 회장이 온양 캠퍼스를 HBM을 포함한 첨단 반도체 패키징의 중심지로 키우겠다고 했어요. 회사는 이곳에 46조 원, 약 345억 달러를 투자해요.
issues.easyKo: 삼성전자가 충남 아산 온양에 AI 반도체용 메모리인 HBM을 만드는 큰 공장을 지어요. 완공은 2028년 6월이 목표이고, 직접 일자리도 약 700개 생겨요.

paragraphs.en: Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong spoke at a groundbreaking ceremony in Onyang on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Onyang is a city in South Chungcheong Province. He vowed to make the company's chip site there a key hub for advanced chip packaging, such as high-bandwidth memory, or HBM. The new facility is part of a government plan to make the central Chungcheong region a global hub for AI innovation.

pro.en: Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong on Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026, pledged at a groundbreaking ceremony in Onyang, a city in South Chungcheong Province, to transform the company's semiconductor operations there into a major hub for advanced chip packaging, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM). The new facility is part of a government initiative to develop the central Chungcheong region into a global center of artificial intelligence-driven innovation.

Samsung intends to invest a total of 46 trillion won ($34.5 billion) in the campus to build five HBM production lines, comprising 6 trillion won in construction costs and 40 trillion won for advanced equipment to be deployed in phases. The site, once devoted chiefly to the basic assembly and testing of conventional semiconductors, will become what Lee called a key hub for cutting-edge HBM, the heart of AI chips.

The new facility, the fifth production line at the site, will feature a three-story, 31,000-square-meter cleanroom dedicated to advanced HBM manufacturing, with operations planned to begin in June 2028. Once completed, the campus's total floor space will expand to 420,000 square meters from 270,000, and the project is expected to create about 700 direct jobs, a figure of interest to students eyeing careers in the chip industry.

views.view: Yonhap reports Lee's pledge to turn Onyang into a hub for cutting-edge HBM, and says the new plant is expected to create about 700 direct jobs.

heads.title: Samsung Electronics chief vows to turn Onyang campus into HBM hub

why: HBM is a key memory chip for AI, so this site could shape Korea's chip future.
The plan also ties into a government goal for regional growth.

lines.life: New chip plants can mean more jobs and training chances for Korean students who study engineering.
lines.next: Watch for the June 2028 start date and how the equipment is added in phases.

issues.title: German Chancellor Merz Visits the DMZ and Hopes Korea Can Reunify
issues.gist: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited the DMZ between North and South Korea and said he hopes Korea can reunify one day, as Germany did. North Korea has recently moved away from talks with the South.
issues.gistKo: 독일 총리 메르츠가 남북한 사이 비무장지대를 찾아 독일처럼 한국도 언젠가 통일하기를 바란다고 말했어요. 북한은 최근 남쪽과의 대화에서 멀어졌어요.
issues.easyKo: 독일 총리가 한국을 찾아 판문점에 갔어요. 독일이 통일된 경험을 떠올리며 한국도 통일할 기회가 오기를 바란다고 했어요. 하지만 북한은 통일 이야기를 헌법에서 지운 상태예요.

paragraphs.en: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited the border between North and South Korea on a Friday in late October. He went to the truce village of Panmunjom, inside the demilitarized zone, which is often called the DMZ. For a short time, he stood on the North Korean side inside a barracks building. The two Koreas have been divided since the fighting of the Korean War ended in 1953.
paragraphs.ko: 독일 총리 프리드리히 메르츠는 10월 말 금요일에 남북한 경계를 찾았어요. 그는 흔히 DMZ라고 부르는 비무장지대 안의 휴전 마을 판문점에 갔어요. 그는 잠시 막사 건물 안에서 북한 쪽에 서 있었어요. 남북한은 1953년 한국전쟁의 전투가 끝난 뒤 갈라져 있어요.

In Seoul, he spoke at a conference of German business and said that supply chains must not become political pawns. He said the European Union is ready to work with Asian economies on a trade order based on rules. South Korea's prime minister said that German companies use Korea as a central hub to expand in the Asia-Pacific region.

paragraphs.en: For Korean students, the visit shows how Korea matters to Europe, both for security and for trade. The same week, Germany's president Frank-Walter Steinmeier was in Beijing to ease trade tensions with China. DW says the two visits show Berlin's effort to lower risks without cutting ties with China.
paragraphs.ko: 한국 학생들에게 이 방문은 안보와 무역 양쪽에서 한국이 유럽에 중요하다는 것을 보여 줘요. 같은 주에 독일 대통령 프랑크발터 슈타인마이어는 중국과의 무역 긴장을 풀려고 베이징에 있었어요. DW는 두 방문이 중국과 관계를 끊지 않으면서 위험을 낮추려는 베를린의 노력을 보여 준다고 해요.

sents.en: The same week, Germany's president Frank-Walter Steinmeier was in Beijing to ease trade tensions with China.
sents.ko: 같은 주에 독일 대통령 프랑크발터 슈타인마이어는 중국과의 무역 긴장을 풀려고 베이징에 있었어요.

pro.en: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited the truce village of Panmunjom in the demilitarized zone that splits the two Koreas on a Friday in late October, and for a brief moment stepped onto the North Korean side within a barracks building; the peninsula has remained partitioned since the Korean War hostilities ended in 1953.

Invoking Germany's reunification 36 years ago, Merz told journalists that the setting illustrated the toll that division takes on a country and the depth of the yearning for reunification, and he noted that he had been questioned about the German experience while in Seoul. "Let us hope that Korea too gets the chance one day to regain state unity," he said.

The remark came at an awkward moment, since Pyongyang has pulled back from diplomacy with the South in recent years, striking reunification wording from its constitution and redefining the South as a hostile state, DW reported.

South Korea was the final leg of Merz's five-day Asia tour, which followed stops in Singapore and Japan; addressing German business leaders in Seoul, he argued that supply chains cannot become political pawns and said the EU stood ready to cooperate with Asian economies on a rules-based economic order, while South Korea's prime minister said German firms use Korea as a central hub for expansion across the Asia-Pacific.

For Seoul's younger generation, the trip signals Korea's weight in European calculations on both security and trade; the same week, President Frank-Walter Steinmeier was in Beijing seeking to smooth trade disputes, and DW characterized the dual visits as Berlin's attempt to reduce risk without decoupling from China.

views.view: Merz drew on Germany's reunification and hoped Korea gets the chance, while North Korea has dropped reunification from its constitution.

heads.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ

why: A leader of Europe's biggest economy linked Germany's reunification to Korea's divided border.
lines.agree: The Korean Peninsula has been divided since 1953, and the border is still sensitive.
lines.split: Merz hopes for reunification, but North Korea has dropped that goal and calls the South a hostile state.
lines.life: Korean students can see how Korea matters to Europe in trade and security, not only in culture.
lines.next: Watch whether Germany and the EU deepen trade ties with Korea and other Asian partners.

issues.title: Koreans Eye Day Trips to Japan for Cheaper Mounjaro After New Customs Rule
issues.gist: A new rule lets travelers bring home medicine they bought abroad for their own use. Some Koreans now talk about day trips to Japan to buy cheaper Mounjaro, while lawmakers ask how repeat trips will be checked.
issues.gistKo: 해외에서 산 개인용 약을 가져올 수 있게 한 새 규정이 시행됐어요. 일부 한국인은 더 싼 마운자로를 사러 일본 당일치기를 생각하고, 국회에서는 반복 반입을 어떻게 확인할지 물었어요.

paragraphs.en: Many Koreans are now thinking about day trips to Japan to buy cheaper Mounjaro, a weight-loss drug. In online forums, users compare flights and share tips on where to get a prescription. They call Mounjaro bought in Japan "sushijaro" and the version from China "jjajangjaro."

paragraphs.en: The talk began after new rules took effect. The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and the Korea Customs Service announced the change on a Wednesday and put it into effect the next day. They said travelers had made repeated complaints because properly prescribed medicines were held at customs. Now travelers may bring up to six containers of medicine for their own treatment if the drug is approved in the country where it was prescribed and bought. If the dosing instructions require more than six, up to a three-month supply is allowed.

paragraphs.en: Customs detected 5,030 unauthorized imports of weight-loss drugs such as Mounjaro and Wegovy in the first eight months of 2026. pro.en: Growing numbers of South Koreans are weighing day trips to Japan to obtain Mounjaro, the weight-loss injection, at lower cost, with online forum users comparing airfares and swapping tips on where to secure a prescription, and dubbing the drug "sushijaro" when sourced from Japan and "jjajangjaro" when sourced from China.

The chatter followed a rule change that the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and the Korea Customs Service announced on a Wednesday and enforced the following day, citing repeated complaints from travelers whose legitimately prescribed medicines had been held at customs; travelers may now carry up to six containers for personal treatment, provided the drug is approved in the country of prescription and purchase, or up to a three-month supply when dosing instructions call for more.

One forum user calculated that a day trip to Fukuoka, including airfare and a three-month supply of 5-mg Mounjaro, would run roughly 700,000 won ($520), against more than 1 million won for the same quantity in Korea even after a 10% local-currency discount; Wegovy reached the Korean market in October 2024 and Mounjaro in August 2025, and in the first half of 2026 medical facilities and pharmacies took delivery of about 11.4 million single-use Mounjaro pens worth 1.01 trillion won.

Customs authorities flagged 5,030 unapproved imports of weight-loss drugs such as Mounjaro and Wegovy in the first eight months of 2026, more than quadruple the 1,189 cases logged for all of 2025, and at a Friday session of the National Assembly's Health and Welfare Committee, People Power Party Rep. Lee Man-hee questioned how inspectors could determine whether medicines carried in on repeat trips were for personal use when no system tracks earlier imports, adding that a grace period might have limited the confusion, while Food and Drug Safety Minister Oh Yu-kyoung said the agencies had moved swiftly in response to public complaints.

For university students drawn by the lower price, the enforcement picture on repeat trips remains murky, and the outcome to watch is whether the two agencies settle on a common approach to repeat imports.

pro.en: A Korean father affixed a banner to the rear of his car announcing that his son, who had just completed military service, was on board, a play on the ubiquitous "Baby on board" sticker. The son had served 18 months of compulsory duty.

The father marked the discharge in this fashion, and a photo of the banner was posted on the online forum Bobaedream. The family drove more than 200 kilometers, from Inje in Gangwon Province to Cheongyang in South Chungcheong Province.

Along the route, fellow motorists offered thumbs-ups and finger hearts, and some honked or rolled down their windows to offer congratulations. In a post shared on Wednesday, the father thanked everyone for the warm reception and apologized in case the car had caused any inconvenience, acknowledging that some might regard the gesture as excessive.

The story went viral, with commenters calling the gesture creative and adorable and predicting that the son would later look back on it fondly. For many Korean families, the end of military service is a milestone worth celebrating.

issues.gist: Workers at Samsung Biologics are holding an online vote on joining the Federation of Korean Trade Unions while a partial strike continues. Talks with management are set to restart on Tuesday.
issues.gistKo: 삼성바이오로직스 노조가 부분 파업을 이어 가면서 한국노총 가입 여부를 온라인으로 투표해요. 회사와의 교섭은 화요일에 다시 시작될 예정이에요.

pro.en: Friction at Samsung Biologics is deepening as the company's union moves to join the Federation of Korean Trade Unions, the nation's second-biggest umbrella labor body, through an online ballot open from Friday to Tuesday. Union leaders say that the constraints of operating as a single-company union convinced them they required a larger organization behind them.

The ballot coincides with the second week of a renewed partial walkout. Roughly 500 members have been off the job since Nov. 6, and the stoppage is planned to run to Nov. 27, covering quality control testing, quality assurance, microbiology, logistics and manufacturing support. Management has maintained that output has so far been unaffected.

The stoppage is only partial because a court decision curtailed industrial action in core manufacturing operations, bringing the categories of work shielded by strike injunctions to nine; the union has therefore directed its effort at support and indirect production roles. The federation has publicly backed the workers and, last month, lodged a petition with the court contesting the company's bid to widen those curbs.

Each camp blames the other for the impasse. Management had sought to push back by two weeks the intensive bargaining sessions set for Nov. 3, pointing to trust concerns and to the union's insistence that some members of its negotiating team be swapped out, while the union charged that the company had unilaterally walked away from the table before it unveiled the second round of action. Both sides insist they are still willing to talk.

The union counts about 4,000 members, every one of whom may vote, and the proposal succeeds only if a majority of registered members turn out and a majority of those casting ballots approve. Some industry watchers doubt that a comparatively young membership will embrace a federation that has frequently been caught up in political quarrels. Negotiations are slated to resume on Tuesday.

views.view: The union wants a bigger labor group's backing, while the company says production has not been hurt and both sides say they are open to talks.

pro.en: The combined net profit of South Korea's five largest brokerages, Mirae Asset, Korea Investment & Securities, NH Investment & Securities, Kiwoom and Samsung Securities, came to 851.2 billion won ($640 million) in the July-September period, an 81.13 percent plunge from a record 4.51 trillion won in the previous quarter.

Mirae Asset Securities, the country's largest brokerage by equity capital, posted the steepest decline, swinging to a net loss of 405.6 billion won in the third quarter after earning 1.91 trillion won in the second. It was hit by massive valuation losses on proprietary investments, driven largely by a decline in the valuation of its stake in US aerospace company SpaceX and by the appreciation of the won against the dollar.

The remaining four brokerages stayed profitable but reported sharp quarter-on-quarter declines: Korea Investment & Securities earned 281.8 billion won, down 70.23 percent; Kiwoom 238.6 billion won, down 64.95 percent; Samsung Securities fell 27.7 percent; and NH Investment & Securities fell 21.62 percent. The common drag was a cooling market that prompted retail investors to pull back, with average daily trading value falling 36.24 percent to 75.3 trillion won from 118.1 trillion won.

Rising market interest rates also weighed on earnings. With the Fair Trade Commission set to impose a total of 1.62 trillion won in fines on 10 brokerage houses and five banks for colluding in government bond auctions for more than three years, the penalties are expected to add to the industry's financial burden.

Cumulative earnings remain strong, as massive first-half profits have kept brokerages at record-high levels for the January-September period. Korea Investment & Securities reported a nine-month net profit of 2.01 trillion won, up 20.1 percent, while Mirae Asset posted a record 2.50 trillion won, up 148.2 percent year-on-year, despite its third-quarter loss. For student investors, the episode shows how quickly market activity can shift.

talk.q: Why do music show wins matter to fans?

talk.answer: A win is a clear sign that a song is popular. TWS won with 9,857 points on Music Bank. I think it also gives fans a chance to celebrate together.
talk.answerKo: 1위는 노래가 인기 있다는 분명한 신호예요. TWS는 뮤직뱅크에서 9,857점으로 이겼어요. 팬들이 함께 축하할 기회도 된다고 생각해요.

paragraphs.en: The K-pop group TWS won its first music show trophy for the song "Call My Name." It happened on the November 13 episode of the KBS show "Music Bank." The two candidates for first place were TWS's "Call My Name" and RESCENE's "With." TWS took the prize with a total of 9,857 points.

sents.en: It happened on the November 13 episode of the KBS show "Music Bank."
sents.ko: 11월 13일 KBS 「뮤직뱅크」 방송에서였어요.

sents.en: The two candidates for first place were TWS's "Call My Name" and RESCENE's "With."
sents.ko: 1위 후보는 TWS의 「Call My Name」과 RESCENE의 「With」였어요.

sents.en: TWS took the prize with a total of 9,857 points.
sents.ko: TWS가 합계 9,857점으로 1위를 차지했어요.

paragraphs.en: The song is the title track of the group's second single album, "TO US." The album came out on November 2 and sold 634,871 copies on its first day. pro.en: K-pop group TWS captured its first music show trophy for "Call My Name" on the Nov. 13 episode of KBS's "Music Bank," edging out RESCENE's "With" with a total of 9,857 points.

The song is the title track of the group's second single album, "TO US," which was released on Nov. 2 and sold 634,871 copies on its first day. According to Hanteo Chart, the album moved 825,360 copies in its first week, topping the weekly album chart, while the music video surpassed 10 million views in roughly three days.

TWS launched its comeback promotions on "Music Bank" on Nov. 6. The Nov. 13 lineup also featured BLACKPINK's Jisoo, ATEEZ, ILLIT and NCT DREAM. For fans, a music show win is a visible barometer of a song's standing in Korea, and the group's next results will show whether the momentum holds.

issues.title: Short Form Dramas Bet on Star Casting to Win Viewers

pro.en: Korea's short form dramas are turning into a fresh casting ground, with television actors sharing the screen with singers, rappers and other entertainers. As the format wins recognition, the roster of performers is growing more varied than before.

One example is the short series Gwang-an: The Crown Prince's Woman, a palace romance about an assassin named Eun-woo who poses as a palace maid and slips into the Western Palace to kill Crown Prince Lee Hyun, yet ends up falling for him and resisting her fate. Its cast features singer Chuu, rapper Swings and actors Seongjun and Kim Eung-soo.

The genre is built on condensed storytelling. Such series usually roll out a long run of episodes lasting only one to two minutes, designed for mobile phones, and rely on fast plotting, twists and cliffhangers that keep audiences hungry for the next episode.

The format also pays off for both sides. Shorter production periods and more compact filming schedules allow performers to try new genres while working on other projects, and production companies can stir early interest by casting familiar faces. Swings stepping away from his rapper image to attempt a historical drama, for instance, adds publicity.

Still, the Korea Times cautions that star casting alone cannot guarantee success: famous names may draw viewers at first, but the story and the acting bring them back. It adds that competition in the content industry is shifting as mobile video opens a new market for production and distribution.

views.view: Star casting can bring early attention to short form dramas, but only a strong story and good acting can keep viewers.

issues.title: Colonial-Era Spy Drama "100 Days of Deception" Climbs to Double-Digit Ratings
issues.gist: The Korean drama "100 Days of Deception" has doubled its ratings since its premiere. It tells a spy story set in 1932 Seoul and plays with familiar tropes.
issues.gistKo: 한국 드라마 '백일의 기만'은 첫 방송 이후 시청률이 두 배로 올랐어요. 1932년 서울을 배경으로 한 첩보 이야기이고 익숙한 공식을 비틀어요.
issues.easyKo: 일제 강점기를 배경으로 한 첩보 드라마가 인기를 끌고 있어요. 시청률은 첫 방송의 5.3%에서 10.7%까지 올랐어요. 애국심보다 살아남으려는 인물의 선택을 그려서 좋은 평을 받아요.

paragraphs.en: The tvN weekend drama "100 Days of Deception" is climbing fast in the ratings. Episode 10 aired on Sunday and reached an average nationwide rating of 10.7 percent, according to Nielsen Korea. That is more than double the 5.3 percent of the premiere, and the show has risen steadily since Episode 8. The Korea Times says the series is praised for twisting familiar spy and independence-movement tropes.

pro.en: Ratings for tvN's weekend series "100 Days of Deception" have climbed steadily since its eighth installment, and Sunday's tenth episode drew a nationwide average of 10.7 percent, according to Nielsen Korea, more than twice the 5.3 percent of its premiere. The Korea Times credited the show with upending the well-worn conventions of colonial-era espionage and independence-movement dramas.

Set in 1932 Seoul, the drama centers on Ga-kyung, played by Kim You-jung, a onetime pickpocket who acquired her English as a maid in an American missionary's household and who dreams only of earning enough for passage to the United States. Seeking that passage, she throws in with the independence group Gukgudan and penetrates the Japanese Government-General as a trainee interpreter, serving as a secret operative.

Tae-woong, played by Park Jin-young, is a Korean brought up as the adopted son of a Japanese vice governor-general. Outwardly a haughty member of the ruling elite who craves his father's approval, he is privately tormented by his Korean identity. Interpretation serves as a core storytelling device, and Jin Seon-kyu reportedly spent two months in Kyoto learning his Japanese dialogue, while Ga-kyung speaks American English and Tae-woong British English to fit their backgrounds.

With six of its 16 episodes still to air, the series is moving toward its climax, and the production team has hinted at a romance between the two leads and at answers about who will live and who will die. For English learners, the deliberate use of different accents gives a rare opportunity to hear English shaped by who the characters are.

views.view: The drama is praised for turning familiar spy and independence-movement tropes into a story about people's choices and changes.

pro.en: Seoul Metro Line 9 Corporation told riders on Friday to review the updated timetables ahead of time, as schedules on the notoriously overcrowded Line 9 are revised starting Monday.

In the morning peak between 5:40 and 7 a.m., services bound for VHS Medical Center will move to a pattern of two express trains for each all-stop train, in place of the present one-for-one alternation. Intervals will be trimmed by as much as 20 seconds, so all-stop frequency holds at about today's level.

For the evening peak, the concentrated-service window shifts 30 minutes earlier, to 4-6:30 p.m. from 4:30-7 p.m. The city unveiled the overhaul in October, aiming to ease crowding by reworking how existing trains are operated rather than buying additional rolling stock.

Riders should check which trains serve their stations, since the order of express and all-stop trains is changing. The real test will be whether the revised timetable measurably eases congestion on one of the capital's most crowded transit corridors.

pro.en: The National Palace Museum of Korea opened a special exhibition on Friday devoted to Sunjong, the last emperor of the Korean Empire, to commemorate the centennial of his death. On view are two portraits of the monarch, one dating from his years as crown prince and the other from after his accession to the throne.
The crown-prince portrait is thought to date from 1902, when it was produced together with one of his father, Emperor Gojong, to mark the 40th anniversary of Gojong's reign.
The portrait of Emperor Sunjong was completed in 1928, two years after his death, by the royal artist Kim Eun-ho, who worked from photographs of the late emperor.

Fires after the outbreak of the Korean War damaged both works, yet authorities were able to authenticate their provenance by examining Sunjong's attire and accessories, the patterns of the mats and the furniture depicted in the paintings, a reminder of how small details help specialists establish where a work came from.

views.view: The show gives visitors a chance to see two portraits of the last emperor and learn how they were identified.

why: The show helps people remember the last emperor of the Korean Empire 100 years after his death.

lines.life: History students can see how experts use details in paintings to prove where they came from.

issues.title: South Korea Breaks Ground on First 'Supergap' Chip and AI Megaproject in Chungcheong
issues.gist: South Korea held a groundbreaking ceremony for the Chungcheong project, the first of three big AI and chip projects. Samsung plans to invest 144 trillion won in the region.
issues.gistKo: 한국이 AI와 반도체 대형 사업 세 가지 중 첫 번째인 충청권 사업의 착공식을 열었어요. 삼성은 이 지역에 144조 원을 투자할 계획이에요.
issues.easyKo: 정부와 기업이 함께 AI와 반도체 분야에서 앞서가려는 큰 사업이 첫 삽을 떴어요. 삼성전자 아산 온양캠퍼스가 AI용 메모리인 HBM의 중심지로 바뀔 예정이에요.

views.view: The report presents the project as a national push where the president and Samsung's chairman both promise a big leap forward.

heads.title: S. Korea Launches Chungcheong Megaproject in Quest for Technical Lead in AI Sector

why: The project shows how Korea uses public and private money together to compete in AI and chips.

talk.q: Why do governments invest so much money in chips and AI?

talk.answer: Chips and AI are important for jobs, exports and national security. Korea already makes many memory chips, so it wants to keep its lead. I think investment is useful, but the plan should also train enough young engineers.
talk.answerKo: 반도체와 AI는 일자리, 수출, 안보에 중요해요. 한국은 이미 메모리 반도체를 많이 만들어서 우위를 지키고 싶어 해요. 투자는 유용하지만 젊은 엔지니어를 충분히 키우는 계획도 함께 있어야 한다고 생각해요.

paragraphs.en: South Korea has started building the first of three giant projects that aim to make the country a leader in AI and chips. A groundbreaking ceremony for the Chungcheong regional project was held on Thursday in Asan, South Chungcheong Province. The site is the future home of an advanced chip packaging plant owned by Samsung Electronics.

paragraphs.en: The government calls the plan the "supergap" project, meaning a technology lead so wide that no other country can catch up. Together, the three projects are set to pour about 1.6 quadrillion won, roughly 1.2 trillion US dollars, into chips, AI data centers and physical AI. The money will come from both public and private sources.

pro.en: Seoul on Thursday launched the first of three flagship regional undertakings designed to secure what officials describe as an unassailable position in artificial intelligence and semiconductors, staging a groundbreaking ceremony for the Chungcheong initiative in Asan, South Chungcheong Province, where Samsung Electronics is to build an advanced chip packaging facility.

President Lee Jae Myung and Samsung Electronics Chairman Lee Jae-yong were present at the company's Onyang Campus, where the president said the Chungcheong package also covers state-of-the-art display lines in Asan and plants in Sejong City that turn out high-performance substrates for AI servers; construction is already furthest along among the regional schemes unveiled in July.

Marketed under the "supergap" label, the campaign is a public-private investment drive intended to open a technological chasm that competitors cannot close; the three megaprojects are to funnel almost 1.6 quadrillion won, close to $1.2 trillion, into semiconductors, AI data centers and physical AI, drawing on both state and private funding.

Samsung Group, for its part, has pledged 144 trillion won for the Chungcheong region and intends to turn a site long dedicated to routine assembly and testing of standard chips into a high-bandwidth memory hub, with a fifth production line slated to start mass-producing next-generation HBM chips in June 2028.

issues.title: Crypto Market Loses $130 Billion After Nvidia CEO's Exit
issues.gist: The crypto market lost more than $130 billion in one day. Bitcoin and Ethereum fell to their lowest levels since August after worries about AI stocks and U.S. rates.
issues.gistKo: 가상자산 시장이 하루 만에 1300억 달러 넘게 줄었어요. AI 주식과 미국 금리에 대한 걱정으로 비트코인과 이더리움이 8월 이후 가장 낮아졌어요.

paragraphs.en: The global crypto market lost more than $130 billion in one day, BusinessKorea reported on Friday. At 4 p.m. on Nov. 13, CoinMarketCap showed a total market value of $2.32 trillion, down 5.41% from 24 hours earlier. Bitcoin traded at $69,119, down 5.98%, and Ethereum was at $1,942.55, down 5.00%. Both coins fell to their lowest levels since August.

pro.en: The global virtual asset market shed more than $130 billion in a single day, BusinessKorea reported. As of 4 p.m. on Nov. 13, CoinMarketCap put total capitalization at $2.32 trillion, a 5.41% decline from 24 hours earlier, with Bitcoin at $69,119, down 5.98%, and Ethereum at $1,942.55, down 5.00%, both sinking to their lowest levels since August.

The article tied the slide to unease over U.S. AI-related equities after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's resignation, which sent the chipmaker's stock down 4.3% in the U.S. market on Nov. 12. Bloomberg attributed the pressure to heightened expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes and concern about tighter regulation next year with the Democratic Party controlling Congress.

Forced liquidations compounded the selling. After Bitcoin slipped below $70,000, more than $1 billion in leveraged long positions was wiped out, according to an AQC Tech derivatives trader, deepening the decline. A GSR executive said swings in AI shares, a strong dollar and the leadership change at Nvidia had weighed on risk assets.

Listed Bitcoin holders also felt the strain. Japan's Metaplanet disclosed a net loss of 27.157 billion yen, about $172.54 million, for January through September, reflecting unrealized valuation losses on its coins, after selling 10,000 Bitcoins in the third quarter and repurchasing 11,000 to end September with 44,000. The next question is whether the Nvidia management shake-up and U.S. rate signals continue to weigh on crypto prices.

paragraphs.ko: 국민연금은 많은 한국인의 노후 자금을 운용하기 때문에 이 소식이 중요해요. 이 선택은 한국의 큰 투자자가 AI 열풍을 어떻게 보는지 보여 줘요. 빅테크는 여전히 믿지만 반도체 가격에는 조심스러워요. 다음으로 볼 것은 다음 분기에 반도체 주식이 회복하는지예요.

pro.en: South Korea's National Pension Service (NPS) continued to see the value of its U.S. equity portfolio rise in the third quarter, according to a filing submitted to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Nov. 12, local time. The fund reported holding 553 U.S.-listed stocks as of the end of September, worth $158.74 billion, an increase of $3.66 billion from the end of the previous quarter.

The Magnificent 7 megacap technology names drove the gains: the fund's combined stake in Nvidia, Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Tesla rose $5.5 billion, or 12.6%, to $49.1 billion. Microsoft posted the largest increase, surging $2.17 billion, or 38.2%, to $7.86 billion, followed by Nvidia, Apple and Meta.

Semiconductor holdings, by contrast, delivered a disappointing return after a third-quarter correction fueled by worries about excessive AI spending. Micron's valuation slipped 7.4%, while Applied Materials dropped 29.1%, Lam Research 24.1%, Broadcom 6.6% and Intel 13.3%. The fund nonetheless added 0.1% to 0.9% to its share counts in major U.S. chipmakers, in what the report described as bargain hunting.

The pension fund also expanded its exposure to space-related companies such as SpaceX and Rocket Lab and to defense contractors including Boeing and Lockheed Martin. It trimmed its positions in Bitcoin-linked companies such as Strategy, and its Roblox share count fell by about 7.4%.

Because the NPS oversees the retirement savings of millions of Koreans, its portfolio moves offer a window into how a major institutional investor is weighing the AI boom: sustained confidence in big tech, tempered by caution on chip valuations. Whether semiconductor shares rebound next quarter is the key point to watch.

pro.en: Hanwha Aerospace is set to develop South Korea's first aviation engine in the 10,000-pound thrust class. The company announced on Nov. 13 that it had been selected as preferred bidder for a project overseen by the Agency for Defense Development, with a total budget of 177.3 billion won (about $130 million) and a schedule running through October 2031.

The powerplant is earmarked for stealthy reconnaissance drones built on homegrown technology. Designers are targeting a service life of thousands of hours and the highest turbine inlet temperature yet achieved in a Korean-developed engine, a combination that lifts thermal efficiency and output. A high-bypass layout will route a greater share of the incoming air around the combustion chamber, which improves propulsive efficiency and trims fuel burn.

Hanwha will shoulder the program from start to finish, covering detailed design, manufacture of key components, assembly, four completed engines and test campaigns. The effort leans on the core of the 5,500-pound turbofan now being developed, whose compressor, combustor and turbine set the engine's output and efficiency. During the bidding, Hanwha also put forward a plan to shed weight, which could stretch range and leave room for extra weapons and equipment.

Hanwha has designed, built, assembled and serviced aviation engines since 1979, an experience base of 47 years. Because military engines are a strategic technology, leading powers tightly police exports and technology transfers, and reliance on imported engines can hem in both aircraft development and sales abroad. The project is therefore viewed as pivotal to the export competitiveness of Korea's defense industry.

The company intends to apply the heat-resistance, longevity and lightweighting technologies gained here to advanced engines for next-generation fighters such as the KF-21 Block 3, proceeding in phases toward higher thrust.

issues.gist: Union leaders of subcontract workers at Hanwha Ocean will start a hunger strike on Nov. 16. They want wages and jobs on the bargaining list, but the company says it will talk only about safety.
issues.gistKo: 한화오션 하청 노동자 노조 간부들이 11월 16일부터 단식에 들어가요. 임금과 고용을 교섭 안건에 넣으라는 것인데, 회사는 안전 문제만 논의할 수 있다고 해요.

paragraphs.en: Subcontract workers at Hanwha Ocean will begin a hunger strike on Nov. 16. They want the company to put wages, jobs and other basic livelihood issues on the bargaining list. Three union leaders will take part: Kang In-seok, Kang Bong-jae and Lee Hyeong-ju. Kang In-seok is already staging a sit-in on the roof of a painting factory in Geoje, and he will continue the hunger strike there. The other two will join from a tent inside the company.

paragraphs.en: The dispute began at the end of September. On Sept. 30, six union members climbed onto a roof and a crane inside the shipyard to demand talks with the main contractor. They say a revised labor law, which took effect on March 10, gives them the right to bargain with Hanwha Ocean. Six rounds of talks that began on Oct. 8 ended without results. The union says Hanwha Ocean has said talks are possible only on six safety-related items. The union argues that talks without wages and jobs would be meaningless.

pro.en: Hanwha Ocean's subcontracted workers will start a hunger strike on Nov. 16 to push for wages, employment and other core livelihood issues to be put on the bargaining table. Three union officials, Kang In-seok, Kang Bong-jae and Lee Hyeong-ju, will take part, with Kang In-seok continuing the fast from the roof of a painting factory in Geoje, where he is staging a sit-in, and the other two joining from a tent inside the company.

The standoff dates to Sept. 30, when six members of the shipbuilding subcontractors branch scaled a factory roof and a crane inside the yard to press for talks with the principal contractor. The workers say a revised labor union law that took effect on March 10 entitles them to bargain with Hanwha Ocean, but six rounds of negotiations that began Oct. 8 ended without results. According to the union, the company has maintained that talks are possible only on six safety-related items, and it contends that bargaining that skips wages and employment would be meaningless.

Management and the company's own staff take a different view. A Hanwha Ocean official described the sit-in as a clear and unjustified illegal act and said the company would respond in accordance with the law. On Nov. 5, a council of about 430 team leaders and foremen rallied at the yard, arguing that the protest disrupts production and hands an advantage to shipyards in China and Japan, and noting that the company had withdrawn a 47 billion won damages suit and paid subcontract workers the same performance bonus.

A separate legal dispute concerns the Welliv branch, a union of workers handling catering and facility management at subcontractors. Labor commissions concluded that Hanwha Ocean qualifies as the branch's employer, but the company has contested the ruling and the matter now sits before the Seoul Administrative Court. For the Welliv branch, preserving employment is the most pressing issue because its contract comes up for renewal in April next year.

The dispute turns on a broader question in Korean industry, where many workers are employed by subcontractors rather than the main company: who should sit across the table when their pay and jobs are decided. Labor and management are scheduled to hold a seventh round of talks on Nov. 19, and the two union branches intend to start behind-the-scenes preparation for a joint strike.

views.view: Union leaders say talks limited to safety items would make negotiations with the main contractor meaningless, so they chose a last-resort hunger strike.
A supervisors' council says the protest disrupts production and hands an advantage to rival shipyards in China and Japan.

pro.en: At the seventh CIO Roundtable hosted by The Korea Economic Daily on Nov. 12, panelists weighed US equity valuations, AI-linked credit risk and private markets. Owen Lamont of Acadian Asset Management asserted that American stocks are probably in a bubble today, with features reminiscent of the dot-com mania of 1999 and 2000, while cautioning that elevated valuations could persist for years.

Lamont cited four red flags: stretched valuations, accelerating share issuance, heavy retail inflows, and investors continuing to buy while believing the market is overpriced. He noted that the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings ratio stood at 40.7 in October, near the all-time high of 44.2 set in December 1999.

He added that Anthropic is preparing a major IPO next week, following SpaceX's record debut in June, and he anticipates hundreds of smaller listings to follow, which he regards as further evidence of surging equity issuance.

Theodore Koenig of Monroe Capital characterized AI-related private credit risk as concentrated in particular sectors rather than systemic, yet flagged five- to ten-year loans financing GPUs that could become obsolete within two or three years. Ted Goldthorpe of BC Partners described AI as a durability test for borrowers, noting US private credit default rates of 2.4% at year-end.

Other panelists pointed to sluggish exits in private equity, with distributions slipping to 4% of net asset value in the first half. The two speakers located the risk in different places, with Lamont focused on equity prices and Koenig describing AI credit risk as concentrated in particular sectors.

views.view: US stocks show four bubble signs like 1999 to 2000, though prices could stay high for years.
AI credit risk is concentrated in some sectors, but long GPU loans and data center financing need care.
AI is a durability test for borrowers, and defaults could be higher once distressed loans are counted.

pro.en: A cyber attack on a company that backs a government-run startup program has exposed participants' personal information, the startups ministry disclosed on Friday. The artificial intelligence solutions company detected the intrusion on Wednesday.

According to the ministry, 20,028 people had their personal data compromised in the breach, 818 of them participants in the startup support program. Exposed details comprise the names, phone numbers and email addresses of service users.

The incident follows by only a few months a comparable hacking attack in June that leaked data on 5,000 participants in the same program, and the ministry had outlined security upgrades in July meant to head off any repeat.

Because the breach is a repeat, scrutiny is likely to fall on whether the strengthened safeguards are effective. For students weighing a startup, the episode underscores the need to be deliberate about the personal details they hand over to support services, and attention turns to what the ministry does to protect participants after the second leak.

views.view: The ministry said personal data of participants leaked just months after a similar attack in June, despite security measures announced in July.

pro.en: Korea Aerospace Industries Co. announced an expanded partnership with Indonesia's state-owned aircraft maker PT Dirgantara Indonesia (PTDI) after the two signed three memorandums of understanding covering the KF-21 fighter jet, flight simulators and commercial aircraft. The accords were concluded Wednesday in Jakarta, on the sidelines of the 12th South Korea-Indonesia Defense Industry Cooperation Committee meeting.
Under the KF-21 accord, the partners will study producing aircraft components on Indonesian soil, among them three kinds of structural parts, with PTDI taking a role in the manufacturing process.

Jakarta has long been a close defense-industry customer of KAI, buying KT-1 basic trainers and T-50 advanced trainer jets and joining the KF-21 program as an international partner. KAI has shipped 20 KT-1B trainers and 22 T-50i jets to the country, and it has also signed a deal to extend the service life of the KT-1Bs.

Building on these ties, KAI is aiming to make Indonesia the first overseas buyer of the KF-21, South Korea's homegrown supersonic fighter, a sale that would give Korean defense contractors a foothold abroad.

issues.title: Korean Vice Foreign Minister to Visit the U.S. for Economic Security Talks
issues.gist: Second Vice Foreign Minister Kim Jina will visit the United States for four days starting Sunday. She will talk with a senior U.S. official about supply chains, trade and investment.
issues.gistKo: 김진아 외교부 2차관이 일요일부터 나흘간 미국을 찾아요. 미국 고위 관리와 공급망, 무역, 투자 협력을 이야기할 예정이에요.
issues.easyKo: 한국 외교부 차관이 다음 주 미국에 가서 경제 안보 이야기를 나눠요. 조선과 에너지 분야 협력도 이야기하고, 미국 학계 인사도 만나요.

paragraphs.en: Korea's Second Vice Foreign Minister, Kim Jina, will go to the United States next week to talk about economic security cooperation, the foreign ministry said on Friday. She will make a four-day trip starting on Sunday.
paragraphs.ko: 김진아 외교부 2차관이 경제 안보 협력을 논의하러 다음 주 미국을 방문한다고 외교부가 금요일에 밝혔어요. 그녀는 일요일부터 나흘간 방문해요.

sents.en: Korea's Second Vice Foreign Minister, Kim Jina, will go to the United States next week to talk about economic security cooperation, the foreign ministry said on Friday.
sents.ko: 김진아 외교부 2차관이 경제 안보 협력을 논의하러 다음 주 미국을 방문한다고 외교부가 금요일에 밝혔어요.

sents.en: She will make a four-day trip starting on Sunday.
sents.ko: 그녀는 일요일부터 나흘간 방문해요.

paragraphs.en: Her first stop is a Monday meeting with Jacob Helberg, the U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs. They are expected to discuss how to strengthen supply chains and how to promote trade and investment that help both countries.
paragraphs.ko: 월요일에 김 차관은 야콥 헬버그 미국 국무부 경제 담당 차관을 만나요. 두 사람은 공급망을 강화하고 양국에 이로운 무역과 투자를 늘리는 방법을 논의할 예정이에요.

paragraphs.en: Then, on Wednesday, she will take part in the 10th Korea-U.S. public-private economic forum. There she will deliver a keynote speech about how to grow economic cooperation, with a focus on shipbuilding and energy.
paragraphs.ko: 수요일에는 제10회 한미 민관 경제 포럼에 참석해요. 거기서 특히 조선과 에너지 분야에서 경제 협력을 늘리는 방법에 대해 기조연설을 해요.

paragraphs.en: Kim also plans to meet academic figures to build support for Korea-U.S. relations. The ministry said this outreach comes as the makeup of the U.S. Congress changes after the midterm elections. paragraphs.ko: 김 차관은 한미 관계에 대한 지지를 넓히려고 학계 인사들도 만날 계획이에요. 외교부는 미국 중간선거 뒤 의회 구성이 바뀌는 때에 이런 접촉을 한다고 했어요. 한국 학생들에게 이번 방문은 공급망과 무역이 외교, 그리고 조선 같은 산업의 일자리와 이어져 있음을 보여 줘요.

sents.en: The ministry said this outreach comes as the makeup of the U.S. Congress changes after the midterm elections.

sents.en: For Korean students, the trip shows how supply chains and trade are linked to diplomacy and to jobs in industries like shipbuilding.

pro.en: Kim Jina, Seoul's Second Vice Foreign Minister, is set to travel to the United States next week for discussions on economic security and bilateral ties, the foreign ministry announced Friday. The trip runs four days from Sunday.

Her schedule opens Monday with talks involving Jacob Helberg, the U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs, on bolstering supply chains and on trade and investment that benefit both countries.

On Wednesday she is due at the 10th Korea-U.S. public-private economic forum, where she will deliver a keynote address on deepening bilateral economic cooperation, with an emphasis on the shipbuilding and energy sectors.

She also plans to meet academics as part of an effort at shoring up American support for Korea-U.S. relations, the ministry said, as the makeup of Congress shifts after the midterm elections. For Korean students, the trip illustrates how supply chains and trade are bound up with diplomacy and with employment in sectors such as shipbuilding.

views.view: The visit aims to strengthen economic security cooperation, supply chains, trade and investment, and to win support in the U.S. after the midterm elections.

talk.q: Why do countries talk about supply chains in diplomacy?

talk.answer: Supply chains connect companies and workers in different countries. If they break, prices and jobs can be hurt. I think talks like this help both sides plan ahead.

issues.title: Korea to Let Card Points Become Local Cash Vouchers From May
issues.gist: From May next year, South Korean credit card users can swap unused points for regional cash vouchers. The government wants to boost spending in local shops.
issues.gistKo: 내년 5월부터 신용카드 이용자는 안 쓴 포인트를 지역 상품권으로 바꿀 수 있어요. 정부는 동네 가게의 소비를 늘리려고 해요.
issues.easyKo: 카드 포인트를 쓰지 않고 두면 아깝죠. 내년 5월부터는 그 포인트를 지역화폐로 바꿔 동네 가게나 전통시장에서 쓸 수 있어요.

paragraphs.en: Credit card users in South Korea will be able to turn unused reward points into regional cash vouchers starting in May next year, officials said on Friday. The goal is to boost spending and bring new life to local economies.
paragraphs.ko: 한국의 신용카드 이용자들은 내년 5월부터 쓰지 않은 적립 포인트를 지역 상품권으로 바꿀 수 있다고 당국자들이 금요일 밝혔어요. 목표는 소비를 늘리고 지역 경제에 활력을 불어넣는 거예요.

The Office for Government Policy Coordination then worked with the interior ministry, the Financial Services Commission and a financial clearing institute to settle the details.

paragraphs.en: Credit card points will be the first to be allowed, and they add up to 2.1 trillion won, or about $1.57 billion. Once the service starts, users can check their points in an app, ask to convert as many as they want, and spend the local currency starting the next day.

pro.en: From May of next year, South Korean cardholders will be allowed to exchange idle reward points for regional cash vouchers, officials said Friday, in a move aimed at lifting consumption and giving local economies a lift.

The measure grew out of a late-June directive from President Lee Jae Myung to permit dormant points to be swapped for local currency. The Office for Government Policy Coordination has since drawn up the particulars together with the interior ministry, the Financial Services Commission and a financial clearing institute.

Credit card points will lead the way as the first eligible category, with outstanding balances amounting to 2.1 trillion won, or about $1.57 billion. After the service goes live, users will be able to look up their points in an app, request conversion of whatever amount they choose and spend the local currency the next day.

Officials plan to widen the program to cover KTX rail miles and other points, and Government Policy Coordination Minister Lim Ki-keun said talks would carry on so that more dormant points get used, households feel less financial strain and money reaches small business owners.

views.view: Yonhap reports the government hopes the change will ease household burdens and send money to small shops.

issues.title: Korea's Money Supply Rises Again in September
issues.gist: South Korea's M2 money supply rose 0.4 percent in September from a month earlier. Short-term deposits led the increase, the central bank said.
issues.gistKo: 9월 한국의 M2 통화량이 한 달 전보다 0.4퍼센트 늘었어요. 중앙은행은 단기 예금이 늘어난 영향이라고 밝혔어요.
issues.easyKo: 나라 안에 돌아다니는 돈의 양이 9월에도 조금 늘었어요. 가계와 금융기관이 가진 돈은 늘고, 기업이 가진 돈은 줄었어요.

paragraphs.en: South Korea's money supply kept rising in September from a month earlier, central bank data showed on Friday. M2, a key gauge of the money supply, averaged 4,283.9 trillion won, or about $3.2 trillion. That was up 0.4 percent, or 17.1 trillion won, from August. The data are preliminary, so the final numbers may change.
paragraphs.ko: 한국의 통화량은 9월에도 한 달 전보다 계속 늘었다고 중앙은행 자료가 금요일 보여 줬어요. 통화량의 핵심 지표인 M2는 평균 4283조 9000억 원, 약 3조 2000억 달러였어요. 이는 8월보다 0.4퍼센트, 17조 1000억 원 늘어난 수준이에요. 자료는 잠정치라서 최종 수치는 달라질 수 있어요.

pro.en: South Korea's money supply continued to expand in September from a month earlier, central bank data showed Friday, extending a steady upward trend that began last November. M2, a key gauge of the money supply, averaged 4,283.9 trillion won (about $3.2 trillion), up 0.4 percent, or 17.1 trillion won, from August, according to preliminary figures that remain subject to revision.
M2 comprises cash, demand deposits and other instruments that can readily be converted into cash, and it has climbed steadily since November last year.
The Bank of Korea attributed the increase to short-term deposits and money trusts with maturities of less than two years, both of which grew in September.

By sector, liquidity held by households and nonprofit organizations rose by 12.6 trillion won, and that held by financial institutions moved up by 5.2 trillion won, while liquidity held by nonfinancial corporations declined by 3.3 trillion won.

views.view: Yonhap reports that M2 rose in September mainly because short-term deposits and money trusts increased.

pro.en: Genesis BBQ Co., a South Korean fried chicken franchise operator, said Friday it had opened its first outlet in Africa as it broadens its global footprint.

The company said it signed a master franchise agreement with Good Tree South Africa, a local distributor of Korean food, in November last year to open the outlet. Under such an agreement, a franchisee may open outlets within a specified territory and sub-franchise them to third parties.

The new restaurant sits in Johannesburg, a major business and financial hub, and will serve the company's signature fried chicken alongside a range of Korean dishes. BBQ Chairman Yoon Hong-geun described the South Africa outlet as a strategic foothold and key market for expansion across the continent.

The company plans to open additional outlets in South Africa gradually next year and currently has none elsewhere in Africa. It operates more than 2,400 outlets in South Korea and about 800 overseas in 57 countries, and the move shows how Korean food brands seek growth abroad through local partnerships.

pro.en: Seoul opened a new inter-ministerial task force on Friday, with a mandate to design policies that bring down the cost of living and lift the real spending power of salaried workers. The presidential office had unveiled the initiative earlier in the week.

First Vice Finance Minister Kwon Dae-young presided over the inaugural session, at which officials from the relevant ministries went through detailed implementation plans. The body is divided into four working groups, which respectively handle existing support schemes, taxation, fiscal policy and finance, with the aim of identifying workable remedies.

Its priorities include assisting employees who must adapt to labor market upheaval stemming from structural change in industry, and easing the swelling expense of raising children and looking after aging parents. It also intends to help workers accumulate assets, hold on to their jobs more securely and look after their health.

Kwon argued that provisions of the 2026 tax revision bill and next year's budget proposal have a direct bearing on household finances for wage earners next year. He pledged that the government would honor National Assembly deliberations, consult closely with both the ruling and opposition camps, and move swiftly to put the measures into effect once they pass, so that workers actually feel the benefits.

pro.en: State-run Korea Electric Power Corp., or KEPCO, disclosed on Thursday that its third-quarter net profit had collapsed 78 percent year on year. Net profit for July through September slid to 835.89 billion won from 3.79 trillion won, operating profit dropped 70.9 percent to 1.64 trillion won from 5.65 trillion won, and sales fell 2.6 percent to 26.85 trillion won from 27.57 trillion won.

A company spokesperson attributed the slump to lower electricity sales and to global thermal coal prices that kept climbing through the quarter. Combined fuel costs at KEPCO's power-generating subsidiaries, including Korea South-East Power Co., topped 2.2 trillion won and weighed on earnings.

For the first nine months of the year, net profit declined 50.4 percent to 3.63 trillion won from 7.33 trillion won, while operating profit fell 43.2 percent to 6.56 trillion won and sales eased 0.8 percent to 73.17 trillion won. KEPCO has operated under an emergency management system since Russia's invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, when soaring fuel prices swelled its debt and interest payments.

The company said it would closely monitor volatile energy prices while maintaining the emergency system and improving its finances through cost reductions and profitability-driven operations. For students, electricity and fuel prices matter because they can feed into living costs, and attention now turns to whether fuel prices stay elevated and how KEPCO's finances evolve.

Saturday will also feel raw: morning lows of seven to 14 degrees Celsius, with Seoul at ten degrees, are paired with daytime highs of 12 to 17 degrees, three to six degrees below Friday's readings.
A cold snap is projected for the middle of next week, coinciding with the College Scholastic Ability Test, which means examinees will want to keep a close eye on the forecast.

pro.en: Kurt Gödel, the Austrian logician whose incompleteness theorems appeared in 1931, published sparingly thereafter yet bequeathed tens of thousands of pages of unpublished material.

Since 2017 the Finnish logician Jan von Plato of the University of Helsinki has directed an effort to decipher 16 workbooks from the early 1940s, totalling 1,009 densely written pages, much of it in Gabelsberger, an obsolete German shorthand that he says only six people can read; progress had been limited to roughly a page a week.

After he fed Claude his own transcriptions, six of his earlier books and other secondary literature, the model produced a 650-page exposition of the workbooks within a couple of days. It enumerated 663 theorems for which Gödel had a proof, a sketch or an idea of a proof, and when these were run through the Coq proof assistant, about 400 were verified as stated, about 200 required repair and about 50 proved false.

The most striking result concerns the axiom of choice: Paul Cohen won the 1966 Fields Medal for proving its independence from standard set theory, while Gödel claimed to have established the result in the 1940s. Claude located a nearly complete argument in the notebooks, marred by a single incorrect definition, and the repaired proof passed verification in Coq.

Joel David Hamkins of Notre Dame called the reconstruction remarkable if it holds up, but said historians must adjudicate how much derives from Claude and how much from Gödel; von Plato, meanwhile, intends to turn next to Gödel's notebooks on physics and cosmology.

views.view: Von Plato said he was flabbergasted and that AI can link ideas across a thousand pages, which humans find hard.
A logician said the reconstruction is remarkable if it holds up, but credit between Claude and Gödel is for historians to decide.

heads.title: ‘Ahead of his time’: AI helps unlock discoveries hidden in notebooks of man who transformed maths

why: AI is starting to help experts read hard old documents and find results people had missed.
lines.agree: Everyone agrees the notebooks hold important ideas and that every AI result must be checked carefully.
lines.split: Experts differ on how much credit belongs to Gödel and how much to Claude for the reconstructed proof.
lines.life: Students may soon use AI to read hard sources and find ideas, but they still need to check the results.
lines.next: Watch for outside experts to review the 663 theorems and for von Plato's work on Gödel's physics notebooks.

paragraphs.en: A new German film asks a hard question about the future: what if a care robot could also help an old person die? The film is "Mrs. Winkler Leaves the House" by director Doris Dörrie, and it is set in Hamburg in the near future. Robots deliver parcels, serve food in cafes, and even walk dogs.

pro.en: A new German film imagines a near-future Hamburg in which care robots can also help elderly patients end their lives. Doris Dörrie's "Frau Winkler verlässt das Haus" ("Mrs. Winkler Leaves the House") is set in a city where robots deliver parcels, wait tables and even walk dogs.

At its core is an elderly woman who can no longer live on her own after a fall. With her only daughter unable to provide permanent care, she is given a care robot with a built-in "End of Life" program that can assist with everyday tasks and, under certain conditions, provide assisted dying when the person explicitly wishes it and meets the medical criteria.

Dörrie told DW that the film probes what happens when artificial intelligence begins weighing the cost of caring for the elderly. It also asks what a free decision really is when a person may feel pressured not to burden loved ones, and it does so with plenty of dark humor; in the film's world, people cannot reverse the decision once made.

Dörrie says she has no interest in demonizing AI: the robot, which Mrs. Winkler names Pavlovich, helps her rediscover some zest for life and leave the house. Noting that an elderly person lives alone in every other German house, she asks why AI should not help in such circumstances. She and her crew were struck by how quickly people bond emotionally with robots.

The director argues that problems arise when people can no longer distance themselves from technology and stop forming their own thoughts, and she makes a clear call for AI regulation, comparing it to the international debate over nuclear weapons. For Korea, an aging society itself, the film offers a prompt to consider care, autonomy and technology together.

issues.title: Housefishing: AI-Enhanced Home Photos Worry UK Buyers
issues.gist: Estate agents in the UK are using AI to make homes look better online. Experts call it housefishing and warn it can mislead buyers.
issues.gistKo: 영국 부동산 중개인들이 온라인에서 집이 더 좋아 보이도록 AI를 써요. 전문가들은 이를 하우스피싱이라 부르며 구매자를 속일 수 있다고 경고해요.
issues.easyKo: AI로 집 사진을 고쳐서 실제보다 좋아 보이게 하는 일이 늘고 있어요. 어느 정도까지가 괜찮은지, 꼭 표시해야 하는지가 논란이에요.

paragraphs.en: Estate agents in the UK are using AI more and more to make homes look better online. The edits can be as small as fresh paint on a wall or as big as a lawn that is not really there. Agents say this helps buyers imagine what a place could become. But experts warn it can go too far and mislead buyers, a trend called housefishing.

All three companies told the BBC they had strict guidelines on AI and took the images down.

pro.en: Property agents throughout Britain are leaning ever more heavily on artificial intelligence to flatter their online listings, whether by freshening up paintwork or conjuring lawns that do not exist, and defend the practice as a way of helping buyers picture what a home might become. Specialists counter that it risks crossing into deception, and the trend has been labelled "housefishing".

Olivia Nicole, 29, who was hunting for a five-bedroom house in south-west London, discovered on arrival that a property advertised on Rightmove looked nothing like its photographs: rooms were much smaller, the decor was different and the windows were visibly reduced. The pictures, which had also been posted on Zoopla and Winkworth, had been touched up with AI without the listing saying so, and all three firms told the BBC that they operate strict AI rules and have pulled the images.

The Guild of Property Professionals, a trade group of independent agents that has published guidance on using AI responsibly, says it is difficult to gauge how widespread the practice is. In a survey of 906 UK homebuyers, one in five of those who bought in the previous year said they had seen listing photos digitally improved to flatter the property. Jack Bushrod, who reviews eccentric listings for his social media channel, has noticed a surge in such images over the last six months; he is relaxed about tidying a cluttered room or adding furniture but objects to deleting a pillar or inserting a window.

Cara, 38, who is selling her home in Lowestoft, was taken aback by an AI-edited photograph in which her son's room had been cleared of toys, although she continues to trust her agent, Howards, which says it now labels every AI-enhanced photo. Trading Standards said agents may carry out basic touch-ups so long as they declare the use of AI, but that reshaping a room, such as adding a window, or concealing features might mislead consumers and could be unlawful.
Bushrod believes every agent should be obliged to label AI-enhanced images prominently, and he predicts that housefishing will become more common as other agents follow suit.

views.view: The BBC said AI can help buyers imagine a home, but it can mislead them when it changes real features, and it should be labeled.
Trading Standards said basic AI edits are fine if disclosed, but structural changes could break the law.
Bushrod said most AI-enhanced images he has seen were not clearly labeled and wants labels on all of them.

why: AI photo editing is making it harder to trust what a home looks like online.

lines.life: When you search for a room or flat online, check the photos carefully and visit in person before you decide.
lines.next: Watch whether agents add clear AI labels and whether rules become stricter.

issues.title: Caine Prize Winner Cleared of Using AI After a Month-Long Investigation
issues.gist: The Caine Prize for African Writing says Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza's winning story was human-written. An AI-detection tool had said the story was almost fully AI-made.

views.view: The prize says the evidence is clear that the story is human-written, and the author says he is relieved the claims were dismissed.

heads.title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza cleared of using AI to write prize-winning story

why: The case shows that AI-detection tools can be wrong and can hurt writers' reputations.
lines.agree: Everyone agrees that claims of AI writing need careful and fair checks.
lines.split: People disagree on how much AI-detection software should be trusted, and some say African writers were unfairly singled out.
lines.life: Korean students who write essays may also face AI checks, so keeping drafts and notes can help show their own work.
lines.next: Watch for the prize ceremony before the end of the year and for more debate about AI detectors.

pro.en: The Caine Prize for African Writing has cleared Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza of using artificial intelligence to write his prize-winning short story, concluding after a month-long investigation that The Blue Fighter was human-written.

The story, which charts a family's declining fortunes after the father invests in fish tanks, was announced as the winner of the £10,000 prize on 6 October; five days later, The Atlantic published a piece by the author and journalist Vauhini Vara reporting that the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, had deemed the text almost completely artificially generated.

Prize chair Ellah Wakatama said the evidence was clear, explaining that the review drew on interviews with the author, the 2026 judging panel and The Shallow Tales Review, where the story was first published, as well as independent, expert-led metadata analysis of drafts written by the author.

Kundizeza, who had strongly denied using generative AI, said he was relieved the allegations had been dismissed, noting the Atlantic article had prompted online outrage from people who argued that Black and African writers were being unfairly singled out, and the prize said it looked forward to awarding him before the end of the year.

issues.title: US Public Workers Fight to Protect Their Jobs From AI
issues.gist: US public workers are pushing for rules on how governments use AI. Some unions have already won protections, like retraining instead of firing.
issues.gistKo: 미국 공공 부문 노동자들이 정부의 AI 사용에 규칙을 요구하고 있어요. 일부 노조는 해고 대신 재교육 같은 보호를 이미 얻어냈어요.
issues.easyKo: 정부가 AI를 쓰기 시작하자 공무원 노조가 일자리를 지키려고 협상에 나섰어요. 오클랜드에서는 파업 투표 뒤 AI 때문에 일이 없어진 직원을 재교육하기로 합의했어요.

glosses.meaning: AI만으로 징계·해고를 못 하게 한 캘리포니아 법안 이름

views.view: The report presents workers as gaining ground, with unions winning AI protections in Oakland, Pennsylvania, Ohio and California.

heads.title: US public workers are fighting to protect their jobs from AI – and some are winning

why: As governments use AI, workers are asking for a say in how it is used.
Some unions have already turned AI worries into written protections.
lines.agree: Unions and union experts say humans should stay in charge when AI is used at work.
lines.split: Unions say AI threatens jobs, while employers often say new tools improve efficiency and cut costs.
lines.life: Future jobs may include AI rules in contracts, so it helps to ask how AI will be used when you apply.
lines.next: Watch the 2027 contract talks in Pennsylvania and new state laws on AI at work.

talk.q: Should workers have a say when their employer starts using AI?
talk.qKo: 회사가 AI를 쓰기 시작할 때 노동자도 의견을 낼 수 있어야 할까요?
talk.answer: In Oakland, a strike vote helped workers win a deal that protects them from being fired because of AI. I think workers should be told about new tools early and be able to give input. At the same time, employers also need room to try useful technology.

paragraphs.en: Public workers in the United States are pushing back as governments start to use AI. In Oakland, California, city workers worried that AI could watch them too closely and judge their work unfairly. Their union voted on 22 October to allow a strike, and 94.1% said yes. The city then reached a tentative three-year deal that includes AI protections. It says the city must retrain or reassign workers displaced by AI instead of firing them, so the 5 November strike was put on hold.
paragraphs.ko: 미국의 공공 부문 노동자들은 정부가 AI를 쓰기 시작하자 맞서고 있어요. 캘리포니아주 오클랜드의 시청 직원들은 AI가 자신들을 지나치게 감시하고 일을 부당하게 평가할까 걱정했어요. 노조는 10월 22일 파업 권한을 주기로 투표했고, 94.1%가 찬성했어요. 이후 시는 AI 보호 조항이 들어간 3년짜리 잠정 합의에 이르렀어요. 합의에는 AI 때문에 일자리를 잃는 직원을 해고하지 않고 재교육하거나 다른 자리로 옮겨야 한다는 내용이 있어서, 11월 5일 파업은 보류됐어요.
